jobinrwanda.title: Associate Attorney
jobinrwanda.description:
About Job Vacancy:

Job title: Associate Attorney

Location: Kigali,Rwanda

Position type: Full time (with an initial probation)

Job Description:

The candidate will serve as a generalist in the office with responsibilities including, among other things, routine and complex contract drafting, review and negotiation, litigation support and management, legal research support, dispute resolution, handling filings with regulatory authorities and legal advice on regulatory procedures and practices.

The candidate will work closely with a supervising partner, who shall assign the day-to-day duties which will involve a wide range of matters reflecting the complex and diverse commercial mattersincluding but not limited to the following:

  • Analyze and help prepare and negotiate contracts, corporate organizational documents, legal opinions and other documents needed to carry out the firm’s objectives.
  • Under the direction of a supervising partner, advise clients on legal issues, as requested.
  • Under the direction of a supervising partner, research and provide information concerning legal and policy issues of concern to the firm in areas such as contracts, regulatory issues, civil procedure, and other matters.
  • Assist with conducting due diligence; work with a supervising partner on corresponding investigations as needed.
  • Assist the designated partner with pursuing alternative dispute resolution, pursuing and defending litigation, and settling outstanding matters. Assist in preparing briefs, complaints, answers and replies, and make appearances and motions as needed. Present evidence at administrative hearings in cases of moderately complex issues, under the direction of a supervising partner.

Qualifications and Education Requirements:

  • Bachelor’s degree in law recognized in Rwanda, or equivalent (a master’s degree in commercial/business law would be an added advantage).
  • Diploma in legal practice recognized in Rwanda, or equivalent.
  • A minimum of 3 years post-qualification experience doing legal work either in Rwanda or abroad.
  • Must be a Rwandan national.
  • Must be a member of the Rwanda Bar Association.

Required Skills:

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English, and good command of verbal and written Kinyarwanda and French would be an added advantage.
  • Demonstrable versatility in the use of information and communication technology (MS office applications and tech-savvy).

Preferred Skills:

  • Excellent conceptual, analytical, documentation, and presentation skills.
  • Excellent planning and prioritization skills.
  • Ability to think strategically and propose solutions.
  • Strong analytical/problem-solving skills.
  • Multi-tasking skills.
  • Must be a self-motivated person able to work with minimal supervision.

How to Apply:

All interested candidates are invited to submit their application enclosed with a cover letter, curriculum vitae, academic and professional qualifications and other relevant work certificates not later than 30th September 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application.

jobinrwanda.title: Senior Maintenance Technician
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION: Senior Maintenance Technician

Job Title: Senior Maintenance Technician

Company: LFL Rwanda Ltd

Reports to: Maintenance Supervisor

Location: Rwanda

Employment Type: Full-time

Job Purpose

The Senior Maintenance Technician will be responsible to performs preventive and corrective maintenance, supports fault diagnosis and equipment improvement, and assists the Maintenance Supervisor in planning and coordinating daily maintenance activities.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

  • Implement the preventive maintenance schedule approved by the Maintenance Supervisor. 
  • Respond promptly to electrical, mechanical, pneumatic, hydraulic, and electromechanical breakdowns. 
  • Diagnose faults and safely restore equipment within the shortest practical time. 
  • Investigate recurring equipment failures and recommend permanent corrective actions. 
  • Maintain hammer mills, mixers, conveyors, elevators, screw feeders, bagging machines, compressors, pumps, motors, gearboxes, and associated equipment. 
  • Enforce lockout/tagout, permit-to-work, hot-work, work-at-height, and confined-space procedures where applicable. 
  • Monitor critical spare-parts levels and report replenishment requirements to the Maintenance Supervisor. 
  • Complete inspection sheets, maintenance checklists, and breakdown reports accurately and on time. 

Qualification and Profile

  • Diploma or Advanced Diploma in Electromechanical Engineering, 
  • Minimum of 2 years’ experience
  • Interpersonal skills with a ‘Can Do’ attitude
  • Good knowledge of preventive and corrective maintenance and fault diagnosis
  • Strong problem-solving, teamwork and communication skills

Reporting to the Maintenance Supervisor, the Senior Maintenance Technician will be responsible to performs preventive and corrective maintenance, supports fault diagnosis and equipment improvement, and assists the Maintenance Supervisor in planning and coordinating daily maintenance activities

How to Apply

Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 16th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application

jobinrwanda.title: Project Manager
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB ADVERTISEMENT: 

CARE International is seeking to recruit a “Project Manager”. 

Introduction

CARE is a leading humanitarian organization fighting global poverty. We seek a world of hope, tolerance and social justice, where poverty has been overcome and people live in dignity and security. CARE International aims to be a global force and a partner of choice within a worldwide movement dedicated to ending poverty.

Are you passionate about building inclusive and resilient communities?

Are you an experienced project management professional with a strong commitment to social cohesion, gender equality, youth empowerment, and inclusive economic opportunities?

Do you thrive on bringing diverse partners together, turning strategies into results, and ensuring that development initiatives deliver meaningful and sustainable change?

If so, CARE Rwanda is seeking an experienced and passionate Project Manager to lead the implementation of the Borderland Project, an initiative focused on strengthening resilience, and inclusive economic opportunities in cross-border communities.

Through this project, you will work alongside diverse partners and stakeholders to support women, youth, displaced people, host communities, and groups experiencing multiple vulnerabilities, helping create communities that are more economically resilient.

About the Role

The Project Manager (PM) contributes to the realization of the Country Office (CO) Program Strategy by managing the implementation of the CO project, namely Borderland, ensuring that plans are aligned with the Country Office strategy and delivered on time and to the project management standards and donor requirements. 

The PM serves as the main contact person and liaises with project consortium members and leadership, the CO team including Program director, CARE MEAL Team, and the Program Support and Finance teams to ensure timely and quality support to projects, e.g. through various CO coordination mechanisms like participation in multi-disciplinary project management teams, program coordination meetings. The position holder works together with the Director of Growth and Knowledge Management department to ensure that learning from projects is used to keep projects on track and continually improve, and develop new strategies, tools and approaches, and do the necessary adaptations. In addition, the PM’s responsible for overseeing the deployment of CARE’s resources in projects and implementing risk management and accountability strategies according to CARE International, Government of Rwanda, and Donor policies. The project manager directly reports to the Program Director.

Who We Are Looking For:

Educational Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in a related field (e.g. Project management, Economics, Development studies or Social Science)
  • Master’s degree in project management or Qualified Project Management certification (added advantage)

Experience:

  •  6-10 years in project management role in the development sector; prior experience in related areas/sector programming preferred.
  • At least three years' experience managing multi-donor-funded projects and projects with foundations and/or institutional donors.
  • Demonstrated experience in program design, implementation and evaluation, including participatory approaches
  • Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with implementing partners, donors and government counterparts.

Technical competencies:

  • Demonstrated leadership and management skills in a complex international setting
  • Demonstrated ability in managing different types of partnerships
  • Strong human resource management skills including capacity building, coaching and conflict management; 
  •  Ability to establish a learning culture and to facilitate knowledge sharing 
  • Ensuring donor compliance and reporting
  • Experience in women and girls-centered programming approach will be an advantage
  • Very high-quality written work and language skills in English; ability to speak in French & Kinyarwanda

How to apply

If you are a dynamic development professional who combines strong project leadership and coordination skills with a genuine commitment to social cohesion, gender equality, and inclusive economic development, you are encouraged to submit your application by October 2, 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further steps.

Notes:

  • CARE seeks to improve the lives of the most marginalized, particularly women and girls. Our diversity is our strength. We are an equal opportunity employer promoting gender, equity, diversity and Inclusion. CARE’s focus as an organization is to empower women and girls as we strongly believe that they are most affected by poverty. In line with our values, we highly encourage women to apply for this position.
  • We are committed to preventing all unwanted behavior at work. This includes sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse, and child abuse. We expect everyone who works for us to share this commitment by understanding and working within the CARE Safeguarding Policy and related framework.
  • CARE International has a zero-tolerance approach to any harm to, or exploitation of any person or child by any of our staff, or partners. CARE International reserves the right to seek information from job applicants’ current and/or previous employers about incidents of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment the applicant may have been found guilty to have committed or about which an investigation was in the process of being carried out at the time of the termination of the applicant’s employment with that employer.
  • We participate in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme and will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, child abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. 
  • By submitting the application, the job applicant confirms that they have no objection to CARE International requesting the information specified above.

*Disclaimer: CARE International does not charge any kind of fee at whichever stage of the recruitment.

jobinrwanda.title: Customer Service Representative – Non-Voice
jobinrwanda.description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

CUSTOMER SERVICE REPRESENTATIVE – NON-VOICE

Company Harmony Support BPO Ltd
Department Operations / Customer Service
Position Customer Service Representative – Non-Voice
Reporting To Team Leader / Operations Supervisor
Location Kigali, Rwanda
Employment Type Full-Time

1. POSITION PURPOSE

The Customer Service Representative – Non-Voice is responsible for providing professional and efficient customer support through written communication channels, including live chat, email, messaging platforms, ticketing systems and other digital communication channels.

The employee shall respond to customer enquiries, resolve customer issues, process requests accurately, maintain customer satisfaction and ensure that all interactions comply with the Company’s operational procedures, quality standards, confidentiality requirements and client instructions.

2. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Respond professionally and promptly to customer enquiries through non-voice communication channels.
  • Handle customer requests, complaints, questions and escalations through chat, email and ticketing systems.
  • Provide accurate information in accordance with approved procedures, FAQs, knowledge bases and client instructions.
  • Investigate customer issues and provide appropriate solutions within the employee’s authority.
  • Escalate complex or sensitive matters to the Team Leader, Supervisor or appropriate department.
  • Record and update customer information accurately in CRM, ticketing and other operational systems.
  • Follow approved customer service procedures, scripts, workflows and quality standards.
  • Maintain professional, clear and grammatically correct written communication.
  • Meet assigned productivity, response-time, quality, attendance and customer-satisfaction targets.
  • Handle customer, Company and client information with strict confidentiality.
  • Comply with information-security, data-protection, access-control and other Company procedures.
  • Identify recurring customer problems and report them to the appropriate supervisor.
  • Participate in training, coaching, quality-assurance sessions and performance reviews.
  • Maintain professional conduct and a positive attitude when dealing with customers and colleagues.
  • Work according to assigned shifts, including evening, night, weekend and public-holiday shifts where required.
  • Perform other reasonable duties related to customer service and BPO operations as assigned by management.

2. PERFORMANCE RESPONSIBILITIES

The employee will be expected to achieve the operational Key Performance Indicators(KPIs)applicable to the assigned client/account, which may include:

  • Customer satisfaction (CSAT)
  • Quality assurance score
  • First response time
  • Average handling/resolution time
  • Productivity and ticket/chat volume
  • First-contact resolution
  • Attendance and punctuality
  • Adherence to assigned working schedules
  • Compliance with procedures and security requirements

Specific KPI targets maybe established or amended by management according to client requirements and operational needs.

3. QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Academic Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s Degree from a recognised higher-education institution.

Preferred fields include Business Administration, Management, Communications, Marketing, Information Technology, Languages, Hospitality, Social Sciences, or another relevant field.

4. EXPERIENCE

Previous experience in customer service, BPO, call centre, back-office operations, online support or a similar position is preferred.

Fresh graduates may be considered where they demonstrate strong communication, computer and customer-service skills.

5. REQUIRED SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES

  • Excellent written communication skills.
  • Strong English-language proficiency.
  • Good computer literacy and ability to work with multiple systems simultaneously.
  • Good typing speed and accuracy.
  • Strong attention to detail.
  • Customer-oriented approach.
  • Problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
  • Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
  • Professional and respectful communication.
  • Ability to learn new software, processes and client procedures quickly.
  • High level of confidentiality and integrity.

Knowledge of Kinyarwanda,French or other relevant languages may be considered an advantage depending on the assigned client/account.

6. WORKING CONDITIONS

The position may operate on a 24/7 operational basis, depending on client requirements.The employee may therefore be required to work day, evening or night shifts, weekends, public holidays and rotating schedules.

Working hours, rest periods,weekly rest days and overtime shall be managed in accordance with the employment contract, Company policies and applicable Rwanda labour legislation.

7. CONFIDENTIALITY AND DATA PROTECTION

The employee shall maintain strict confidentiality regarding all customer, client and Company information accessed during employment.

The employee shall not copy, disclose, transfer,misuse or retain confidential information except as authorised for legitimate business purposes.

Any breach of confidentiality, information security or Company/client procedures may result in disciplinary actionin accordance with applicable Company policies and Rwanda law.

8. REPORTING

The employee shall report directly to the designated TeamLeader/Operations Supervisor and shall comply with reasonable and lawful instructions issued by management.

How to Apply 

.The deadline for submitting applications is Thursday, October 15, 2026, at 17:00 hrs Kigali time. 

Only short-listed candidates shall be contacted..

jobinrwanda.title: Chief Strategy Officer
jobinrwanda.description:
Aviation Travel & Logistics Holding Ltd invites qualified, experienced, and visionary leaders to apply for the position of Chief Strategy Officer (CSO). The successful candidate will lead the Group’s strategic agenda and provide executive leadership in corporate strategy, business growth, portfolio management, investments, strategic partnerships, transformation, and performance management across ATL and its subsidiaries.

Job Title:Chief Strategy Officer (CSO)

Reports To:Chief Executive Officer

Job Level:C-Level

Employment Type: Full-Time

Location:Kigali, Rwanda

1. Job Purpose

The Chief Strategy Officer (CSO) will lead ATL’s enterprise-wide strategy development, strategic planning, corporate performance management, growth initiatives, investment evaluation, strategic partnerships, and transformation programmes.

Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the role will work closely with the Board, executive leadership, and subsidiary management teams to drive sustainable growth, long-term value creation, operational excellence, and effective execution of ATL’s strategic objectives across aviation, logistics, travel, training, infrastructure, and related business portfolios.

2. Key Duties & Responsibilities;

a. Group Strategy & Strategic Planning

  • Lead the formulation, execution and regularrefresh of ATL Holding’s strategy, ensuring alignment with shareholder expectations, market realities and long-term enterprise priorities.
  • Translate the Group vision into clear strategic priorities, measurable objectives and practical execution plans across ATL and its Strategic Business Units.
  • Define and refine strategic priorities, key initiatives and performance measures that guide executive decision-making and strengthen business accountability.
  • Lead the annual strategic planning cycle and facilitate executive strategy discussions across the Group.
  • Embeda consistent strategy planning framework and governance discipline across all Strategic Business Units.

b. Strategy Execution & Transformation

  • Leadenterprise-wide strategic initiatives, transformation programmes and priority projects from concept to delivery.
  • Establish clear governance, milestones, accountabilities and performance measures for major strategic initiatives.
  • Work with business leaders to resolvedelivery barriers, accelerate execution and maintain focus on strategic priorities.
  • Convert strategic priorities into well-resourced execution plans aligned with capabilities, investment choices and performance expectations.
  • Trackexecution progress and recommend timely corrective actions where performance or delivery falls behind approved plans.

c. Business Development, Growth & Portfolio Management

  • Identify and advance growth opportunities across aviation, airports, travel, logistics, training and adjacent sectors.
  • Assess acquisitions, joint ventures, partnerships, investments and new ventures with strong strategic and commercial judgement.
  • Oversee due diligence, market assessments, business cases and investment analysis to support sound executive decisions.
  • Advise the CEO, CFO, business leaders, Boards and external advisors on investment and portfolio decisions.
  • Monitor portfolio performance and recommend expansion, restructuring, optimisation or exit options that support long-term value creation.

d. Market Intelligence & Strategic Advisory

  • Provide forward-looking market intelligence to inform strategy across aviation, travel, logistics and related sectors.
  • Lead market research, competitor analysis, scenario planning and review of emerging trends, technologies and regulatory developments.
  • Assess external developments that may affect ATL’s strategy, competitive position, operating model and growth agenda.
  • Develop strategic options that mitigate emerging risks and position the Group to capture high-value opportunities.
  • Advise on business models, market entry, growth strategies, partnerships and major investment decisions.

e. Financial, Investment & Business Case Analysis

  • Partner with the CFO and business leaders to ensure strategic plans are supported by sound financial assumptions, capital requirements and sustainable business models.
  • Review and challenge business cases, financial models, investment proposals and strategic project plans to strengthen decision quality.
  • Support financial scenarios, capital planning and long-term projections for priority strategic initiatives.
  • Ensure major strategic proposals demonstrate clear strategic alignment, commercial viability, risk discipline and expected returns.
  • Support Group funding, investment and restructuring strategies in close collaboration with the CEO and CFO.

f. Performance Management & Strategic Reporting

  • Establish and oversee Group strategic performance measures, business objectives and executive-level performance indicators.
  • Lead regular strategic and business performance reviews with the CEO and business leaders to reinforce accountability and delivery focus.
  • Provideexecutive reporting on strategy execution, portfolio performance, growth opportunities and key performance trends.
  • Strengthen reporting tools and processes to improve transparency, accountability and executive decision-making.
  • Identify performance gaps and work with accountable leaders to drive timely corrective action.

g. Corporate Communications & Strategic Positioning

  • Lead the Group’s corporate communications and strategic positioning agenda, ensuring ATL’s external narrative reflects its strategy, vision and growth ambition.
  • Shape and protect ATL’s corporate reputation with government, shareholders, investors, industry partners, media and other strategic stakeholders.
  • Advise the Group CEO and Board on executive communications, stakeholder messaging, reputation matters and communications risks.
  • Lead communication of major strategic initiatives, investments, partnerships, transformation programmes and corporate milestones.
  • Oversee executive and external communications, media engagement and issues management to strengthen ATL’s visibility, credibility and sector influence.

h. Strategic Partnerships & Stakeholder Engagement

  • Develop strategic partnerships with governments, investors, financial institutions, aviation partners, development institutions and industry stakeholders.
  • Represent ATL at strategic, industry, investment and business forums as delegated by the CEO.
  • Build relationships that strengthen ATL’s market position, investment pipeline, strategic influence and access to critical capabilities.
  • Coordinate with shareholder representatives and relevant government institutions on strategic matters through the Group CEO.
  • Support clear communication of ATL’s strategic direction to employees, subsidiaries, partners, investors and other stakeholders.

i. Governance & Executive Decision Support

  • Provide strategic counsel to the Group CEO, Board and relevant Board Committees on major corporate, investment and portfolio decisions.
  • Ensure strategic initiatives are supported by appropriate governance, business cases, accountability mechanisms and decision rights.
  • Facilitate executive discussions thatstrengthen alignment, prioritisation and coordinated execution across the Group.
  • Champion a culture of strategic discipline, accountability, innovation and high performance across the Group.
  • Anticipate strategic risks and recommend mitigation measures or alternative strategic options.

3. Desired Profile

a. Qualifications & Experience

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration, Economics, Finance, Strategy, Engineering, Project Management or a related discipline. Relevant executive or professional qualifications are an advantage.
  • At least 15+ years of progressive experience in strategy, business development, investment, transformation or a related field, with significantsenior leadership exposure.
  • Proven track record of shaping and executing corporate strategies, growth agendas, transformation programmes and major strategic initiatives.
  • Strong experience in investment evaluation, portfolio management, strategic partnerships and business case development.
  • Experience in aviation, travel, logistics, infrastructure or another complex, regulated or multinational environment is highly desirable.

b. Core Competencies

  • Strategic Leadership & Corporate Strategy
  • Business Growth, Development & Portfolio Management
  • Commercial, Investment & Financial Acumen
  • Market Intelligence, Strategic Risk & Foresight
  • Transformation & Strategy Execution

How to Apply

Interested candidate should submit their application no later than 05th October 2026. Please click on the “Apply” button to complete your application.

Interested candidates should also submit their application including an application letter, updated curriculum vitae, copies of academic and professional certificates, and any other relevant supporting documents through the official recruitment channel indicated by ATL.

Applications should clearly indicate the position applied for: Chief Strategy Officer (CSO).

Equal Opportunity Statement

ATL is an equal opportunity employer. Recruitment will be conducted on the basis of merit, competence, leadership experience, and alignment with the requirements of the position.

jobinrwanda.title: Quantity Surveyor
jobinrwanda.description:
Aviation Travel & Logistics Holding Ltd invites qualified, competent, and motivated candidates to apply for the position of Quantity Surveyor. The role will support cost planning, estimating, procurement, contract administration, cost control, commercial risk management, and value-for-money delivery across ATL's aviation and airport infrastructure projects, including logistics, travel, infrastructure, and related development projects.

Job Title:Quantity Surveyor

Reports To:Senior Site Engineer 

Job Level:Senior Specialist

Employment Type:Full-Time

Location:Kigali/Bugesera, Rwanda

1. Job Purpose

The Senior Quantity Surveyor will provide senior-level professional cost, commercial and quantity surveying expertise and leadership throughout the planning, design, procurement, construction and completion of ATL's aviation and airport infrastructure projects.

The role will ensure effective cost planning, estimating, budgeting, tendering, contract administration, cost control and commercial risk management, while ensuring that project expenditure remains aligned with approved budgets, scope, quality, programme and value-for-money objectives. The Senior Quantity Surveyor will also provide commercial leadership, direction and mentorship to project quantity surveyors and cost control staff, and may deputise for senior commercial leadership on aviation and airport infrastructure matters as required.

2. Key Duties & Responsibilities;

a. Cost Planning & Estimation

  • Develop and maintain project cost plans, estimates and budgets for ATL projects and work packages.
  • Prepare and review Bills of Quantities (BoQs), cost estimates, schedules of rates and other cost documentation.
  • Undertake cost analysis and benchmarking against comparable international airport and infrastructure projects.
  • Monitor changes in scope, design and market conditions and assess their impact on project costs.
  • Provide cost advice to support design development, value engineering and investment decisions.
  • Provide senior commercial leadership, direction and mentorship to project quantity surveyors and cost control staff engaged on ATL aviation and airport infrastructure projects.

b. Procurement & Tender Management

  • Support the development of procurement strategies, tender documentation and commercial evaluation criteria.
  • Prepare, review and analyse tender documents, BoQs, pricing schedules and contractors’ submissions.
  • Participate in tender evaluation and provide professional advice on pricing, commercial risks and value for money.
  • Support negotiations with contractors, consultants and suppliers in accordance with approved procurement procedures.
  • Ensure procurement decisions are consistent with approved budgets, project requirements and applicable procurement regulations.

c. Contract Administration

  • Support the administration of construction, consultancy and supply contracts throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Monitor contractual obligations, payment provisions, milestones, variations, claims and commercial deliverables.
  • Review and assess contractor payment applications, interim valuations, certificates and final accounts.
  • Provide advice on contractual and commercial matters and escalate potential disputes or financial exposures.
  • Maintain accurate records of contractual and commercial information.

d. Cost Control & Financial Management

  • Monitor actual and committed expenditure against approved project budgets and cost plans.
  • Maintain comprehensive cost reports, forecasts and cash-flow projections.
  • Track cost movements, variations, commitments and potential cost overruns and provide early-warning reports.
  • Analyse financial implications of design changes, project delays, claims and scope changes.
  • Recommend corrective actions to maintain cost discipline and protect project financial objectives.

e. Variations, Claims & Commercial Risk

  • Assess and advise on variations, extensions of time, claims, compensation events and other commercial matters.
  • Evaluate the financial and contractual impact of proposed changes and provide recommendations to project leadership.
  • Identify commercial risks and support appropriate mitigation strategies.
  • Support the resolution of contractual and commercial disputes in coordination with project management and legal teams.
  • Ensure all commercial adjustments are properly documented, justified and approved.

f. Value Engineering & Cost Optimisation

  • Lead or support value engineering and cost optimisation initiatives throughout design and construction.
  • Evaluate alternative materials, technologies, construction methods and design solutions.
  • Identify opportunities to improve whole-life value while maintaining required safety, quality, operational performance and aviation standards.
  • Provide commercial input into design reviews and major technical decisions.

g. Project Reporting & Commercial Governance

  • Prepare regular cost, commercial and contract management reports for ATL project leadership and relevant governance structures.
  • Maintain accurate records of budgets, forecasts, commitments, payments, variations, claims and final accounts.
  • Provide timely commercial advice on project performance, emerging cost pressures and financial risks.
  • Support project audits and ensure compliance with approved financial, procurement and contract management procedures.
  • Contribute to project reviews, steering committees and other governance forums as required.

h. Project Close-Out & Handover

  • Support preparation and agreement of final accounts and commercial close-out of contracts.
  • Verify completion of contractual obligations and outstanding commercial matters.
  • Support resolution of final claims, variations and defects-related financial matters.
  • Ensure complete and accurate commercial documentation is maintained for project handover and audit purposes.

3. Desired Profile

a. Qualifications & Experience

  • Demonstrated experience providing commercial leadership, guidance and mentorship to quantity surveyors and cost teams on complex capital projects.
  • Strong knowledge of contract management, variations, claims, commercial risk management, contract negotiations, and FIDIC or similar international construction contracts. 
  • Demonstrated expertise in cost planning, estimating, procurement, tender evaluation, contract administration, cost control, and final accounts management. 
  • Proven experience delivering large-scale aviation, airport, transportation, infrastructure, commercial, or other complex capital projects. 
  • Minimum of 8 years’ experience in quantity surveying, cost management, commercial management, or project controls, including prior experience operating at a senior or lead commercial level. https://aviationtravellogistics-my.sharepoint.com/personal/francis_shyaka_atl_rw/_layouts/15/Doc.aspx?sourcedoc={B80AD200-A9AA-4422-ABD0-BD80DDB0C8CB}&file=Quantity Surveyor - Advert.docx&action=default&mobileredirect=true
  • Bachelor’s degree in Quantity Surveying, Construction Economics, Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field; A Master’s degree and professional certification (RICS, AIQS, or equivalent) are an added advantage. 

b. Core Competencies

  • Cost Planning, Estimation & Commercial Analysis
  • Quantity Surveying & Cost Control
  • Procurement & Tender Management
  • Contract Administration & Commercial Management
  • Claims, Variations & Commercial Risk Management
  • Value Engineering & Cost Optimisation
  • Stakeholder Management, Negotiation & Reporting
  • Commercial Leadership & Team Mentoring

How to Apply

jobinrwanda.title: Electrical Engineer
jobinrwanda.description:
Aviation Travel & Logistics Holding Ltd invites qualified, competent, and motivated candidates to apply for the position of Electrical Engineer. The role will support the design, coordination, installation, testing, commissioning, and technical oversight of electrical systems for ATL projects, including aviation, airport, logistics, and related infrastructure projects.

Job Title:Electrical Engineer

Reports To:Senior Site Engineer 

Job Level:Specialist

Employment Type:Full-Time

Location:Kigali/Bugesera, Rwanda

1. Job Purpose

The Electrical Engineer will provide professional engineering expertise in the design, coordination, installation, testing and commissioning of electrical systems across ATL projects. The role will ensure that electrical infrastructure and systems are safe, reliable, energy-efficient and fit for continuous airport operations, while complying with ICAO requirements, applicable Rwandan regulations, approved designs and international engineering standards.

2. Key Duties & Responsibilities;

a. Electrical Design & Engineering

  • Develop, review and coordinate electrical designs, drawings, calculations, specifications and technical documentation for ATL facilities, projects, and infrastructure.
  • Ensure electrical systems meet airport operational requirements, approved project specifications, applicable codes and relevant international standards.
  • Review design proposals and technical submissions and recommend technically sound, safe and cost-effective solutions.
  • Support design development, value engineering and technical optimisation throughout the project lifecycle.

b. Electrical Systems & Infrastructure

  • Provide technical oversight for electrical systems including power generation, medium- and low-voltage distribution, substations, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, lighting, emergency power and earthing systems.
  • Coordinate electrical requirements for terminal buildings, airside and landside facilities, utilities and other airport infrastructure.
  • Ensure appropriate redundancy, reliability and resilience are incorporated into critical airport electrical systems.
  • Coordinate electrical interfaces with mechanical, civil, structural, ICT, aviation systems and other specialist disciplines.

c. Construction Supervision & Technical Assurance

  • Monitor installation and construction activities to ensure compliance with approved electrical designs, drawings, specifications and method statements.
  • Conduct site inspections and verify workmanship, materials, equipment and installation quality.
  • Review contractor shop drawings, material submissions, method statements, inspection and test plans and technical queries.
  • Identify defects, non-conformances and technical issues and ensure appropriate corrective actions are implemented.
  • Provide technical guidance to contractors and coordinate resolution of electrical engineering challenges.

d. Aviation Safety, Compliance & Standards

  • Ensure electrical systems comply with applicable ICAO Standards and Recommended Practices, Rwanda Civil Aviation Authority requirements, national regulations and recognised international electrical standards.
  • Ensure appropriate electrical safety, fire protection, emergency power, lightning protection, earthing and equipment protection measures are incorporated.
  • Support regulatory inspections, technical reviews, approvals and compliance assessments.
  • Identify electrical safety and compliance risks and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.

e. Testing, Commissioning & Handover

  • Develop and review testing and commissioning requirements for electrical systems and equipment.
  • Witness and verify testing of power generation, distribution, protection, lighting, emergency power and other critical electrical systems.
  • Support system commissioning, integrated testing and operational readiness activities.
  • Review test certificates, commissioning records, as-built drawings and operation and maintenance documentation.
  • Support snagging, defect rectification and final handover of electrical systems.

f. Energy Efficiency & Sustainability

  • Support the implementation of energy-efficient and sustainable electrical solutions across ATL projects.
  • Evaluate opportunities for energy optimisation, renewable energy integration, intelligent lighting and efficient power management.
  • Provide technical input into energy performance, lifecycle cost and sustainability considerations.
  • Support monitoring and improvement of electrical energy consumption and system efficiency.

g. Project Coordination & Risk Management

  • Monitor electrical engineering deliverables, construction progress and technical milestones.
  • Identify design, construction, supply and interface risks affecting electrical systems and recommend mitigation measures.
  • Provide technical input into variations, claims, design changes and contractor proposals.
  • Coordinate with project controls, quantity surveying and commercial teams on electrical works and technical changes.
  • Support achievement of project scope, quality, cost, safety and schedule objectives.

h. Technical Reporting & Documentation

  • Prepare technical reports, site inspection reports, design review comments and progress updates.
  • Maintain accurate records of electrical drawings, calculations, inspections, tests, approvals and technical decisions.
  • Track outstanding technical issues, non-conformances, design changes and corrective actions.
  • Provide professional technical advice and recommendations to project leadership.

3. Desired Profile

a. Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electrical & Electronic Engineering, Power Systems Engineering or a related discipline; a Master’s degree is an added advantage.
  • Professional registration with the relevant Rwandan engineering professional body and a valid practising licence, where applicable, is required.
  • Minimum 5+ years of relevant electrical engineering experience, preferably in major infrastructure, airports, transportation, commercial, industrial or other critical infrastructure projects.
  • Proven experience in the design, supervision and delivery of large-scale electrical systems, including power generation and distribution, MV/LV systems, substations, emergency power, lighting, earthing and electrical safety systems.
  • Strong knowledge of ICAO requirements, applicable Rwandan regulations and recognised international electrical standards, with experience coordinating multidisciplinary teams, consultants, contractors and specialist suppliers.

b. Core Competencies

  • Electrical design and power systems
  • Construction supervision and quality control
  • Aviation safety and compliance
  • Testing and commissioning
  • Risk management and reporting

The role will ensure that all architectural and engineering solutions are technically sound, operationally fit for purpose and compliant with applicable laws and regulations, approved project requirements, safety standards, quality requirements and sustainability objectives. 

The position will work as part of multidisciplinary project teams, coordinating with designers, consultants, contractors, regulators, stakeholders and other technical specialists to support the successful delivery of ATL projects to the required quality, cost, schedule, safety and performance standards. jobinrwanda.title: Research Project Director
jobinrwanda.description:
Job Description: Research Project Director

Projects: HealthyStart and PROPS Rwanda
Duty Station: Rwanda with project-site travel
Reports to: Principal Investigator
Employment Terms: One-year renewable, subject to funding

Position Overview

The Research Project Director is a senior management position responsible for the overall executive leadership, management, and operational delivery of the HealthyStart and PROPS Rwanda Projects. The Research Project Director will work closely with the Principal Investigator to shape project strategy, annual workplans, budgets, and implementation priorities. The Director will hold overall responsibility for project operations, financial management, staffing, partnerships, risk management, compliance, and delivery of project objectives across all project teams, sites, and partners. The successful candidate will ensure that the projects are implemented on time, within approved budgets, and in accordance with approved protocols, ethical and regulatory requirements, donor agreements, safeguarding standards, and institutional policies.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide overall executive leadership and management of the projects, setting operational direction and priorities for all project teams.
  • Work with the Principal Investigator to shape project strategy, annual workplans and budgets, and lead their implementation across teams, sites and partners.
  • Hold overall accountability for project budgets, approving expenditures within delegated authority and ensuring sound financial management, forecasting and reporting.
  • Lead the recruitment, appointment, performance management and development of project staff in coordination with the KFHRF HR team and decide on staffing structures within approved budgets.
  • Chair the project management team and represent the projects in senior-level meetings with donors, government institutions, implementing partners and institutional leadership.
  • Monitor milestones, deliverables and risks, make timely decisions to resolve operational challenges and direct corrective action.
  • Ensure compliance with approved protocols, ethical and regulatory requirements, donor agreements, safeguarding standards and institutional policies.
  • Approve progress reports and key project documents before submission, and escalate major scientific, clinical or strategic matters to the Principal Investigator.
  • Build a culture of teamwork, accountability, problem-solving and continuous improvement.

Authority and Accountability

  • The Research Project Director shall advise and, when required, make decisions concerning the operations and management of the projects, acting within approved protocols, budgets, donor agreements, institutional policies, and delegated authority.
  • The Director's areas of authority include, but are not limited to:
  • Operational decisions: Setting priorities, allocating resources, and assigning work across project teams and sites.
  • Financial decisions: Approving expenditures, procurement, and budget reallocations within approved budget lines and delegated financial limits.
  • People decisions: Recruiting, appointing, supervising, evaluating, and managing project staff, including approval of leave, travel, and performance-related actions within delegated authority.
  • Partnership decisions: Signing off on operational arrangements, reports, and communications with partners within delegated authority.
  • Risk and implementation decisions: Taking timely corrective and operational decisions to address project implementation challenges within approved authority.
  • Scientific, clinical, and protocol decisions, as well as changes to the overall project strategy, total project budget, or contractual commitments with donors, shall be made jointly with the Principal Investigator and approved by the relevant institutional authorities.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  • Master's degree in Public Health, Health Policy, Project Management, Health Management, or another relevant field.
  • At least ten (10) years of progressively responsible experience in public health, research, programme implementation, or project leadership.
  • At least five (5) years of experience in a senior management role with responsibility for budgets and staff.
  • Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary teams.
  • Demonstrated experience managing complex, multi-partner health or research projects in Rwanda.
  • Demonstrated experience in project planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Strong experience in financial management, budget oversight, and resource allocation.
  • Strong experience in stakeholder and partnership management.
  • Demonstrated experience in staff management and performance management.
  • Strong understanding of research, public health, and project implementation environments.
  • Excellent leadership, strategic planning, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent communication skills in English and Kinyarwanda.

Preferred

  • Experience managing donor-funded health or research projects.
  • Experience working with international research institutions or development partners.
  • Experience working with government institutions and public-sector health programmes in Rwanda.
  • Experience managing multi-site research or public health programmes.
  • Knowledge of research ethics, regulatory requirements, and institutional research governance.
  • Experience in project risk management and organizational change management.
  • Knowledge of donor compliance and reporting requirements.
  • French language proficiency.

Required Technical and Management Skills

  • Strategic project management.
  • Project planning and implementation.
  • Budget development and financial management.
  • Staff and team management.
  • Performance management.
  • Risk management.
  • Stakeholder and partnership management.
  • Monitoring and reporting.
  • Resource allocation and operational planning.
  • Microsoft Office and project management tools.
  • Report writing and presentation skills.
  • Data interpretation for project performance monitoring.
  • Understanding of research and public health project management systems.

How to Apply:

Interested candidates should apply via this link by October 05, 2026

Within the health domain, the Foundation’s major objectives will be to support researchers through funding, training and facilitation in dissemination of research data, establishing strategic relationships with academic, research-driven and research sponsoring institutions and supporting training for medical researchers. As part of a social welfare that constitutes an integral part of the foundation, the hospital will financially assist patients who cannot afford medical care and will continue to sensitize the public on NCDs, congenital and surgical diseases for prevention and early consultation. jobinrwanda.title: Laboratory Technologist
jobinrwanda.description:
Job Description: Laboratory Technologist – PROPS Trial

Project: PROPS Trial (Efficacy of Probiotic Supplementation in Preterm and Small-for-Gestational-Age Infants)
Duty Station: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Laboratory, Kigali, with liaison to hospital laboratories and the centralised study laboratory under the trial’s hub-and-spoke model
Reports to: Principal Investigator, in coordination with the Site Laboratory Lead/Co-Investigator
Employment Terms: Fixed-term, for the duration of the PROPS trial at the Rwanda site, renewable subject to performance and funding

Position Overview

The Laboratory Technologist will be responsible for the receipt, processing, quality-controlled analysis, and storage of biological specimens, including blood culture and faecal specimens, collected under the PROPS Trial. The Laboratory Technologist will ensure that all laboratory procedures are performed accurately, safely, and in strict compliance with the study protocol, trial laboratory SOPs, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), ICH-GCP, national laboratory requirements, biosafety standards, and institutional policies.

The Laboratory Technologist will support the trial's hub-and-spoke laboratory model, including specimen reception and initial processing, transportation and receipt of specimens at the centralised study laboratory, definitive processing, biobanking, quality assurance, documentation, and preparation of specimens for further analysis or shipment as required by the study protocol.

Key Responsibilities

  • Ensure readiness of all laboratory-related SOPs, protocols, equipment, supplies, and processes as required by the PROPS multi-country assessment team.
  • Receive, log, and verify blood culture and faecal specimens delivered from study sites, hospital collection points, and home visits, and verify specimen identifiers against accompanying request forms, CRFs, and study records.
  • Ensure blood culture specimens are appropriately inoculated, transported, received, and processed within the required timelines, including receipt within one hour at the hospital laboratory and within 24 hours at the central laboratory, as applicable.
  • Process blood culture specimens using automated blood culture equipment and approved standard laboratory methods.
  • Process faecal specimens using the laboratory methods specified in the study protocol and applicable SOPs.
  • Freeze isolates and specimens at the specified temperatures, including −20°C to −80°C for faecal specimens and −60°C to −80°C for blood culture isolates requiring further testing.
  • Maintain the study biorepository/freezers, including temperature monitoring, freezer maintenance logs, and organised and retrievable storage of specimens for the approved retention period.
  • Package and prepare specimens for transport or shipment to the centralised laboratory or other approved destination, maintaining cold-chain integrity and completing the relevant shipment and freezer-storage logs.
  • Complete all laboratory-related CRFs, logs, registers, and study documentation accurately and promptly, including specimen reception, automated blood culture processing, blood isolate processing, faecal specimen processing, freezer storage, and shipment logs.
  • Communicate laboratory results, particularly positive blood culture results, promptly to the clinical/outcome team as required by the study protocol.
  • Participate in internal quality control and quality assurance activities and support external audits, monitoring visits, and assessments conducted by the study team, contracted infectious disease consultants, sponsors, or relevant authorities.
  • Address and document findings related to specimen handling, storage, processing, documentation, equipment, and laboratory procedures in accordance with approved corrective and preventive actions.
  • Maintain up-to-date ICH-GCP certification and complete all study-specific laboratory SOP training before undertaking trial-related laboratory duties, together with required refresher training.
  • Maintain specimen confidentiality and data protection in accordance with the study's consent provisions, national regulations, and institutional requirements, including restrictions relating to specimen export and secondary use.
  • Follow national biosafety, infection prevention and control, occupational safety, and laboratory waste-management procedures at all times when handling biological specimens.
  • Maintain laboratory equipment, including automated blood culture systems, freezers, thermometers, and other relevant equipment, in good working condition and escalate equipment faults or temperature excursions immediately.
  • Ensure proper specimen traceability from receipt through processing, storage, retrieval, shipment, and final disposition.
  • Work collaboratively with clinical, outcome, data, research, laboratory, and other study teams to ensure timely and effective implementation of laboratory activities.
  • Support the Principal Investigator and study team with any other laboratory-related duties required for the successful conduct of the PROPS Trial.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  • Master of Science (MSc) in Biotechnology, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical Sciences, or a closely related field.
  • Valid registration/license as a Laboratory Technologist/Technician with the relevant Rwandan professional regulatory body, such as the Rwanda Allied Health Professions Council, or national accreditation as required by the trial protocol.
  • A minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience in a clinical, microbiology, or research laboratory, preferably within a hospital or clinical trial setting.
  • Demonstrated experience in laboratory specimen reception, processing, documentation, storage, and quality control.
  • Sound understanding of biosafety, infection prevention and control, and safe handling of biological specimens.
  • Ability to accurately maintain laboratory records, CRFs, specimen logs, freezer records, and shipment documentation.
  • Ability to work in accordance with laboratory SOPs, study protocols, quality management procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Ability to maintain confidentiality and security of participant information, biological specimens, and study data.

Preferred

  • Experience working with automated blood culture systems.
  • Experience with faecal or other microbiological specimen processing.
  • Experience with cold-chain specimen handling and storage.
  • Prior experience working on a clinical trial.
  • Experience working in a GCLP- or ICH-GCP-compliant laboratory environment.
  • Experience with biobanking and long-term biological specimen storage.
  • Familiarity with electronic data capture systems or laboratory information management systems.
  • Experience supporting laboratory audits, monitoring visits, or external quality assessments.
  • Experience working within a multi-site or multi-country research study.

Required Technical and Management Skills

  • Laboratory specimen processing and handling.
  • Microbiological specimen processing.
  • Automated blood culture systems.
  • Biological specimen storage and biobanking.
  • Cold-chain management.
  • Laboratory quality control and quality assurance.
  • Biosafety and infection prevention and control.
  • Laboratory documentation and record keeping.
  • Completion of CRFs, specimen logs, freezer records, and shipment documentation.
  • ICH-GCP and Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP).
  • Laboratory equipment operation and maintenance.
  • Specimen traceability and data management.
  • Microsoft Office and relevant laboratory/data management systems.
  • Report writing and documentation skills.
  • Good communication and teamwork skills.
  • Understanding of clinical research and laboratory systems.

How to Apply:

Interested candidates should apply via this link by October 05, 2026

jobinrwanda.description:
Job Description: Senior Pharmacist (Chief Study Pharmacist) – PROPS Trial

Project: PROPS Trial (Efficacy of Probiotic Supplementation in Preterm and Small-for-Gestational-Age Infants)
Duty Station: Central study office/pharmacy, King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Foundation, Kigali, with oversight of investigational product (IP) storage at participating study hospital sites
Reports to: Principal Investigator, with functional reporting to the Study Sponsor/Coordinating Centre on investigational product (IP) matters
Employment Terms: One year (Renewable), for the duration of the PROPS trial at the Rwanda site, renewable subject to performance and funding

Position Overview

The Senior Pharmacist (Chief Study Pharmacist) will have overall responsibility for the receipt, storage, blinding integrity, allocation, distribution, monitoring, accountability, and destruction of the investigational product (IP) and placebo used in the PROPS Trial. The Chief Study Pharmacist will ensure that all investigational product management activities are conducted accurately and in strict compliance with the Investigational Product Management SOP, Product Provision SOP, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable national pharmaceutical regulations, and trial requirements.

The Chief Study Pharmacist will oversee central receipt and storage of investigational product, coordinate IP overlabelling and blinding activities, maintain participant ID master lists, manage site-level IP supply and replenishment, monitor temperature and storage conditions, oversee IP accountability and reconciliation, and coordinate end-of-study destruction. The position will also provide supervision, training, and technical guidance to pharmacy and unblinded support staff involved in trial IP management.

Key Responsibilities

  • Ensure investigational product is stored immediately under controlled temperature conditions of 2–8°C upon receipt and maintained under continuous temperature monitoring.
  • Coordinate and directly oversee the unblinded team responsible for overlabelling individual IP sticks to obscure manufacturer batch numbers while preserving the integrity of trial blinding and complying with applicable regulatory requirements.
  • Ensure that IP Temperature Deviation Logs are completed for any period during which IP boxes are outside the required 2–8°C storage range during overlabelling activities, and ensure that overlabelling records are complete and accurate.
  • Maintain the master lists of available participant IDs separately for preterm and term SGA infants and generate and verify daily sub-lists for IP allocation across participating study sites.
  • Reconcile participant ID master lists on a daily basis, recycle unused participant IDs where permitted, and ensure unused participant boxes are appropriately reissued to minimise product wastage.
  • Review and approve requests from site/hospital pharmacists for IP box shipments, ensuring participating hospital sites maintain an appropriate buffer supply, including at least a two-week supply where required by the study.
  • Ensure IP shipments to participating hospital sites are dispatched in appropriate temperature-controlled containers, including cool boxes with icepacks and thermometers, with complete and accurate shipment documentation.
  • Ensure the PROPS IP Temperature Monitoring Log, including required AM and PM readings, is completed at every storage location and that temperature excursions are promptly reported to the Site Principal Investigator within the required timeframe.
  • Monitor cumulative time that IP sachets are outside the required 2–8°C range and ensure that applicable study thresholds are not exceeded, taking appropriate corrective action where thresholds are approached or breached.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for the Sponsor, Coordinating Centre, external monitors, auditors, and relevant regulatory stakeholders on all investigational product-related matters.
  • Maintain inspection- and audit-ready IP accountability records, including receipt, storage, overlabelling, allocation, distribution, temperature monitoring, reconciliation, return, and destruction records.
  • Lead end-of-study reconciliation of remaining, unused, and expired investigational product and coordinate destruction in accordance with applicable regulations and Sponsor/Coordinating Centre requirements.
  • Coordinate destruction of expired or unused IP with an appropriately licensed incineration facility and ensure all required approvals and documentation are obtained.
  • Obtain and retain incineration certificates and ensure the PROPS IP Destruction Log is completed accurately and retained within the study records.
  • Supervise, train, and mentor Pharmacist(s) and pharmacy/unblinded support staff on the Investigational Product Management SOP, Product Provision SOP, and other relevant trial procedures.
  • Monitor compliance of pharmacy staff with study-specific procedures and ensure that required training and certifications are maintained throughout the trial.
  • Maintain and, where necessary, escalate proposed updates to IP-related SOPs, logs, forms, and processes in collaboration with the Principal Investigator and Coordinating Centre.
  • Ensure all pharmacy staff complete and maintain current ICH-GCP certification and study-specific training before undertaking trial-related IP activities.
  • Identify, document, and escalate IP quality concerns, temperature excursions, stock discrepancies, supply interruptions, and other issues that may affect participant safety, trial integrity, or study compliance.
  • Ensure strict confidentiality and protection of information related to participant IDs, investigational products, randomisation, allocation, and trial documentation.
  • Support the Principal Investigator and study team with other pharmacy and investigational product management duties required for the successful conduct and closeout of the PROPS Trial.

Qualifications and Experience

Essential

  • Minimum of Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) or equivalent professional pharmacy qualification.
  • Current registration and valid license to practice as a pharmacist with the Rwanda Pharmacy Council or equivalent national regulatory body.
  • Minimum of ten (10) years of post-registration professional experience, including experience in hospital pharmacy, clinical trial pharmacy, investigational product management, pharmaceutical supply-chain management, or related areas.
  • Demonstrated experience in pharmacy operations, pharmaceutical inventory management, storage, distribution, and accountability.
  • Prior supervisory or team-leadership experience.
  • Current ICH-GCP certification, or demonstrated willingness and ability to complete the required certification before undertaking trial activities.
  • Working knowledge of Rwanda FDA requirements and applicable national pharmaceutical and regulatory requirements for clinical trials.
  • Demonstrated ability to maintain accurate pharmaceutical records, accountability documentation, and temperature-controlled storage records.
  • Strong understanding of confidentiality requirements and the importance of maintaining trial blinding and allocation safeguards.

Preferred

  • Master's degree in Pharmacy or related pharmaceutical sciences.
  • Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) qualification.
  • Prior experience managing investigational products in a clinical trial.
  • Experience with blinded clinical trial products and overlabelling procedures.
  • Experience managing temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical products and cold-chain systems.
  • Experience coordinating pharmaceutical supply and inventory across multiple hospital sites.
  • Experience supporting clinical trial monitoring visits, audits, or regulatory inspections.
  • Experience with clinical trial IP management systems, electronic tracking systems, or tablet-based applications.
  • Experience working with international research institutions, Sponsors, or clinical trial Coordinating Centres.

Required Technical and Management Skills

  • Investigational product management.
  • Clinical trial pharmacy operations.
  • Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
  • Good Pharmacy Practice.
  • Pharmaceutical inventory and stock management.
  • Cold-chain management and temperature monitoring.
  • IP receipt, storage, allocation, distribution, reconciliation, and destruction.
  • Blinding and randomisation safeguards.
  • Pharmaceutical documentation and accountability systems.
  • Temperature deviation and excursion management.
  • Multi-site pharmaceutical logistics and supply management.
  • Quality assurance and regulatory compliance.
  • Audit and inspection readiness.
  • Staff supervision, training, and mentoring.
  • Risk identification, problem-solving, and corrective action.
  • Confidentiality and protection of trial information.
  • Electronic data, inventory, and IP tracking systems.
  • Microsoft Office and relevant pharmacy or study management systems.
  • Report writing and documentation skills.
  • Understanding of clinical research and pharmaceutical regulatory systems.

How to Apply:

Interested candidates should apply via this link by October 05, 2026

jobinrwanda.title: Plant Operator
jobinrwanda.description:
Job Title: Plant Operator (Processing)
Location: Kigali, Processing Plant
Reporting to: Mike Crivea

Contract Type: Full-time, on-site (shift-based operations)

About Kivu Choice:

Kivu Choice is Rwanda’s largest protein producer and one of the fastest-growing aquaculture companies in Africa. Founded in 2022, Kivu Choice is the sister company to Victory Farms, East Africa’s leading aquaculture platform based in Kenya. The company operates a fully vertically integrated aquaculture model, encompassing hatchery operations, cage-based grow-out, processing, distribution, and sales. Kivu Choice is also one of the country’s largest employers with over 700 employees, and plans to grow to 1,200 employees within the next three years, reflecting its strong commitment to job creation and inclusive economic development. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region.

Job Purpose:

The plant operator leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Production & Process Control

  • Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines.
  • Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent.
  • Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment.
  • Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste.
  • Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders.

2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance

  • Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities.
  • Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum.
  • Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory.
  • Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs.
  • Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion.

3. Quality Control & Food Safety

  • Implement and maintain food safety systems in line with HACCP, GMP, and ISO 22000 principles.
  • Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached.
  • Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant.
  • Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings.
  • Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods.

4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity

  • Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges.
  • Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points.
  • Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution.

5. Shift Leadership & People Management

  • Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers.
  • Train operators on safe equipment use, SOPs, hygiene, and food safety practices.
  • Set clear performance expectations, give regular feedback, and contribute to performance reviews.
  • Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations.

6. Production Reporting & KPIs

  • Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste.
  • Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management.
  • Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records.
  • Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts.

Qualifications & Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, industrial, or food process engineering, food science, or a related field.
  • At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines.
  • Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs.
  • Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000.
  • Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus.
  • Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment.
  • Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel.
  • Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose equipment and process issues quickly under pressure.
  • Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role).
  • Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda; French or Swahili is an advantage.

How to Apply:

  • If you are interested in this position, prepare the following:
  • Job application letter
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Copy of your degree and other academic qualifications
  • Copy of your ID How to apply: send all the required documents to our email address: recruiting@kivuchoice.com 
  • Submission Deadline: 30th September 2026.
  • Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis as they are submitted.
  • Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
