jobinrwanda.description:
APPENDIX A

PALAST ROCK HOTEL (PRH) Ltd

Job Title: General Manager

Department: General Manager (GM)’s Office

Direct Reports to: Palast Group CEO 

Functional Reports to: The Group DCEO, Group HR Manager & Group Operations Manager. 

Job Description 

Palast Rock Hotel (PRH), a subsidiary of Palast Group Ltd, is a dynamic hospitality establishment currently operating as a 3-Star hotel with a clear strategic ambition to elevate its standards toward 4-Star recognition while consistently delivering a 4 plus -Star guest experience during the process. The hotel is committed to providing professional, high-quality, and customer-centered services across accommodation, Banqueting and events, restaurants & bars, as well as wellness and recreational facilities including sauna, massage, swimming pool, gym, and sports amenities.

PRH is driven by a culture of operational excellence, continuous improvement, and exceptional guest satisfaction. Through strong teamwork, professionalism, and innovation, the hotel aims to position itself among the leading hospitality destinations, recognized for superior service delivery, strong brand reputation, and an unwavering commitment to exceeding guest expectations.

Position Summary:

The General Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, operational performance, financial performance, and business growth of Palast Rock Hotel.

The role provides leadership and direction to all hotel departments and ensures effective coordination of accommodation, food and beverage, conferences and events, wellness and recreational services, and supporting functions.

The General Manager is accountable for maintaining high standards of hospitality, guest satisfaction, operational excellence, financial sustainability, staff performance, regulatory compliance, and PRH brand standards, in line with the vision, objectives, and strategic direction of Palast Group.

Key Responsibilities Include but not Limited to:

Strategic Leadership & Business Management

  • Provide overall leadership and strategic direction for Palast Rock Hotel.
  • Develop and implement annual business plans, operational strategies, and performance objectives aligned with the hotel's strategic goals.
  • Translate the hotel's strategic objectives into clear departmental priorities, targets, and action plans.
  • Lead initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency, profitability, service quality, and business growth.
  • Advise the Group CEO and senior management on hotel performance, business opportunities, operational challenges, and strategic priorities.
  • Represent the hotel in key business, professional, government, corporate, and stakeholder engagements.
  • Promote a culture of professionalism, accountability, teamwork, innovation, and service excellence.

Hotel Operations & Service Excellence

  • Provide overall oversight of the hotel's day-to-day operations and ensure effective coordination across all departments.
  • Oversee accommodation, restaurants and bars, conferences, weddings and events, wellness and recreational facilities, and other hotel services.
  • Ensure departments operate in accordance with approved policies, procedures, service standards, and operational requirements.
  • Monitor service delivery and ensure appropriate action is taken to address operational gaps and improve efficiency.
  • Monitor guest satisfaction and ensure guest complaints and service issues are addressed promptly and professionally.
  • Ensure appropriate standards of cleanliness, safety, maintenance, functionality, and presentation of hotel facilities and equipment.
  • Oversee the implementation of quality assurance and continuous service improvement initiatives.
  • Ensure effective planning and coordination of major conferences, weddings, events, and other functions hosted by the hotel.

Financial Performance & Cost Management

  • Take overall accountability for the financial performance and profitability of the hotel.
  •  Review and monitor budgets, financial reports, forecasts, revenue performance, and expenditure plans.
  • Monitor hotel revenues, operational costs, departmental performance, and profitability against approved targets.
  • Ensure effective cost control and responsible utilization of hotel resources.
  • Support the implementation of revenue optimization and business development strategies.
  • Review and authorize purchases, contracts, and operational expenditures within approved authority limits.
  • Work closely with the Finance & Administration Manager and Group Finance function to ensure accurate financial reporting, financial controls, and compliance.
  • Monitor key financial indicators and ensure appropriate corrective actions are taken where performance is below target.

Sales, Marketing & Business Development

  • Provide leadership and support in the development and implementation of sales, marketing, and revenue-generation strategies.
  • Drive initiatives aimed at increasing room occupancy, food and beverage revenue, conferences, events, weddings, and other revenue streams.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with corporate clients, government institutions, travel agencies, business partners, and other key stakeholders.
  • Identify new business opportunities, partnerships, and potential markets for the hotel.
  • Monitor market trends, customer preferences, competitor activities, and industry developments to support the hotel's competitiveness.
  • Promote the PRH brand, reputation, products, and services through appropriate business and market engagement activities.

People Leadership & Performance Management

  • Provide leadership, direction, and support to Heads of Departments and hotel management teams.
  • Ensure appropriate staffing levels, workforce planning, and deployment of employees in line with operational requirements.
  • Ensure clear departmental objectives, performance targets, and accountability across the hotel.
  • Promote staff development, coaching, training, succession planning, and employee engagement initiatives.
  • Foster a professional, respectful, collaborative, and performance-oriented working environment.
  • Ensure employee relations and disciplinary matters are handled fairly, consistently, and in accordance with company policies and applicable labour requirements.
  • Monitor staff productivity, performance, conduct, and adherence to hotel and company standards.
  • Work closely with HR to address workforce-related matters and strengthen employee performance and engagement.

Compliance, Risk Management & Internal Controls

  • Ensure compliance with applicable hospitality regulations, labour laws, health and safety requirements, licensing requirements, and other legal and regulatory obligations.
  • Ensure effective implementation of internal controls, risk management measures, and accountability mechanisms across hotel operations.
  • Oversee hotel security, emergency preparedness, occupational health and safety, and business continuity measures.
  • Ensure appropriate measures are in place to safeguard hotel assets, guests, employees, and business operations.
  • Coordinate and facilitate internal and external audits, inspections, regulatory reviews, and other compliance assessments.
  • Ensure timely implementation of agreed corrective and preventive actions arising from audits, inspections, or management reviews.

Management, Reporting & Governance

  • Monitor departmental performance against agreed objectives, budgets, service standards, and KPIs.
  • Chair regular hotel management meetings and ensure effective follow-up and implementation of agreed action points.
  • Establish effective communication and coordination mechanisms across departments.
  • Ensure accurate and timely operational, financial, and management reporting.
  • Prepare and submit weekly, monthly, quarterly and yearly hotel performance reports to the Group CEO and/or Board of Directors as required.
  • Provide management with timely information on significant operational, financial, customer, staffing, compliance, and business matters.
  • Ensure proper documentation, accountability, and communication across the hotel.
  • Perform any other duties assigned by the Board of Directors or Group CEO consistent with the nature and seniority of the position.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

Performance shall be assessed based on, but not limited to:

  • Achievement of approved hotel revenue and profitability targets.
  • Room occupancy and Average Daily Rate (ADR) performance.
  • Growth in revenue from accommodation, food and beverage, conferences, events, weddings, and other hotel services.
  • Achievement of agreed departmental and operational performance targets.
  • Guest satisfaction, customer feedback, and resolution of guest complaints.
  •  Improvement and maintenance of hotel service quality and operational standards.
  • Effective cost control and adherence to approved budgets.
  • Timely and effective implementation of approved business and operational plans.
  • Employee productivity, performance, engagement, and retention.
  • Compliance with applicable legal, regulatory, safety, and hotel standards.
  • Effective implementation of internal controls and corrective actions.
  • Growth in corporate, institutional, travel trade, and other strategic business relationships.
  • Successful execution of conferences, weddings, events, and other major hotel functions.
  • Timely submission of accurate operational and management reports.
  • Progress toward the hotel's strategic objectives, including its ambition to achieve 4-Star recognition and maintain a 4+ Star guest experience.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Hospitality Management, Business Administration, Hotel Management, or a related field.
  • Master’s Degree in Business Administration (MBA) or Hospitality Management is an added advantage.
  • Minimum of 7–10 years of progressive experience in hotel or hospitality management.
  • At least 5 years in a senior management or leadership role within the hospitality industry.
  • Strong understanding of hotel operations, financial management, customer service, and business development.
  • Experience managing multi-department hotel operations including accommodation, food & beverage, events, and recreational services.
  • Knowledge of hospitality industry regulations, health & safety standards, and operational best practices.

Key Competencies

  • Strong leadership, people management, and team-building skills.
  • Strategic planning, organizational management, and business growth orientation.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, and conflict-resolution abilities.
  • Strong financial management, budgeting, and operational analysis skills.
  • Good understanding of hotel operations, performance management, revenue optimization, and customer service standards.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, interpersonal, and stakeholder relationship-management skills.
  • High level of professionalism, integrity, accountability, and commitment to quality standards.

jobinrwanda.description:
JOB ADVERTISEMENT

Position: REGISTRATION AND LICENSING OFFICER
Organization: Rwanda National Pharmacy Council (NPC)
Duty Station: Kigali, Rwanda
Employment Type: Permanent, Full-time
Salary: As per the NPC's approved salary structure.
Application Deadline: October 3, 2026, at 5:00 PM (Kigali time)

ABOUT US

The National Pharmacy Council (NPC) is an independent statutory regulatory authority established by Law No. 45/2012 of 14/01/2013, mandated to ensure that the rules, honour and dignity of the pharmacy profession are upheld and that public health is protected. The Council promotes the principles of morality, integrity and dedication essential to pharmacy practice, and ensures that all its members comply with their professional obligations and the laws and regulations governing pharmacy professionals in Rwanda. The vision of the National Pharmacy Council is to become a Centre of Excellence in the regulation and control of the pharmacy profession.

ABOUT THE ROLE

The National Pharmacy Council is seeking to recruit a qualified and experienced Registration and Licensing Officer to be based in the City of Kigali. Under the overall supervision of the Permanent Secretary and Registrar, the Registration and Licensing Officer will support the effective administration and implementation of the Council’s registration, licensing, internship, indexing, pre-registration examination, and related professional regulatory functions. The Officer will ensure that registration and licensing processes are conducted efficiently, accurately, transparently, and in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, policies, standards, and NPC procedures, while providing timely professional support and communication to pharmacy professionals, applicants, training institutions, and other relevant stakeholders.

DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The Registration and licensing officer will be responsible for the following:

  • Review all matters relating to applicants for registration and licensing and determine applicants’ eligibility for registration including establishing the conditions, restrictions and requirements for registration; 
  • Establishing academic standards and the qualifications required for registration as a pharmacy professional in Rwanda; 
  • Coordinate the internship program for pharmacy professionals; 
  • Responsible for the timeous execution of the registration and licensing of pharmacy professionals; 
  • Participate in the development and execution of the NPC action plan and strategic plan; 
  •  Develop policies and requirements with respect to the registration, licensing and reinstating registrants; 
  • Set, administer and maintain policies on all matters related to assessment competencies, standards, principles, selection or design and processes; 
  • Work with technical committee to develop, administer and maintain assessments for the purposes of the registration processes; 
  • Establish protocols for substantial equivalence assessment processes; 
  • Standardize consolidation and timely dissemination of reports and statistics on registration data; 
  • Inform pharmacy professionals and the public about professional obligation and responsibilities of registration and licensing; R
  • Manage the communication related to the indexing, pre-registration exams, internship, registration, licensing and any other communication assigned by his/her supervisors; 
  • Initiation of the day-to-day activities of the Professional operations affairs department of the NPC; 
  • Perform any other duties assigned to her/him either by the Professional operations Manager and/or the Registrar 

QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

Educational Qualifications

  • A Bachelor degree in Pharmacy with at least 3 years of experience.
  • Having the License to practice Pharmacy Profession in Rwanda is a must; 
  • Be in good standing in the pharmacy profession and practice.

Knowledge and Skills

  • organizational skills, both analytical and problem solving, and the ability to work with confidential documents; 
  • The ability to work on multiple projects simultaneously and being able to work under pressure; 
  • Demonstrated leadership, strategic planning, visioning and management abilities; 
  • Demonstrated ability to build and maintain relationships with senior-level colleagues; particularly interacting productively, and comfortably with NPC stakeholders; 
  • Excellent writing skills, communication skills and presentation skills in English are required, along with good French; 
  • Computer literate and a friendly user of most Microsoft Office programs; 
  • Must be able to work independently and solve complex problems using own judgment/discretion; 
  • Must be able to develop/maintain effective partnerships with medical, pharmaceutical and health teaching institutions. 

HOW TO APPLY

Interested and qualified candidates should submit a complete application package comprising:

  • A cover letter addressed to the Chairperson of the National Pharmacy Council
  • A Curriculum Vitae
  • Proof of relevant work experience
  • A notarized copy of the Pharmacy degree
  • A notarized copy of the equivalence certificate of the degree from the higher Education Council (for applicant who studied abroad)
  • A copy of the license to practice pharmacy
  • A copy of the National Identity Card
  • A valid criminal record certificate, to be submitted by the successful candidate prior to issuance of the appointment letter.

APPLICATION SUBMISSION

  • Submission Deadline: October 3, 2026, at 5:00 PM (Kigali time) 
  • Submission Channel: Complete application packages must be submitted in hard copy. 
  • Submission Venue: National Pharmacy Council (NPC) Head Office, KG 632 St, Kimihurura, Rugando, City of Kigali. 
  • Incomplete applications: Incomplete applications will not be considered.
  • Late Applications: Late applications will not be accepted. 
  • Selection Process: Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for an exam.
  • Proposed Examination Date: October 9, 2026, tentatively scheduled and subject to confirmation or change by the Rwanda National Pharmacy Council.

CONTACT FOR MORE INFORMATION

  • Telephone: (+250) 784 614 601 
  • Email:info@pharmacycouncil.rw; rwandanpc@gmail.com

Disclaimer: The National Pharmacy Council does not charge any fee at any stage of the recruitment process.

jobinrwanda.title: Rwanda Driver (Fixed-Term)
jobinrwanda.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.

Responsibilities

Cargo Transport

  • Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.
  • Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.
  • Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).
  • Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.

Vehicle Maintenance

  • Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.
  • Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.
  • Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.
  • Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.
  • Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.

Documentation & Communication

  • Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 
  • Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.
  • Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.
  • Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.
  • Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • Valid category C driver’s licence
  • Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali
  • Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems
  • Working knowledge of electric vehicle mechanics (truck maintenance, interpret truck KM range / battery life)
  • Sound knowledge of road safety regulations
  • Effective communication skills (verbal and written) in Kinyarwanda
  • Punctual and reliable, customer service

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off 

Contract Duration

3 months

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Application Deadline

23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. jobinrwanda.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking an agriculture professional with 1–2 years of Hybrid Maize seed industry experience and a Bachelor's in Agriculture to serve as Seed Quality Control Coordinator. You will oversee quality, SOPs, and compliance for our 4,000 MT processing plant.

Responsibilities

Seed Quality Assurance & SOP Compliance

  • Oversee comprehensive quality assurance, SOP implementation, and regulatory compliance across every stage of the 4,000 MT seed processing plant to meet partner, client, and regulatory standards.

Processing Plant Operations & Technical Guidance

  • Partner closely with the Processing Coordinator to provide technical guidance, conduct continuous quality inspections, and balance operational efficiency with production targets.

People & Team Management

  • Lead and manage plant quality staff and casual workers, driving capacity building and training to ensure strict adherence to SOPs and quality standards.

Stakeholder Management & System Improvement

  • Act as the primary liaison between internal processing teams, external clients, and regulatory bodies while continuously strengthening quality control systems across the seed value chain.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • 1–2 years of experience in the hybrid maize seed industry, seed quality control, or plant operations.
  • Bachelor's degree in Agriculture
  • Proven expertise in seed quality assurance, SOP development, and regulatory compliance
  • Demonstrated technical understanding of 4,000 MT processing plant operations and quality risk mitigation.
  • Strong leadership and people management skills with experience training diverse plant staff and casual workers

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Eastern Province, Gatsibo District, Kabarore, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off 

Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.

Application Deadline

16 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

1. ROLE SUMMARY 

The Legal Officer supports the Head of Legal & Company Secretary in providing sound legal advice, drafting and reviewing corporate documents, and managing legal risks to protect the commercial and regulatory interests of Ecofleet Solutions Ltd. 

2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE 

The role involves supporting corporate governance, contract management, regulatory compliance, and litigation processes. The Legal Officer works closely with internal departments and external counsel, reporting directly to the Head of Legal & Company Secretary.

  • Draft, review, and negotiate commercial contracts, agreements, and MOUs. 
  • Provide legal opinions on labor law, commercial transactions, and intellectual property matters. 
  • Maintain statutory records and ensure timely corporate filings with RDB and relevant authorities. 
  • Coordinate with external counsel on litigation and represent the company in administrative proceedings where required. 
  • Review and update internal policies to ensure legal and regulatory compliance. 
  • Identify and mitigate legal risks across company operations. 

4. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS

Relationship  Nature of Engagement
Head of Legal & Company Secretary Direct reporting line; legal strategy and escalation of key legal matters.

External Counsel  Coordination on litigation and specialised legal matters.
RDB & Regulatory Authorities Corporate filings and regulatory compliance.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS 

  • Legal documents reviewed and returned within 48-72 hours. 
  • Minimisation of legal exposure and successful out-of-court settlements. 
  • 100% compliance with statutory filing deadlines. 

6. CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS

  • Fluent in English and Kinyarwanda; French is an added advantage.

Career Opportunities: Head of Programmes (54963)

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge. We won’t stop until we are all equal.

The Head of Programmes is responsible for leading and providing strategic leadership and operational oversight for designing, implementing and evaluating quality gender transformative programmes and influencing that are consistent with the Country Strategy of Plan International Rwanda and Plan International standards, priorities and principles for advancing children and youth’s rights and equality for girls.

As a staff member of a child-centred international development and humanitarian organisation, the Head of Programmes will commit to complying with Plan International’s standards and policies related to Safeguarding and PSHEA (Preventing Sexual Harassment, Exploitation and Abuse), gender equality, inclusion and diversity. All Plan staff are expected to uphold the organisation's values and behaviours in every aspect of their work.

The Head of Programmes provides strategic leadership and operational oversight for all programmatic aspects of the country office. S/He is responsible for developing and executing programmes aligned with the country office strategy, ensuring high-quality, gender-transformative projects that advance children and youth’s rights, with a focus on girls' equality. S/He works closely with Programme Managers, Project Managers, and Programme Unit Managers to oversee project design, planning, implementation, monitoring, risk and budget management, and project closure, all within the framework of the Country Strategy and Plan International standards of project management and of management standards.

As a strategic member of the Country Management Team, the Head of Programme provides strategic vision on the implementation of the Country strategy but also supports the Country Office through its technical advisers in fundraising, through positioning and supporting the development of strong quality proposals.

S/He also plays a crucial role in integrating safeguarding policies into programmatic work, ensuring that all activities are carried out with the highest standards of safety and protection for children and youth.

By fostering collaboration, driving continuous learning, and influencing positive change, the Head of Programmes plays a pivotal role in shaping impactful, sustainable programmes that transform the lives of children, girls and young people across the country.

To view the Job description click here: Head of Programmes_JD.pdf

Location: Country Office-Kigali

Type of Role: Head of Programmes (For Rwandan National Only) 

Reports to: Country Director

Grade: Level 18

Closing Date: 30/09/2026

Equality, diversity and inclusion is at the very heart of everything that Plan International stands for.

We want Plan International to reflect the diversity of the communities we work with, offering equal opportunities to everyone regardless of age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage and civil partnership, pregnancy and maternity, race, religion or belief, sex or sexual orientation.

Plan International is based on a culture of inclusivity and we strive to create a workplace environment that ensures every team, in every office, in every country, is rich in diverse people, thoughts, and ideas.

We foster an organisational culture that embraces our commitment to racial justice, gender equality, girls’ rights and inclusion.

Plan International believes that in a world where children face so many threats of harm, it is our duty to ensure that we, as an organisation, do everything we can to keep children safe. This means that we have particular responsibilities to children that we come into contact with and we must not contribute in any way to harming or placing children at risk.

A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with Plan International's Safeguarding Children and Young People policy. Plan International also participates in the Inter Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. In line with this scheme we will request information from applicants previous employers about any findings of sexual exploitation, sexual abuse and/or sexual harassment during employment, or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By submitting an application, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Please note that Plan International will never send unsolicited emails requesting payment from candidates.

jobinrwanda.description:
FINANCE LEAD JD

COMPANY INTRODUCTION

Wicloudrwd is a global digital transformation and IT outsourcing company established in 2022, with operations across multiple international locations. The company provides technology and IT outsourcing solutions tailored to Microsoft environments, with expertise across Microsoft Dynamics 365, Microsoft Azure, Microsoft Windows Commercial, and Microsoft Office 365.

Location: Kigali, Rwanda
Employment Type: Full-time
Working Hours: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–6:00 PM

About the Role

We are seeking a hands-on Finance Lead to independently manage the Company's routine accounting, tax compliance, payroll, project costing, and local finance administration.

The Finance Lead will work closely with the Kigali team and HQ Finance & Operations functions to ensure accurate financial reporting, strong financial controls, and compliance with applicable Rwanda requirements.

The successful candidate must be able to independently perform core finance activities and possess a sound academic and professional understanding of more complex financial and tax concepts.

Key Responsibilities

1. Accounting & Financial Reporting

  • Independently manage full-cycle accounting, including:
    • Journal entries.
    • Accounts payable and receivable.
    • Accruals and bank reconciliations.
    • Fixed asset records and depreciation.
  • Manage month-end closing and preparation of monthly financial reports.
  • Maintain accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare schedules and information for management, audit, and statutory purposes.

2. Tax, Invoice & Payroll Compliance

  • Independently manage routine Rwanda finance and compliance matters, including:
    • VAT, PAYE, withholding tax, and other applicable statutory obligations.
    • Invoice and supporting document compliance.
    • Payroll records, statutory deductions, and employer contributions.
    • Tax filing deadlines, supporting documentation, and statutory records.
  • Coordinate with the Rwanda Revenue Authority, auditors, and external tax advisors.
  • Review the accounting and basic tax treatment of revenue and expense transactions and identify potential tax benefits or exposures.

3. Project Costing & Financial Control

  • Maintain project and cost center records.
  • Track and allocate direct and indirect costs.
  • Prepare project costing, profitability analysis, and budget-versus-actual reporting.
  • Support cash-flow forecasting and management reporting.
  • Identify financial control or compliance issues and report them to management or relevant HQ functions.

4. Financial Administration & External Coordination

  • Prepare payment documentation and maintain finance records in accordance with company policies.
  • Support the implementation of finance SOPs and internal controls.
  • Act as the primary local finance contact for banks, auditors, accounting firms, and tax advisors.
  • Coordinate with external advisors on tax, accounting, and regulatory matters and follow up on agreed actions.
  • Prepare information and supporting documents requested by HQ or external advisors.

5. Finance & Tax Knowledge

The candidate should have a sound understanding of finance and tax principles and be able to recognize relevant issues, understand their potential implications, and escalate matters where necessary.

Knowledge should include:

  • Cross-border transactions and foreign exchange.
  • Profit repatriation and related financial considerations.
  • Transfer pricing and related-party transactions.
  • Intercompany arrangements and cost allocation.
  • Relevant tax, foreign exchange, and documentation requirements.

Qualifications & Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a closely related discipline.
  • Minimum 3 years of relevant accounting or finance experience.
  • Demonstrated experience in full-cycle accounting, month-end closing, and financial reporting.
  • Practical experience with Rwanda tax compliance, payroll, and statutory reporting.
  • Experience in project costing, cost allocation, or profitability analysis.
  • Proficiency in accounting software or ERP systems and Microsoft 365, particularly Excel.
  • Strong written and spoken English.
  • Ability to work independently and manage routine finance operations in a start-up environment.
  • Partial completion of ACCA, CPA, or another recognized professional accounting qualification is an advantage.
  • Experience in IT, technology, outsourcing, or professional services is an advantage
  • Local Language: Fluent in reading, writing, and speaking.
  • English: Strong professional proficiency in written and spoken English.

Application Process

Interested and qualified candidates can send their CV to Francis@itechwx.com in the format 'Role+Application+ their name'.

Reporting To: Finance and Admin Officer Years of Experience 2+ Years
Location: Kigali Travel Required: 30%
Job description

About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact. 

To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

Position Purpose is to Support the Finance Team to ensure accurate bookkeeping, budget formulation, financial analysis, monitoring, reporting and accounting/budget execution across assigned field districts. Provide financial advisory support to field officers and help maintain strong financial controls and compliance.

Key Responsibilities

  • Maintain and file all financial documents (cash advances, requests, receipts) to ensure records are audit-ready and readily available.
  • Update finance systems with timely and accurate financial data; participate in monthly Sage project reconciliations.
  • Support budgeting, budget tracking and implementation of financial policies; act as finance business partner to assigned field offices.
  • Reconcile staff advances, petty cash and project-specific accounts (monthly) and manage weekly staff advance activity.
  • Post journal entries (JE), manage fuel accountability and government official payment records.
  • Receive, log and verify invoices before entry; process invoices via the procurement module and follow up on vendor disputes.
  • Review and reconcile project activity accountability; investigate and resolve discrepancies.
  • Oversee individual accounts for assigned field officers and follow up on outstanding accountability.
  • Review mobile-money transactions for compliance; initiate payments via Beyonic, verifying beneficiaries, and flagging variances.
  • Report any non-compliant financial practices to the Senior Finance Officer or Senior Finance & Admin Manager.
  • Recommend improvements to increase accuracy, efficiency and cost savings; provide financial guidance to staff to ensure adherence to procedures.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor's degree in accounting, Accounting & Finance, Business Administration (Accounting) or equivalent.
  • Minimum 2 years’ professional experience in accounting, bookkeeping, finance management or audit.
  • Practical experience with mobile money payment solutions is essential.
  • Familiarity with accounting software (Sage or similar) is an advantage.
  • CPA/ACCA partial or full qualification is an advantage.

Technical & Personal Skills

  • Strong numerical, analytical, and Excel skills.
  • Knowledge of accounting standards, financial regulations, and data privacy principles.
  • High integrity, discretion, and ability to manage confidential information.
  • Good time management and attention to detail.
  • Critical thinking and business service orientation.
  • Willingness to travel up to 30% to field districts.

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace. Disclaimer: Raising the Village DOES NOT charge any kind of FEE(s) at whichever stage of the recruitment process.

jobinrwanda.description:
JOB VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

Location: Nyagatare District, Rwanda

1.About GAH Ltd

Gabiro Agribusiness Hub Ltd (GAH Ltd) is a flagship agribusiness initiative established through a partnership between the Government of Rwanda and NETAFIM Ltd, a global leader in precision irrigation solutions. Located in Nyagatare District, GAH Ltd is at the forefront of transforming Rwanda’s agricultural sector through large-scale irrigated farming, modern agribusiness infrastructure, and climate-smart agriculture. The Hub is designed to drive modern, irrigated agriculture, enhance productivity, and attract commercial farming investment.

The Hub was established to drive agricultural commercialization, enhance food security, promote technology-driven farming, and attract private sector investment into high-value agriculture. Through its integrated irrigation infrastructure and modern farming ecosystem, GAH Ltd aims to position Rwanda as a regional model for sustainable and productive agribusiness development. 

2. About the Position

Job Title: Legal Officer 

Reporting to: CEO

Contract Terms: Open Ended

As the organization continues to scale its operations, we are seeking to recruit a competent candidate to fill the position of Legal Officer, who will be responsible for overseeing and managing the legal aspects of the company's operations. This role requires a deep understanding of corporate law, contract management, and regulatory compliance. The ideal candidate will possess strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and the ability to provide sound legal advice and guidance to the management team.

3. Duties & Responsibilities

  • Provide legal guidance and support to the management team on a wide range of legal issues, including but not limited to contracts, corporate governance, compliance, and regulatory matters.
  • Review, draft, and participate in negotiation of various contracts, agreements, and legal documents to ensure they adhere to the company's policies and comply with relevant laws and regulations.
  • Conduct legal research and analysis to stay updated on changes in laws and regulations that may affect the company's operations, and make recommendations to ensure compliance.
  • Collaborate with different departments to develop and/or update existing internal policies and procedures to mitigate legal risks and ensure the company's operations align with legal standards and best practices.
  • Collaborate with external legal counsel, as necessary, to handle complex legal matters and represent the company's interests in legal proceedings or negotiations.
  • Assist in the resolution of legal disputes and litigation, including managing external legal resources and representing the company in negotiations, mediations, and arbitrations.
  • Work closely with other departments, such as finance, human resources, and operations, to ensure legal compliance in all aspects of the business.
  • Conduct legal due diligence for potential business transactions, partnerships, and acquisitions to assess and mitigate legal risks.
  • Prepare and deliver training sessions and workshops to educate employees on legal matters, policies, and compliance requirements.
  • Keep accurate and up-to-date records of all legal documents, contracts, and correspondences.

4. Required Qualifications

The ideal candidate should possess:

  • Bachelor's degree in law (LLB)) from an accredited institution.
  • Minimum of 4 years of experience working as a legal officer or in a similar legal role, preferably in the agricultural or agribusiness sector.
  • In-depth knowledge of corporate law, contract law, and regulatory compliance.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to provide strategic legal advice and solutions.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate complex legal issues clearly and effectively.
  • Proven track record of managing legal contracts and negotiations effectively.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a team environment.
  • Strong attention to detail and the ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks simultaneously.
  • Familiarity with relevant software and tools for legal research and document management.

5. Key competencies

The successful candidate should demonstrate the following competencies:

  • Legal Risk Management: Ability to identify, assess, and proactively mitigate legal risks arising from the company’s operations, transactions, contracts, and business relationships.
  • Strategic Legal Advisory: Ability to translate complex legal requirements into practical, commercially sound recommendations that support management decision-making and the company’s strategic objectives.
  • Contract Negotiation and Management: Strong ability to develop and negotiate agreements while protecting the company’s interests, maintaining balanced commercial relationships, and ensuring effective contract implementation.
  • Corporate Governance: Sound understanding of good governance principles, board and management.

6. How to apply 

Interested candidates should submit the following documents compiled into a single PDF file:

  • Application letter addressed to the Chief Executive Officer of GAH Ltd
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV) with three referees and their contact details
  • Copy of the relevant academic degree and professional certificates
  • Copy of National ID
  • Proof of required work experience

Applications should be sent to: recruitment@gah.rw

Deadline for submission:Monday, 05th October, 2026 at 5 pm.

Done on 14 September 2026
 

NGARAMBE Aloysius
Chief Executive Officer
Gabiro Agribusness Hub Ltd

CHAI RWANDA

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT

Title: Associate, Data Scientist 

Program: Health Systems Strengthening

Job Location: Kigali, Rwanda

Type: Full-Time Paid

Start date: Immediate

Overview

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.

CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.

At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.

Programs Overview

The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, putting an emphasis on primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system.

CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to support the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health center level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services, and to support improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care.

Position overview 

CHAI currently seeks an Associate Data Scientist to work with the Ministry of Health (MOH), reporting directly to the head of data science at the National Health Intelligence Center to help improve the quality, governance, and use of evidence on policy decision making. S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI supported initiatives.

The Associate Data Scientist is responsible for leading advanced data analytics, statistical modeling, and applied machine learning across priority public health and clinical domains. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigor, reproducibility, and national-scale usability.

This is a top government priority for MOH, and the Associate, Data Scientist will therefore be seconded to the MOH/NHIC, S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI-supported initiatives.

Job responsibilities: 

The key functions and deliverables of this role will include:

Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Modeling 

  • Lead advanced descriptive, predictive, and inferential analyses across clinical, surveillance, and health systems datasets.
  • Develop and validate predictive models, risk stratification algorithms, forecasting models, epidemiological and operational analytics
  • Apply rigorous statistical methods, hypothesis testing, and causal inference techniques to support decision-making.
  • Ensure all analytics are clinically interpretable, policy-relevant, and scientifically defensible. 

Feature Engineering & Machine Learning Support

  • Design robust feature engineering pipelines from EMRs, HMIS, LMIS and surveillance platforms
  • Support AI Engineers with high-quality training datasets, feature selection, bias detection and data representativeness testing
  • Contribute to development of machine learning models, particularly in tabular health data, time-series forecasting and population-level risk prediction.

Data Quality, Governance and Integrity

  • Lead implementation of data quality frameworks, completeness, consistency, accuracy and timeliness checks
  • Perform data audits, outlier detection, bias and missing data analysis
  • Ensure compliance with national health data governance standards, privacy and ethical data use policies. 
  • Maintain full data documentation, metadata standards, and lineage tracking. 

Health Systems Intelligence & Decision Support

  • Develop decision-support analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking,

resource allocation and service delivery optimization. 

  • Translate analytical outputs into policy briefs, executive dashboards, technical report. 
  • Ensure outputs are actionable, explainable, and aligned with the national health priorities.

Data Engineering Support and Pipeline optimization

  • Work closely with Data engineers, integration teams and AI engineers to ensure analytics assets are scalable, reproducible and production ready. 
  • Support data pipeline optimization, ETL quality validation and real-time and batch processing readiness 

Mentorship, Capacity Building & Collaboration

  • Mentor junior data scientists and analysts
  • Lead internal analytics communities of practice, code reviews and methodology workshops
  • Serve as a technical reviewer for analytics protocols, research designs and data science deliverables

Innovation and Continuous Improvement

  • Stay current with advances in Machine Learning, Statistical Science, Health Analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Causal Inference trends
  • Propose innovative analytics and data science use cases for public health, service delivery, health financing, supply chain and logistics for pharmaceuticals and disease surveillance

Required Qualifications 

  • MSc degree in relevant discipline (Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Operations Research, Statistics, Epidemiology, Health Informatics)
  • 5-8 years of professional experience in the field of advanced analytics and/or applied statistics preferably with Data Science applications
  • Solid mathematical foundation and knowledge of a variety of statistical methods (e.g. regression, classification, clustering, experimental design, modeling, advanced forecasting) 
  • Proven experience working with large-scale datasets, regulated data environments, preferably within a health domain. 
  • Strong proficiency in data visualization, demonstrated experience in Python, R, SQL, and working with structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets
  • Ability to focus on vaguely defined problems requiring the application of a creative approach. 
  • Strong teamworking skills 
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across teams. 
  • Ability to mentor and lead teams in a fast-paced and changing environment. 

Application procedure 

Interested candidates should email a letter of interest (maximum 1 page) outlining how their background meets the requirements outlined above; CV (maximum 3 pages); and the names of three references through chairwandarecruiting@clintonhealthaccess.org with " Associate, Data Scientist " in the subject line. The deadline for applications is October 09, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

In compliance with the data protection law of Rwanda and by submitting your application and CV, you explicitly consent to the collection, processing, and storage of your personal data by Clinton Health Access Initiative for the sole purpose of managing and conducting the recruitment process for the position for which you have applied.

jobinrwanda.title: Customer Service Agent
jobinrwanda.description:
Job Title: Customer Service Agent

Department: Communications

Location: AC Mobility Offices, Kigali - Rwanda

Modality: Full-Time 

Contract Duration: One Year 

Contract Type: Fixed Term

Reporting Structure:

  • Direct Supervisor/Reports To: Head of Communications 
  • Works Closely With: Solutions Support Associate 

Role Overview

As the Customer Service Agent, you are responsible for providing timely, professional, and empathetic frontline assistance to AC Mobility customers across all customer-care touchpoints. The role serves as a primary point of contact for commuter enquiries, complaints, and service requests, ensuring accurate information is provided, resolving standard issues at the first point of contact, and properly documenting and escalating complex cases requiring technical or operational investigation.

Core Responsibility

To provide customers with a reliable, reassuring, and positive support experience by understanding their needs, delivering accurate information, achieving high first-contact resolution on routine enquiries, and ensuring unresolved issues are documented and routed efficiently through established escalation pathways.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Frontline Customer Support: Receive, handle, and resolve incoming customer enquiries and complaints professionally, courteously, and empathetically. 
  2. Customer Information Delivery: Provide clear, precise, and up-to-date guidance regarding AC Mobility products, Tap&Go fare structures, card usage, and service procedures. 
  3. First Contact Resolution (FCR): Resolve routine, frequently occurring customer enquiries (such as balance queries, basic card issues, and system guidance) during the initial interaction.
  4. Complaint Handling and De-escalation: Actively listen to customer grievances, defuse tense interactions with composure, and provide appropriate assistance while upholding professional standards. 
  5. Follow-up and Communication: Contact commuters to provide progress updates, request additional information, or confirm the successful resolution of reported issues. 
  6. CRM and Case Management: Accurately record, categorise, and manage all customer interactions, service requests, and feedback within the company’s CRM and ticketing systems. 
  7. Tier-2 Escalation: Accurately document and escalate technical faults, transactional discrepancies, or operational challenges to the Solutions Support Associate in line with standard operating procedures. 
  8. Customer Feedback Logging: Systematically identify and flag recurring commuter pain points, agent network issues, or validator failure patterns to supervisory and technical teams. 
  9. Data Security and Confidentiality: Maintain absolute discretion and protect sensitive commuter identity, card data, and transaction histories in strict adherence to data protection standards. 
  10. Continuous Learning and Compliance: Maintain a thorough understanding of AC Mobility platforms, updates, workflows, and assigned shift rotas. 

Working Relationship with the Solutions Support Associate

  • The Customer Service Agent provides Tier-1 frontline support, handling initial commuter engagements and resolving routine queries using documented procedures. 

  • Where an issue requires technical diagnosis, backend transaction verification, or cross-departmental coordination, the Agent documents the case and formally escalates it to the Solutions Support Associate. 

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • First Contact Resolution (FCR): Achieve ≥80% resolution rate on standard enquiries during the first interaction. 
  • Response and Resolution Timelines: Adhere strictly to agreed customer response and ticket resolution times across all live support channels. 
  • Customer Satisfaction (CSAT): Maintain a positive customer satisfaction rating of ≥85% based on post-interaction feedback. 
  • CRM Record Accuracy: 100% of customer interactions accurately tagged, documented, and categorised with zero critical omissions. 
  • Escalation Accuracy: Zero critical misroutings of technical or operational tickets escalated to the Solutions Support Associate. 
  • Schedule Adherence: High punctuality and compliance with allocated shift rotas and operational breaks. 

Performance Evaluation and Terms

Performance in this role will be continuously evaluated to ensure against customer care benchmarks, response accuracy, and adherence to operational standards. 

Ramifications of Underperformance:

Expectations for this role are high, reflecting its importance to the organisation's overall success. A sustained failure to achieve Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), fulfil core responsibilities, or uphold AC Mobility’s standards of professional conduct will trigger a formal Performance Improvement Plan (PIP). Inability to demonstrate the required improvement within the stipulated timeframe may result in the termination of employment.

Qualifications and Core Competencies

1. Educational Background

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Customer Care, Communications, Public Relations, Business Administration, or a related field. 

2. Professional Experience

  • Prior customer-facing or call centre experience within technology, telecommunications, financial services, or transport environments is an added advantage.

3. Language Proficiency

  • Fluency in Kinyarwanda and English is required; working knowledge of French is an added advantage.

4. Professional Certifications

Preferred: 

  • Certified Customer Service Professional (CCSP) or Customer Service Excellence Certification (CSEC): Demonstrates mastery of foundational service principles, complaint resolution, and front-facing relationship management.
  • Help Desk Institute (HDI) Support Center Analyst: Validates best-practice competencies in multi-channel ticket logging, service desk workflows, and issue escalation.
  • ITIL Foundation (v4): Recommended for agents operating alongside technical teams to understand incident ticketing, service level agreements (SLAs), and change escalation procedures.
  • CRM Platform Certifications: Practical product badges or credentials in industry-standard ticketing and CRM suites (such as Zendesk, HubSpot Service Hub, or Salesforce Service Cloud).

5. Additional Hard Competencies

  • CRM and Ticketing Systems: Competence in logging, categorising, and tracking tickets within enterprise CRM or customer support software. 
  • Digital Literacy: Comfort working across multiple web applications, digital mobility tools, and office productivity platforms with high typing speed and accuracy. 
  • Product Literacy: Comprehensive understanding of cashless payment flows, bus ticketing workflows, and Tap&Go operational rules.

Soft Competencies

  • Command of key competencies needed for the modern workplace, including but not limited to: Strategic Leadership, High-Level Problem Solving, Critical Thinking, Uncompromising Integrity, Excellent Cross-Functional Communication, Work Ethic, Dependability, Empathy, Professionalism, and effective Stress Management in high-stakes environments. 

In addition:

  • Customer-Centric Communication: Active listening and clear, professional verbal and written expression across diverse commuter demographics.
  • Emotional Resilience and De-escalation: Proven ability to remain calm, patient, and polite when managing difficult situations or high-volume peak periods.
  • Attention to Detail and Accuracy: Rigour in recording accurate ticket details, capturing caller data, and relaying factual procedural information.
  • Dependability and Process Discipline: Strict adherence to shift rosters, attendance guidelines, SOPs, and tiered escalation matrices.
  • Ethical Conduct and Discretion: Absolute integrity and responsible handling of private commuter and transaction records.

What We Offer

AC Mobility offers a vibrant, purpose-driven workplace at the forefront of East Africa’s cashless transit revolution. As a Customer Service Agent, you will join a supportive, collaborative Communications and Customer Care team dedicated to delivering world-class service to millions of daily commuters. We offer competitive compensation packages, comprehensive health insurance coverage, structured shift patterns, continuous professional coaching in modern CRM platforms and conflict de-escalation, and clear internal career progression pathways into technical support, operations, or supervisory roles within the organisation.

Application Instructions

Interested candidates who meet the above requirements are invited to submit their applications through the AC Mobility recruitment portal using the link below:

Application link: https://acm-odoogit-odooerp.odoo.com/jobs/customer-service-agent-52

Application deadline: 10 October 2026

Operating since 2015, they enhance urban mobility in Rwanda through digital payments, fleet management, and IoT services for public transport.

jobinrwanda.title: Pediatric Surgery Faculty
jobinrwanda.description:
Position: Pediatric Surgery Faculty

Job Title: Faculty, Pediatric Surgery

Reports to: Head, Department of Surgery

Group/Department: Department of Surgery / Division of Clinical Medicine, University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)

Location: Primarily Butaro Campus and Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, with frequent travel to Kigali and other teaching sites in Rwanda

Position Overview

The Faculty of Pediatric Surgery will play a key role in advancing UGHE’s mission to deliver equitable, high-quality medical education and surgical care for children. The faculty member will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, clinical pediatric surgical service delivery, research, and global surgery initiatives focused on children’s surgical care.

The Pediatric Surgery faculty member will actively participate in clinical teaching at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital and affiliated training sites, contribute to curriculum development in pediatric surgery, mentor students and trainees, and support the implementation of the General Surgery Residency Program aligned with COSECSA standards, including strengthening pediatric surgical training exposure.

The ideal candidate is highly self-motivated, academically productive, and committed to surgical education, research, and strengthening pediatric surgical capacity in resource-limited settings. The individual must be organized, collaborative, adaptable, and passionate about improving access to safe, timely, and affordable surgical care for children.

Responsibilities

Undergraduate Medical Education

  • Contribute to curriculum, syllabus, and content development in pediatric surgery across the MBBS/MGHD curriculum.
  • Deliver lectures, small group sessions, simulation-based teaching, and bedside clinical instruction.
  • Provide clinical supervision to medical students during surgery clerkships, with emphasis on pediatric surgical conditions.
  • Participate in student assessment (OSCEs, written exams, workplace-based assessments).
  • Supervise and mentor undergraduate research projects.
  • Coordinate pediatric surgery teaching activities with visiting and adjunct faculty.
  • Collaborate with affiliated hospitals to ensure effective delivery of pediatric surgical education.
  • Ensure quality and consistency of clinical teaching across all rotation sites.
  • Provide leadership for pediatric surgery modules or thematic blocks as assigned.
  • Participate in direct patient care as part of clinical teaching responsibilities.

Postgraduate and Residency Education

  • Contribute to implementation of competency-based training aligned with COSECSA standards.
  • Ensure quality supervision of residents rotating through pediatric surgery.
  • Provide structured clinical supervision in neonatal and pediatric surgical care.
  • Participate in WBAs, logbook reviews, case discussions, and operative competency assessments.
  • Contribute to exam preparation for COSECSA membership and fellowship examinations.
  • Mentor residents in clinical practice, research, leadership, and professionalism.
  • Participate in M&M conferences, journal clubs, and academic rounds.
  • Support development of simulation-based training for pediatric surgical procedures.
  • Contribute to accreditation and quality assurance processes.
  • Support development of pediatric surgery training pathways within UGHE programs.

Clinical Service Delivery

  • Support and scale-up of comprehensive pediatric surgical services at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, including:

  • Pediatric general surgery and emergency care
  • Pediatric Oncologic Surgery
  • Strengthen systems for perioperative care of children, including anesthesia, critical care, and nutrition.
  • Develop and implement clinical protocols, safety standards, and quality improvement initiatives.
  • Support multidisciplinary care involving pediatrics, anesthesia, nursing, and allied health professionals.
  • Strengthen referral systems and district-level capacity for pediatric surgical care.
  • Participate in on-call coverage and emergency pediatric surgical services.

Research and Scholarship

  • Initiate and support research in pediatric surgery, neonatal surgery, and global children’s surgery.
  • Develop grant proposals, research publications, and technical reports.
  • Mentor students and residents in research activities.
  • Conduct implementation and operational research focused on improving access to pediatric surgical care in Rwanda and similar settings.

Center for Equity in Global Surgery (CEGS) Activities

  • Participate in CEGS academic and administrative activities.
  • Contribute to global surgery conferences, seminars, and collaborations.
  • Build partnerships with national and international pediatric surgery programs.
  • Support grant writing and resource mobilization.
  • Advocate for equitable access to surgical care for children.

Institutional Service and Leadership

  • Serve on UGHE committees as assigned.
  • Contribute to departmental strategy and academic program development.
  • Engage in community outreach and child health advocacy initiatives.
  • Promote interprofessional education and collaboration.
  • Perform other duties as assigned by UGHE leadership.

Qualifications and Skills

Mandatory

  • Medical degree (MD, MBBS, or equivalent) from a recognized institution.
  • Postgraduate qualification in Pediatric Surgery (Fellowship, MMed, or equivalent recognized specialist qualification).
  • Board certification or equivalent specialist recognition in Pediatric Surgery.
  • Eligible for medical licensure/registration in Rwanda.
  • Demonstrated clinical expertise in pediatric surgical care, including neonatal surgery.
  • Experience in teaching undergraduate and postgraduate trainees.
  • Demonstrated research experience.
  • Commitment to academic medicine and mentorship.
  • Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills in multidisciplinary settings.
  • Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Preferred

  • MSc in Public Health, Global Health, or Medical Education.
  • Experience in health systems strengthening and surgical capacity building in low-resource settings.
  • Experience working in academic medical centers.
  • Expertise in research methods and implementation science.
  • Experience in competency-based medical education.
  • Grant writing experience and peer-reviewed publications.
  • Familiarity with COSECSA or similar regional training frameworks.

How to Apply

Applicants should provide: (1) curriculum vitae, (2) Degree, (3) A cover letter describing your interest in UGHE and relevant experience. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page.

University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Organizational Profile

UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system.

UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima—PIH’s sister organization—and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade.

Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team.

At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including community members – as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy.

Description

Department/Unit: IGHER-Biobank

Reports To: Biobank Program

Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites

Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension

Position SummaryThe Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain is responsible for maintaining accurate biobank information systems, managing specimen inventory records, monitoring storage conditions, and ensuring uninterrupted cold chain operations.The position ensures sample traceability, data integrity, specimen security, and compliance throughout the biobank lifecycle.   • Data management, quality assurance, Excel/database systems, cold-chain monitoring, and research documentation.

jobinrwanda.description:
Position Title: Biobank Technician I

Department/Unit: IGHER - Biobank Program

Reports To: Biobank Head

Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites and sample collection locations

Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension

Position Summary

The Biobank Technician I – Sample Processing is responsible for supporting the collection, receipt, processing, aliquoting, labeling, storage preparation, and quality control of biological specimens collected from clinical trials, population-based research studies, and other biomedical research projects.The position ensures that all biological samples are handled, processed, and stored according to approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), biosafety requirements, and biobank quality standards.The Biobank Technician I works closely with Clinical Research Coordinators, Principal Investigators, laboratory personnel, data management teams, and research partners to ensure specimen integrity, traceability, and compliance throughout the research lifecycle.

  • Maintain biosafety, GCLP/GCP, confidentiality, and laboratory safety standards.
  • Monitor laboratory supplies and report equipment or operational issues.
  • Collaborate with clinical, laboratory, data management, and research teams to support clinical trials and research projects.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical/Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biotechnology, Biology, Biochemistry, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field.

Experience

  • Minimum 2 years of laboratory experience, preferably involving human biological specimens in research, clinical trials, hospitals, or diagnostic laboratories.
