jobinrwanda.description:
Description

Position Title: Biobank Head

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda

Contract Duration: Two (2) years, renewable based on performance

Position Summary

The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is responsible for leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to support clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research.

The Head is responsible for the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel.

Reporting to the Clinical research lead/Director of IGHER, the Biobank Head works closely with the Head of the UGHE-AVEGA Clinical Trial Unit to ensure seamless integration of biobanking services into all clinical trials and research activities conducted through UGHE. The position also collaborates closely with the Biobank Project Consultant (External Scientific Consultant) to establish the biobank according to international standards, develop governance structures, implement quality systems, strengthen institutional capacity, and position UGHE as a national and regional centre of excellence in biobanking.

The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities.
  • Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices.
  • Lead implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management.
  • Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations.
  • Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and develop national and international collaborations.
  • Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management.

Qualifications

Education

PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Certification in GCLP, GCP, ISO 20387, ISO 15189, ISBER Best Practices, or QMS/Laboratory Management is a plus.

Experience

  • 8+ years in biobank management, biomedical research, clinical laboratory management, or clinical trial support, including 5+ years in senior leadership supervising multidisciplinary teams
  • Proven track record establishing or expanding a biobank/biospecimen repository — infrastructure planning, workflow development, and operations
  • Experience implementing LIMS and laboratory/biobank Quality Management Systems
  • Hands-on management of biospecimen collection, processing, cryopreservation, storage, and distribution
  • Equipment lifecycle management (procurement through calibration/maintenance)
  • Experience managing donor-funded programs, budgets, and strategic/donor reporting
  • Developed SOPs, quality manuals, and governance structures (Oversight/Scientific Advisory/Data Access Committees)
  • Prepared labs for ISO 20387, ISO 15189, or ISBER accreditation; built CAPA and audit systems
  • Prepared IRB/ethics/regulatory documentation; ensured compliance with biospecimen collection, storage, and export regulations
  • Developed informed consent, data privacy, and biobank governance frameworks
  • Supported regulatory inspections and audits
  • Strong command of ISBER, ISO 20387/15189, GCLP/GCP, LIMS, and biosafety/QMS standards. Excellent leadership, project and financial management, and scientific writing/communication skills.
  • Experience establishing a national/regional biobank; integrating biobanking into clinical trials; working with international institutions or in LMIC/Africa settings; PMP/PRINCE2 certification; strong publication and grant-management record.

To apply 

Applicants should provide: (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) graduate transcripts, (3) examples of relevant teaching experience or course materials, where available, and (4) a personal statement describing their teaching approach and experience working with diverse student populations. Applicants may also include an example of relevant scholarly work. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page.

University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

Organizational Profile 

UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system. 

UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima-PIH’s sister organization and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade. 

Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team. 

Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Sexual Harassment: 

At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including community members – as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy.

UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.

Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)

Location: Kigali with regular travel to research sites

jobinrwanda.description:
Job Title: Project Assistant (3 Vacancies)

Department/Group: Implementation

Reporting To: Project Officer Years of Experience 2+ Years

Location: Rutsiro (2) and Nyamasheke (1)

Travel Required: 90%

Job description

About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.

To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

Role and Responsibilities

Project Implementation

  • Conduct project design review meetings with respective partner villages and provide feedback as required to update project designs and budgets prior to implementation;
  • Coordinate training activities including but not limited to financial literacy and behavior and mindset change, water and health sanitation, village savings and loans associations, agriculture, livestock care and management, etc.
  • Responsible to implement RTV’s project methodologies with the purpose of increasing household income and reducing extreme poverty as per project designs;
  • Develop and submit list of required goods and services for project implementation to the procurement and logistics officer;
  • Responsible to verify goods/inputs prior to distribution;
  • Conduct project follow-up and provide support and guidance to community groups and individual households to ensure project compliance continuation.
  • Identify potential risks and issues and provide mitigation measures and recommendations for improvements;
  • Conduct regular meetings with leadership and community members on performance, participation, and perceptions of RTV based projects.

Government & Community Coordination and Support

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with Cell-level government officials (SEDOs and Executive Secretaries) to support day-to-day RTV program activities.
  • Work closely with community leadership and support structures including Inteko z’abaturage, Incuti z’umuryango, Abajyanama b’Ubuzima, Abajyanama b’Ubuhinzi (farmer promoters), para-social workers, community coaches, technical and village coaches, and other community actors to ensure their active participation in RTV programs.
  • Mobilize households and communities for trainings, meetings, and program activities to promote clear understanding, strong participation, and adoption of RTV program components.
  • Assist in delivering trainings to community and cell-level actors on RTV program methodology, M&E processes, technology use, and field protocols, under the guidance of the Project Officer or Project Manager.
  • Provide on-the-job support and follow-up to community and government actors during implementation to help address challenges and encourage consistent participation.
  • Promote positive collaboration and trust between RTV staff, government officials, and community structures to strengthen community ownership and contribute to sustainable program impact.

Reporting and Administration

Develop and manage work plans;

  • Complete field reporting on a weekly basis and provide support with information sharing for donor reporting and proposal writing as might be required;
  • Attend and participate in weekly staff meetings as well as cluster team meetings to highlight issues and success and outline next steps;
  • Complete weekly financial request, submissions and accountabilities to the Project Officer;
  • Take photographs and share them for data repository.

Monitoring and Evaluation:

  • Support field monitoring activities such as attendance tracking, basic data collection, household follow-ups, and reporting using RTV tools and systems.
  • Providing feedback and recommendations to the Project Officer and Project Manager, and the program team to improve RTV’s way of work;
  • Provide suggestions to management on potential activities that need to be redone, reviewed or introduced to ensure sustainability of RTV projects, methodologies, and improvement in the lives of community members.

Note: Other requirements might be required by their direct supervisor and/or management.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, Social Work, Humanities, Community Development, or related field of study
  • Bachelor’s degree in agriculture is preferred but not required
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant work experience at the village level
  • Demonstrated experience working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at Sector and Cell levels (mandatory)

Preferred Skills if any

Strong training & facilitation skills;

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English;
  • Fluent in local languages where RTV works;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs i.e. Word and Excel
  • Understanding of Community Based Development Principles
  • Organizes work effectively while remaining aware of changing priorities and deadlines;
  • Able to work independently to accomplish tasks, but also as part of a team to achieve mutual goals and objectives;
  • Able to think outside of the box to provide plausible solutions to issues and challenges;
  • Strong work ethic, flexible, and able to build relationships with various stakeholders most notably colleagues, and community members;
  • Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;
  • Energetic and physically able to hike high to hike high terrain;
  • Able to travel approximately 90% of time;
  • Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit (class A) and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory).

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace.

Job description

 

About Raising The Village

Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

 

Position Summary

The Project Manager plays a critical role in overseeing the successful implementation of multiple projects within a district, ensuring alignment with RTV’s strategic goals, project designs, and work plans. This role involves providing strong leadership, mentorship, and operational support to Team Leads and Officers, ensuring they have the necessary resources, guidance, and capacity to execute projects effectively.
In addition to people and team management, the Project Manager is responsible for office administration and operations, fostering an environment where teams are fully supported to meet program objectives. They serve as the key liaison between staff, government counterparts and management, proactively addressing challenges, streamlining processes, and ensuring smooth communication and workflow across all levels.
The ideal candidate is a results-oriented leader with strong experience in coaching and managing teams, mobilizing and coordinating with government institutions, and delivering complex, multi-sector projects in rural contexts. They are solutions-driven, highly organized, and committed to building high-performing teams that deliver sustainable, government-aligned impact for communities served by RTV. Note: The Project Manager may be based at a District Government Office and embedded with government teams to foster collaboration and strengthen partnerships.

 

Role and ResponsibilitiesProject Management

  • Reports to the Area Manager, providing key updates and where needed arises escalates issues to the Area Manager for Support or decision guidance.
  • Coordinates weekly plans of activities and key deliverables to Team Leads every Friday for the coming week
  • Debrief with Team Leads and Officers on project progress in the communities (covering deliverables, key issues and risks, key activities in villages)
  • Identify key issues and risks for projects during project reporting.
  • Oversee the timely and effective execution of day-to-day activity, work plans, and project life cycles, starting from project identification to implementation to post-implementation and evaluation to ensure that organizational objectives are achieved.
  • Ensure strong collaboration with all departments to optimize project performance
  • Strategic growth and resource planning, recruitment, supervision, and training and development of program staff
  • On-the-ground sourcing and procurement of trainers and supplies, with cost and delivery evaluations
  • Strategic planning and execution of strategic initiatives to further RTV’s mission and program strategy
  • Create a detailed work plan that identifies and sequences the activities in different communities
  • Review project schedules with Team Leads and other staff to ensure community problems and issues are solved.
  • Monitor the progress of community activities and adjust as necessary to ensure the successful completion of planned activities;

 

Government Coordination, Capacity Building & Partnership Management

  • Plan, coordinate, and oversee trainings for government staff on RTV methodologies, implementation standards, roles, and accountability frameworks.
  • Coach and mentor sector- and district-level government staff to strengthen joint planning, supervision, reporting, and implementation quality.
  • Support government counterparts in supervision and monitoring of RTV-supported activities, including joint field visits, household coaching sessions, and structured problem-solving.
  • Collect, validate, and consolidate activity and progress reports from government counterparts and ensure timely integration into RTV reporting systems.
  • Promote a strong partnership culture between RTV staff and government officials to enable smooth, effective, and sustainable project implementation at scale.

Methodology

  • Provide contributions and feedback to project designs and methodologies;
  • Support implementation and transition activities;

Supervision

  • Coordinate contacts and planning of initial project visits and prepare budgets;
  • Conduct the initial project visits for prospective visitors and resolve any challenges pertaining to visit
  • Monitor performance of program staff and provide continuous coaching and corrective feedback
  • Maintain strong working relationship within and among the programs, planning and evaluation, M&E, and operations teams
  • Ensure staff receive proper orientation and training;

Administration and logistical support

  • Oversee store management and ensure effective utilization of all input management tools such as the Goods Received Note, Stock Request Form and Goods Returned Form.
  • Conduct on-going interviews of leadership and community on performance, participation, and perceptions
  • Manage and report on office budgets and expenditures
  • Track and review on-going financial reports and progress
  • Complete weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports and provide them to relevant management staff
  • Complete necessary reporting for local government district office
  • Oversee on-going growth and development programming
  • Support in the recruitment of new staff
  • Prepare office accountability and ensure bi-weekly submission to the Finance Officer

Qualifications, Education and Job Requirements

  • University Degree in Project Management, Social Work and Social Administration, Project planning and Development, Community Development, or related fields
  • Masters or Post Graduate Diploma in Project planning and Management will be an added advantage.
  • Minimum of four (5) years of working experience.
  • Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at District and Sector levels (mandatory)
  • At least 3 years at a supervisory level.
  • Experience in project design, budgeting and project management and implementation at village levels

Personal and Skills Development

  • Develop skills and attend training in RTV’s focus areas, including but not limited to: health, agriculture, income-generation, WASH, VSLAs, Market Linkages/Collective Marketing, etc.
  • Provide input in skills development of team members under your management
  • Conduct mid-term and final performance evaluations for team leads

Preferred Experience and Skills

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English & Kinyarwanda
  • Strong Computer Skills with good knowledge of Microsoft Suite;
  • Excellent organizational and leadership skills with keen attention to details;
  • Accurately completes multiple tasks while taking into consideration special assignments, frequent interruptions, available resources and multiple reporting relationships
  • Strong training & facilitation skills
  • Strong interpersonal skills
  • Reliable, with high integrity and strong work ethic
  • Able to work as part of a team and create a sense of cohesion within teams;
  • Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;
  • Energetic and physically able to hike high terrain;
  • Able to travel 80% of time
  • Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory)

jobinrwanda.title: Rwanda Construction Quality Assurance and Quality Check Engineer (Fixed-term)
jobinrwanda.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.

About the Role

Seeking a Civil/Structural Engineer (3–5+ years) to oversee RICA Seed Centre construction, ensure quality, and resolve site issues by producing and providing designs/drawings and other relevant technical specifications.

Responsibilities

Construction Quality Compliance

  • Review construction plans, specifications, drawings, and technical documentation to ensure compliance with approved quality standards, codes, and regulations.
  • Inspect construction materials upon delivery and verify quality, specifications, quantities, and conformity with approved submittals.
  • Conduct quality compliance checks throughout construction and maintain accurate records of inspections, findings, non-conformities, and corrective actions.
  • Review and/or prepare civil and structural engineering reports, drawings, and structural detailing to support quality assurance and project delivery.

Construction Process Oversight & Coordination

  • Conduct regular site inspections to monitor construction activities and verify compliance with approved drawings, specifications, method statements, and quality requirements.
  • Work closely with consultants, contractors, subcontractors, and construction teams to identify deviations and agree on appropriate corrective actions.
  • Monitor construction processes continuously to identify quality risks early and ensure issues are resolved before they affect project delivery.
  • Coordinate quality assurance activities with project teams to ensure inspections and corrective actions remain aligned with construction schedules and milestones.

Quality Control & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and implement quality control procedures and testing requirements across key construction phases, including concrete, structural, material, and installation works.
  • Provide practical training and guidance to construction teams on quality standards, inspection procedures, testing requirements, and quality control practices.
  • Investigate recurring quality issues, identify root causes, and recommend preventive measures to improve construction quality and reduce rework.
  • Track quality performance and use inspection and testing findings to identify trends, risks, and opportunities for continuous improvement.

Quality Documentation, Reporting & Administration

  • Establish and maintain an organised quality database covering inspection reports, test results, material approvals, non-conformities, and corrective actions.
  • Maintain complete and accessible project documentation, including specifications, quality control plans, inspection schedules, and compliance records.
  • Prepare concise quality reports that summarise inspection findings, outstanding issues, risks, corrective actions, and overall project quality performance.
  • Coordinate inspection and testing schedules with construction teams to minimise disruption while ensuring quality activities are completed on time.

Stakeholder Coordination & Technical Support

  • Facilitate clear communication between construction teams, consultants, contractors, and subcontractors on quality requirements, inspections, and corrective actions.
  • Provide technical recommendations on construction quality issues and support teams in resolving deviations from approved designs and specifications.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

jobinrwanda.title: Umushoferi
jobinrwanda.description:
ITANGAZO RY’AKAZI N’AMAHIRWE

MGK – GUPATANA PROGRAM

Aho ibikorwa bibera: Kigali, Rwanda

Ikigo: MGK

Umwanya: Umushoferi – Gupatana

Andi mahirwe: Marketing Volunteers

KURI MGK

MGK ni ikigo gikora mu bijyanye na transport, gukodesha no gucunga imodoka, kikaba gitanga amahirwe ku bantu bafite ubushake bwo gukora no kwiteza imbere binyuze muri gahunda ya Gupatana.

MGK irashaka abantu bafite ubunyamwuga, ubunyangamugayo, ubushake bwo gukora ndetse n’ubwitange kugira ngo bifatanye n’iyi gahunda.

1. ABASHOFERI BIFUZA KWITABIRA GUPATANA IMODOKA NO GUKORA MARKETING VOLUNTEERING 

MGK irashaka abashoferi bifuza kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana, aho umukandida wujuje ibisabwa ashobora guhabwa imodoka yo gukoresha mu rwego rwa transport, hakurikijwe amasezerano n’amabwiriza bya MGK Cyangwa ushobora gukora ubukorerabushake mu mwuga wa transport (volunters)

Ibisabwa ku mushoferi

Umukandida agomba:

  • Kuba afite uruhushya rwo gutwara ibinyabiziga rufite agaciro, cyane cyane icyiciro B cyangwa C.
  • Kuba azi gutwara imodoka neza kandi afite uburambe mu gutwara.
  • Kuba azi neza imihanda n’uduce dutandukanye twa Kigali.
  • Kuba ari umuntu w’umunyakuri, wizerwa kandi ufite inshingano.
  • Kuba yiteguye kubahiriza gahunda yo gukora no kwishyura hakurikijwe amasezerano.
  • Kubahiriza amabwiriza ya MGK ajyanye no gukoresha, kubungabunga no kwita ku modoka.
  • Kuba azi kuvugana neza n’abakiriya no gutanga serivisi nziza.
  • Kuba yiteguye gutanga ibyangombwa n’amakuru bisabwa mu gihe cyo gusaba.

AMAHIRWE YA GUPATANA

Abashoferi bujuje ibisabwa bashobora kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana, batangiriye ku deposit ya 1,000,000 RWF, hakurikijwe ibisabwa n’amasezerano ya MGK.

Gahunda igamije guha umushoferi amahirwe yo gukoresha imodoka mu buryo bwateguwe, gukora transport no kubona amafaranga, mu gihe agenda yegera intego yo kuzagira imodoka ye bwite, hakurikijwe amasezerano agirana na MGK.

Icyitonderwa: Ingwate/deposit, uburyo bwo kwishyura, igihe cy’amasezerano n’ibindi bisabwa bizasobanurwa neza ku bakandida bujuje ibisabwa mbere yo gutangira gahunda.

Cyangwa kuba uzi :

  • Kumenyekanisha gahunda ya Gupatana mu bice bitandukanye bya Kigali.
  • Gushaka no kwegera abashoferi bashobora kwitabira gahunda.
  • Gukoresha WhatsApp n’imbuga nkoranyambaga mu kumenyekanisha amahirwe ya MGK.
  • Kugeza kuri MGK amakuru y’abifuza kwitabira gahunda.
  • Gufasha mu bikorwa byo kwamamaza no kwegera abakiriya cyangwa abakozi bashya.
  • Kumenyekanisha MGK n’ibikorwa byayo.

Umuntu ushakishwa

Turashaka umuntu:

  • Ufite ubushobozi bwo kuvugana n’abantu neza.
  • Ukoresha neza WhatsApp n’imbuga nkoranyambaga.
  • Ufite umuhate kandi ukunda gushaka ibisubizo.
  • Ushobora gukora neza atagomba guhora akurikiranwa.
  • Ushishikajwe na Marketing, Sales, Transport cyangwa Entrepreneurship.
  • Uzi neza Kigali n’abantu bahatuye.
  • Uburambe muri Marketing cyangwa Sales ni inyongera, ariko si ngombwa.

KUKI WAKWIFATANYA NA MGK?

  • Amahirwe yo kwinjira muri gahunda ya Gupatana.
  • Amahirwe yo kubona uburambe mu bijyanye na Transport na Marketing.
  • Gukorera muri gahunda ifite amabwiriza n’amasezerano asobanutse.
  • Amahirwe yo kwagura imiyoboro y’akazi n’ubucuruzi.
  • Amahirwe yo gukorana n’ikigo gikora mu rwego rwa transport n’imicungire y’imodoka mu Kigali.

UKO WASABA

Abifuza kwitabira amahirwe ya Gupatana Driver cyangwa kuba Marketing Volunteer basabwe kohereza ubusabe bwabo kuri:

Email:mgkltd26@gmail.com    

Aho ibikorwa bibera: Kigali, Rwanda

Uko wandika ku busabe

Ku bashoferi: andika “GUPATANA DRIVER”

Ku ba Marketing Volunteers: andika “MARKETING VOLUNTEER”

MGK

Dufasha abantu kubona amahirwe binyuze muri Transport.

jobinrwanda.description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.

Responsibilities

Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

  • Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.
  • Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.
  • Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.
  • Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

  • Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots.
  • Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption.
  • Provide timely agronomic troubleshooting to farmers and field teams addressing crop, soil, pest, and climate-related challenges.
  • Work with MEL and field teams to develop and implement systems that track adoption, farmer outcomes, and opportunities for scaling.

Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact

  • Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.
  • Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes.
  • Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming.
  • Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

  • Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives.
  • Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners.
  • Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives.
  • Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field.
  • Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems.
  • Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.
  • Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners.
  • Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings.
  • Proficiency in English is required; additional regional or international languages are an advantage.

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

Kigali, Rwanda

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Contract Duration

2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.

Eligibility

This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred.

Application Deadline

03 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

About the Role

We are looking for an exceptional strategist and communicator to improve coordination between all of the Impact Division's workstreams. You will support the CIO in advancing One Acre Fund's Global Impact Strategy.

Responsibilities

The Impact Division supports all One Acre Fund programs to generate more impact, wherever we work. We help the organization keep three core aspects of impact at the forefront of our work: 

  1. Improving farmer livelihoods in the short-term
  2. Ensuring long-term viability through sustainable agricultural practices (soil health, crop diversity, etc.)
  3. Addressing non-agricultural needs of farming households (energy, nutrition, etc.)

The role of the Impact Chief of Staff is to support the Chief Impact Officer (CIO) in advancing our organization’s Impact Strategy. Three critical components of this role are to:

  1. Improve coordination of many different actors to implement our Impact Strategy.
  2. Increase the reach and effectiveness of Impact Division leadership.
  3. Lead strategic research, communications, or operational initiatives.

Increasing the reach of Impact leadership

jobinrwanda.description:
GEOLOGIST – MINING 

Company: Lyon Mining Services Ltd 

Location: Rwanda – Based in Kigali with regular travel to mining sites Reporting to: Technical Director 

Employment Type: Full-time 

Positions: 2 

About Us 

Lyon Mining Services Ltd is a Rwanda-based mining consulting company providingspecialized technical and operational support to mining projects. 

Our services include mine surveying, underground and surface 3D SLAM/LiDARscanning, geological consulting, mining engineering, mine planning and design, digital mining solutions, and mine management support. 

We combine experienced technical professionals with modern technologies to helpmining companies improve safety, productivity, accuracy, operational control, anddecision-making. 

Our goal is to contribute to the development of a mining industry that is smarter, more productive, and globally competitive. 

The Role 

Lyon Mining Services Ltd is seeking a motivated and technically competent Mining Geologist to join our technical team. 

The Geologist will support geological activities across various mining and explorationprojects, including geological mapping, sampling, logging, mineral identification, grade control, geological data collection and interpretation, resource evaluation, and geological reporting. 

The position involves regular fieldwork at mining and exploration sites across Rwanda and close collaboration with mining engineers, surveyors, processing teams, mine operators, and clients. 

Key Responsibilities 

  • Conduct geological mapping, sampling, logging, and mineral identification at mining andexploration sites. 
  • Support grade control, orebody interpretation, and geological data collection. 
  • Prepare geological maps, sections, sampling records, and technical reports. 
  • Interpret geological and assay data to support mine planning and production activities.
  •  Assist with exploration, resource evaluation, and geological modelling. 
  • Collaborate with mining, survey, processing, and operational teams. 
  • Maintain accurate geological databases, sample records, and field documentation.
  • Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and professional standards. 

Requirements 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Applied Geology, Mining Geology, Earth Sciences, or a related field. 
  • Practical knowledge of mining or exploration geology. 
  • Good understanding of geological mapping, sampling, logging, grade control, and mineral identification. 
  • Ability to interpret geological and assay data and prepare clear technical reports.
  •  Familiarity with GIS, geological, CAD, or mine-planning software is an advantage.
  •  Strong analytical, communication, teamwork, and fieldwork skills. 
  • Willingness to travel regularly and work at mining sites across Rwanda. 
  • Good command of English; knowledge of Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.

What We Offer 

  • Opportunity to work on a variety of mining, exploration, and geological consulting projects.
  •  Exposure to both underground and surface mining operations. 
  • Opportunity to work alongside mining engineers, surveyors, geologists, and other technical specialists. 
  • Exposure to modern mining and digital technologies, including SLAM/LiDARscanning, GNSS surveying, drone surveying, 3D mine visualization, and geological data integration.  Continuous professional development and practical field experience. 
  • A dynamic working environment with opportunities for increased technical and professional responsibility. 
  • Competitive remuneration based on qualifications, experience, and demonstrated capability.

How to Apply 

Interested candidates should submit the following documents to office@lyonmining.com : 

  • An updated Curriculum Vitae (CV); 
  • A short cover letter explaining their suitability for the position; 
  • Copies of relevant academic and professional qualifications; and 
  • Any relevant professional certificates or supporting documents. 
  • Applications should clearly indicate “Application – Geologist (Mining)” inthesubject line. 

Application Deadline: 30 September 2026

ndangira.title: Driver  at Water Access Rwanda
ndangira.title_raw: Driver  at Water Access Rwanda: (Deadline 2 Oct 2026)
ndangira.description:
About the Role
The Company Driver moves WAR staff, partners and equipment safely and on time between our Kigali office, our project sites and government and partner offices. The role sits in the Finance & Logistics team. A driver at WAR is a trusted ambassador of the company on the road and a first-line guardian of our vehicles.
BookWalking Tours
Key Result Areas

??Safe and on-time transport of staff, partners and cargo to all designated destinations.
??Day-to-day vehicle care — cleanliness and basic maintenance of the assigned company vehicle.
??Accurate trip logging — fuel reporting and adherence to WAR's vehicle policies.
??Professional representation — courteous conduct with passengers and the public.
??Full compliance with the Rwandan highway code and all WAR safety and integrity policies.

Detailed Responsibilities

??Drive WAR staff and authorised passengers within Kigali and to project sites in Bugesera, Eastern Province and Western Province.
??Conduct daily pre-trip vehicle checks (fluids, tyres, lights, fuel) and report defects immediately.
??Carry out basic vehicle troubleshooting and arrange professional repairs through the Direct Supervisor.
??Maintain accurate trip logs, fuel records and mileage reports; submit weekly to Finance & Logistics.
??Plan routes ahead of time; anticipate traffic, road and weather conditions to ensure punctuality.
??Keep the vehicle clean inside and outside at all times; safeguard tools, equipment and documents on board.
??Observe the Rwandan highway code at all times; respect WAR speed limits, seat-belt and no-phone-while-driving rules.
??Support light loading and unloading of equipment when collecting parts or delivering materials.
??Be on call for early-morning, evening or weekend trips when the schedule requires.
Strictly observe WAR's anti-corruption policy — accepting or offering any bribe is grounds for immediate termination.

Qualifications & Profile

?? Education: High school diploma or equivalent certificate (A2, TVET or recognised vocational driving school).
??License: Valid Rwandan driving license covering at least two of the following categories: B, C, D or F.
??Experience: 3+ years professional driving experience preferred — applications with less are still considered if other qualifications are strong.
??Mechanical Knowledge: Basic vehicle mechanics — able to diagnose simple faults and perform routine maintenance.
??Languages: Fluent Kinyarwanda; English is a strong advantage.
??Clean driving record — we will request and verify.

Skills & Values Fit

??Trustworthiness — reliable, honest, discreet with confidential passenger information.
??Accountability — owns mistakes, reports issues early, never hides incidents.
??Punctuality — non-negotiable; excellent time management.
??Multitasking - comfortable juggling shifting schedules, last-minute changes and competing requests.

Compensation

Base Salary: RWF 165,340 / month gross
Transport Allowance: RWF 83,900 / month gross
Retention Pay: RWF 35,000 / month gross
Net Take-Home (probation, first 3 months): RWF 187,000 / month
Net Take-Home (post-probation): RWF 221,000 / month
Annual Review: 5-7% Cost-of-Living Adjustment (COLA)
Benefits: Statutory per WAR HR Manual and Rwandan labour law (RSSB, public holidays, leave)

How to Apply
Send the following to: hr@wateraccess.rw
Subject: Application: Company Driver — (Your Full Name)

??Your CV with at least two contactable references
??A short cover letter (max one page) covering: (1) which driving license categories you hold and since when, (2) the most challenging trip you have ever completed and how you handled it, and (3) why you want to drive for Water Access Rwanda specifically

Note: Shortlisted candidates will be invited for a practical driving test, a Kinyarwanda highway-code interview, and our standard bribe-test screening before any offer is made.

ndangira.description:
Job Description: Laboratory Technologist – PROPS Trial
Project: PROPS Trial (Efficacy of Probiotic Supplementation in Preterm and Small-for-Gestational-Age Infants)Duty Station: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Laboratory, Kigali, with liaison to hospital laboratories and the centralised study laboratory under the trial’s hub-and-spoke modelReports to: Principal Investigator, in coordination with the Site Laboratory Lead/Co-InvestigatorEmployment Terms: Fixed-term, for the duration of the PROPS trial at the Rwanda site, renewable subject to performance and funding
Position Overview
The Laboratory Technologist will be responsible for the receipt, processing, quality-controlled analysis, and storage of biological specimens, including blood culture and faecal specimens, collected under the PROPS Trial. The Laboratory Technologist will ensure that all laboratory procedures are performed accurately, safely, and in strict compliance with the study protocol, trial laboratory SOPs, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), ICH-GCP, national laboratory requirements, biosafety standards, and institutional policies.
The Laboratory Technologist will support the trial's hub-and-spoke laboratory model, including specimen reception and initial processing, transportation and receipt of specimens at the centralised study laboratory, definitive processing, biobanking, quality assurance, documentation, and preparation of specimens for further analysis or shipment as required by the study protocol.
Key Responsibilities

Ensure readiness of all laboratory-related SOPs, protocols, equipment, supplies, and processes as required by the PROPS multi-country assessment team.
Receive, log, and verify blood culture and faecal specimens delivered from study sites, hospital collection points, and home visits, and verify specimen identifiers against accompanying request forms, CRFs, and study records.
Ensure blood culture specimens are appropriately inoculated, transported, received, and processed within the required timelines, including receipt within one hour at the hospital laboratory and within 24 hours at the central laboratory, as applicable.
Process blood culture specimens using automated blood culture equipment and approved standard laboratory methods.
Process faecal specimens using the laboratory methods specified in the study protocol and applicable SOPs.
Freeze isolates and specimens at the specified temperatures, including −20°C to −80°C for faecal specimens and −60°C to −80°C for blood culture isolates requiring further testing.
Maintain the study biorepository/freezers, including temperature monitoring, freezer maintenance logs, and organised and retrievable storage of specimens for the approved retention period.
Package and prepare specimens for transport or shipment to the centralised laboratory or other approved destination, maintaining cold-chain integrity and completing the relevant shipment and freezer-storage logs.
Complete all laboratory-related CRFs, logs, registers, and study documentation accurately and promptly, including specimen reception, automated blood culture processing, blood isolate processing, faecal specimen processing, freezer storage, and shipment logs.
Communicate laboratory results, particularly positive blood culture results, promptly to the clinical/outcome team as required by the study protocol.
Participate in internal quality control and quality assurance activities and support external audits, monitoring visits, and assessments conducted by the study team, contracted infectious disease consultants, sponsors, or relevant authorities.
Address and document findings related to specimen handling, storage, processing, documentation, equipment, and laboratory procedures in accordance with approved corrective and preventive actions.
Maintain up-to-date ICH-GCP certification and complete all study-specific laboratory SOP training before undertaking trial-related laboratory duties, together with required refresher training.
Maintain specimen confidentiality and data protection in accordance with the study's consent provisions, national regulations, and institutional requirements, including restrictions relating to specimen export and secondary use.
Follow national biosafety, infection prevention and control, occupational safety, and laboratory waste-management procedures at all times when handling biological specimens.
Maintain laboratory equipment, including automated blood culture systems, freezers, thermometers, and other relevant equipment, in good working condition and escalate equipment faults or temperature excursions immediately.
Ensure proper specimen traceability from receipt through processing, storage, retrieval, shipment, and final disposition.
Work collaboratively with clinical, outcome, data, research, laboratory, and other study teams to ensure timely and effective implementation of laboratory activities.
Support the Principal Investigator and study team with any other laboratory-related duties required for the successful conduct of the PROPS Trial.

Qualifications and Experience
Essential

Master of Science (MSc) in Biotechnology, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical Sciences, or a closely related field.
Valid registration/license as a Laboratory Technologist/Technician with the relevant Rwandan professional regulatory body, such as the Rwanda Allied Health Professions Council, or national accreditation as required by the trial protocol.
A minimum of two (2) years of relevant experience in a clinical, microbiology, or research laboratory, preferably within a hospital or clinical trial setting.
Demonstrated experience in laboratory specimen reception, processing, documentation, storage, and quality control.
Sound understanding of biosafety, infection prevention and control, and safe handling of biological specimens.
Ability to accurately maintain laboratory records, CRFs, specimen logs, freezer records, and shipment documentation.
Ability to work in accordance with laboratory SOPs, study protocols, quality management procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and security of participant information, biological specimens, and study data.

Preferred

Experience working with automated blood culture systems.
Experience with faecal or other microbiological specimen processing.
Experience with cold-chain specimen handling and storage.
Prior experience working on a clinical trial.
Experience working in a GCLP- or ICH-GCP-compliant laboratory environment.
Experience with biobanking and long-term biological specimen storage.
Familiarity with electronic data capture systems or laboratory information management systems.
Experience supporting laboratory audits, monitoring visits, or external quality assessments.
Experience working within a multi-site or multi-country research study.

Required Technical and Management Skills

Laboratory specimen processing and handling.
Microbiological specimen processing.
Automated blood culture systems.
Biological specimen storage and biobanking.
Cold-chain management.
Laboratory quality control and quality assurance.
Biosafety and infection prevention and control.
Laboratory documentation and record keeping.
Completion of CRFs, specimen logs, freezer records, and shipment documentation.
ICH-GCP and Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP).
Laboratory equipment operation and maintenance.
Specimen traceability and data management.
Microsoft Office and relevant laboratory/data management systems.
Report writing and documentation skills.
Good communication and teamwork skills.
Understanding of clinical research and laboratory systems.

How to Apply:
Interested candidates should apply via this link by October 05, 2026

ndangira.description:
Job Description: Research Project Director
Projects: HealthyStart and PROPS RwandaDuty Station: Rwanda with project-site travelReports to: Principal InvestigatorEmployment Terms: One-year renewable, subject to funding
Position Overview
The Research Project Director is a senior management position responsible for the overall executive leadership, management, and operational delivery of the HealthyStart and PROPS Rwanda Projects. The Research Project Director will work closely with the Principal Investigator to shape project strategy, annual workplans, budgets, and implementation priorities. The Director will hold overall responsibility for project operations, financial management, staffing, partnerships, risk management, compliance, and delivery of project objectives across all project teams, sites, and partners. The successful candidate will ensure that the projects are implemented on time, within approved budgets, and in accordance with approved protocols, ethical and regulatory requirements, donor agreements, safeguarding standards, and institutional policies.
Key Responsibilities

Provide overall executive leadership and management of the projects, setting operational direction and priorities for all project teams.
Work with the Principal Investigator to shape project strategy, annual workplans and budgets, and lead their implementation across teams, sites and partners.
Hold overall accountability for project budgets, approving expenditures within delegated authority and ensuring sound financial management, forecasting and reporting.
Lead the recruitment, appointment, performance management and development of project staff in coordination with the KFHRF HR team and decide on staffing structures within approved budgets.
Chair the project management team and represent the projects in senior-level meetings with donors, government institutions, implementing partners and institutional leadership.
Monitor milestones, deliverables and risks, make timely decisions to resolve operational challenges and direct corrective action.
Ensure compliance with approved protocols, ethical and regulatory requirements, donor agreements, safeguarding standards and institutional policies.
Approve progress reports and key project documents before submission, and escalate major scientific, clinical or strategic matters to the Principal Investigator.
Build a culture of teamwork, accountability, problem-solving and continuous improvement.

Authority and Accountability

The Research Project Director shall advise and, when required, make decisions concerning the operations and management of the projects, acting within approved protocols, budgets, donor agreements, institutional policies, and delegated authority.
The Director's areas of authority include, but are not limited to:
Operational decisions: Setting priorities, allocating resources, and assigning work across project teams and sites.
Financial decisions: Approving expenditures, procurement, and budget reallocations within approved budget lines and delegated financial limits.
People decisions: Recruiting, appointing, supervising, evaluating, and managing project staff, including approval of leave, travel, and performance-related actions within delegated authority.
Partnership decisions: Signing off on operational arrangements, reports, and communications with partners within delegated authority.
Risk and implementation decisions: Taking timely corrective and operational decisions to address project implementation challenges within approved authority.
Scientific, clinical, and protocol decisions, as well as changes to the overall project strategy, total project budget, or contractual commitments with donors, shall be made jointly with the Principal Investigator and approved by the relevant institutional authorities.

Qualifications and Experience
Essential

ndangira.description:
Job Description: Senior Pharmacist (Chief Study Pharmacist) – PROPS Trial
Project: PROPS Trial (Efficacy of Probiotic Supplementation in Preterm and Small-for-Gestational-Age Infants)Duty Station: Central study office/pharmacy, King Faisal Hospital Rwanda Foundation, Kigali, with oversight of investigational product (IP) storage at participating study hospital sitesReports to: Principal Investigator, with functional reporting to the Study Sponsor/Coordinating Centre on investigational product (IP) mattersEmployment Terms: One year (Renewable), for the duration of the PROPS trial at the Rwanda site, renewable subject to performance and funding
Position Overview
The Senior Pharmacist (Chief Study Pharmacist) will have overall responsibility for the receipt, storage, blinding integrity, allocation, distribution, monitoring, accountability, and destruction of the investigational product (IP) and placebo used in the PROPS Trial. The Chief Study Pharmacist will ensure that all investigational product management activities are conducted accurately and in strict compliance with the Investigational Product Management SOP, Product Provision SOP, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), applicable national pharmaceutical regulations, and trial requirements.
The Chief Study Pharmacist will oversee central receipt and storage of investigational product, coordinate IP overlabelling and blinding activities, maintain participant ID master lists, manage site-level IP supply and replenishment, monitor temperature and storage conditions, oversee IP accountability and reconciliation, and coordinate end-of-study destruction. The position will also provide supervision, training, and technical guidance to pharmacy and unblinded support staff involved in trial IP management.
Key Responsibilities

Ensure investigational product is stored immediately under controlled temperature conditions of 2–8°C upon receipt and maintained under continuous temperature monitoring.
Coordinate and directly oversee the unblinded team responsible for overlabelling individual IP sticks to obscure manufacturer batch numbers while preserving the integrity of trial blinding and complying with applicable regulatory requirements.
Ensure that IP Temperature Deviation Logs are completed for any period during which IP boxes are outside the required 2–8°C storage range during overlabelling activities, and ensure that overlabelling records are complete and accurate.
Maintain the master lists of available participant IDs separately for preterm and term SGA infants and generate and verify daily sub-lists for IP allocation across participating study sites.
Reconcile participant ID master lists on a daily basis, recycle unused participant IDs where permitted, and ensure unused participant boxes are appropriately reissued to minimise product wastage.
Review and approve requests from site/hospital pharmacists for IP box shipments, ensuring participating hospital sites maintain an appropriate buffer supply, including at least a two-week supply where required by the study.
Ensure IP shipments to participating hospital sites are dispatched in appropriate temperature-controlled containers, including cool boxes with icepacks and thermometers, with complete and accurate shipment documentation.
Ensure the PROPS IP Temperature Monitoring Log, including required AM and PM readings, is completed at every storage location and that temperature excursions are promptly reported to the Site Principal Investigator within the required timeframe.
Monitor cumulative time that IP sachets are outside the required 2–8°C range and ensure that applicable study thresholds are not exceeded, taking appropriate corrective action where thresholds are approached or breached.
Serve as the primary point of contact for the Sponsor, Coordinating Centre, external monitors, auditors, and relevant regulatory stakeholders on all investigational product-related matters.
Maintain inspection- and audit-ready IP accountability records, including receipt, storage, overlabelling, allocation, distribution, temperature monitoring, reconciliation, return, and destruction records.
Lead end-of-study reconciliation of remaining, unused, and expired investigational product and coordinate destruction in accordance with applicable regulations and Sponsor/Coordinating Centre requirements.
Coordinate destruction of expired or unused IP with an appropriately licensed incineration facility and ensure all required approvals and documentation are obtained.
Obtain and retain incineration certificates and ensure the PROPS IP Destruction Log is completed accurately and retained within the study records.
Supervise, train, and mentor Pharmacist(s) and pharmacy/unblinded support staff on the Investigational Product Management SOP, Product Provision SOP, and other relevant trial procedures.
Monitor compliance of pharmacy staff with study-specific procedures and ensure that required training and certifications are maintained throughout the trial.
Maintain and, where necessary, escalate proposed updates to IP-related SOPs, logs, forms, and processes in collaboration with the Principal Investigator and Coordinating Centre.
Ensure all pharmacy staff complete and maintain current ICH-GCP certification and study-specific training before undertaking trial-related IP activities.
Identify, document, and escalate IP quality concerns, temperature excursions, stock discrepancies, supply interruptions, and other issues that may affect participant safety, trial integrity, or study compliance.
Ensure strict confidentiality and protection of information related to participant IDs, investigational products, randomisation, allocation, and trial documentation.
Support the Principal Investigator and study team with other pharmacy and investigational product management duties required for the successful conduct and closeout of the PROPS Trial.

Qualifications and Experience
Essential

Minimum of Bachelor of Pharmacy (BPharm) or equivalent professional pharmacy qualification.
Current registration and valid license to practice as a pharmacist with the Rwanda Pharmacy Council or equivalent national regulatory body.
Minimum of ten (10) years of post-registration professional experience, including experience in hospital pharmacy, clinical trial pharmacy, investigational product management, pharmaceutical supply-chain management, or related areas.
Demonstrated experience in pharmacy operations, pharmaceutical inventory management, storage, distribution, and accountability.
Prior supervisory or team-leadership experience.
Current ICH-GCP certification, or demonstrated willingness and ability to complete the required certification before undertaking trial activities.
Working knowledge of Rwanda FDA requirements and applicable national pharmaceutical and regulatory requirements for clinical trials.
Demonstrated ability to maintain accurate pharmaceutical records, accountability documentation, and temperature-controlled storage records.
Strong understanding of confidentiality requirements and the importance of maintaining trial blinding and allocation safeguards.

Preferred

Master's degree in Pharmacy or related pharmaceutical sciences.
Doctor of Pharmacy (PharmD) qualification.
Prior experience managing investigational products in a clinical trial.
Experience with blinded clinical trial products and overlabelling procedures.
Experience managing temperature-sensitive pharmaceutical products and cold-chain systems.
Experience coordinating pharmaceutical supply and inventory across multiple hospital sites.
Experience supporting clinical trial monitoring visits, audits, or regulatory inspections.
Experience with clinical trial IP management systems, electronic tracking systems, or tablet-based applications.
Experience working with international research institutions, Sponsors, or clinical trial Coordinating Centres.

Required Technical and Management Skills

Investigational product management.
Clinical trial pharmacy operations.
Good Clinical Practice (GCP).
Good Pharmacy Practice.
Pharmaceutical inventory and stock management.
Cold-chain management and temperature monitoring.
IP receipt, storage, allocation, distribution, reconciliation, and destruction.
Blinding and randomisation safeguards.
Pharmaceutical documentation and accountability systems.
Temperature deviation and excursion management.
Multi-site pharmaceutical logistics and supply management.
Quality assurance and regulatory compliance.
Audit and inspection readiness.
Staff supervision, training, and mentoring.
Risk identification, problem-solving, and corrective action.
Confidentiality and protection of trial information.
Electronic data, inventory, and IP tracking systems.
Microsoft Office and relevant pharmacy or study management systems.
Report writing and documentation skills.
Understanding of clinical research and pharmaceutical regulatory systems.

Interested candidates should apply via this link by October 05, 2026

ndangira.title: Plant Operator at Kivu Choice Ltd
ndangira.title_raw: Plant Operator at Kivu Choice Ltd: (Deadline 30-09-2026)
ndangira.description:
Job Title: Plant Operator (Processing)Location: Kigali, Processing PlantReporting to: Mike Crivea
Contract Type: Full-time, on-site (shift-based operations)
About Kivu Choice:
Kivu Choice is Rwanda’s largest protein producer and one of the fastest-growing aquaculture companies in Africa. Founded in 2022, Kivu Choice is the sister company to Victory Farms, East Africa’s leading aquaculture platform based in Kenya. The company operates a fully vertically integrated aquaculture model, encompassing hatchery operations, cage-based grow-out, processing, distribution, and sales. Kivu Choice is also one of the country’s largest employers with over 700 employees, and plans to grow to 1,200 employees within the next three years, reflecting its strong commitment to job creation and inclusive economic development. Over the next five years, Kivu Choice aims to scale into Africa’s largest and most sustainable protein producer, producing and distributing 30,000 tons of fish annually for the Rwandan market and for export across the region.
Job Purpose:
The plant operator leads the day-to-day running of Kivu Choice’s fish processing plant, ensuring that machinery-heavy production lines run safely, efficiently, and without unplanned stoppages. The role owns process control, preventive and corrective maintenance, and quality and food safety compliance across the plant, while leading shift teams and operators. As Kivu Choice scales volumes toward 30,000 tons a year, this position is critical to protecting throughput, yield, and product quality from intake through to cold storage and dispatch.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Production & Process Control

Plan and run daily production to meet volume, yield, and quality targets across all processing lines.
Set, monitor, and adjust process parameters (line speeds, temperatures, and processing times) to keep output consistent.
Develop and enforce standard operating procedures (SOPs) for every line and piece of equipment.
Identify bottlenecks and lead continuous improvement to raise throughput and reduce waste.
Coordinate with harvest, logistics, and sales teams so that raw material intake matches plant capacity and orders.

2. Preventive & Corrective Maintenance

Build and run a preventive maintenance schedule for all plant machinery, refrigeration, and utilities.
Lead fast troubleshooting and corrective repairs to keep unplanned downtime to a minimum.
Maintain equipment history, maintenance logs, and a critical spare parts inventory.
Manage external technicians and suppliers for specialized servicing and repairs.
Advise on equipment upgrades, new installations, and capacity expansion.

3. Quality Control & Food Safety

Implement and maintain food safety systems in line with HACCP, GMP, and ISO 22000 principles.
Monitor critical control points and ensure corrective action is taken and documented when limits are breached.
Enforce hygiene, sanitation, and cleaning-in-place standards across the plant.
Prepare the plant for internal, customer, and regulatory audits (e.g. Rwanda FDA, RSB) and close out findings.
Ensure full product traceability from raw material intake to finished goods.

4. Cold Chain & Product Integrity

Oversee chilling, freezing, and cold storage operations to keep product within required temperature ranges.
Monitor and record temperatures across processing, storage, and loading points.
Work with logistics to protect cold chain integrity through dispatch and distribution.

5. Shift Leadership & People Management

Lead, schedule, and supervise shift supervisors, machine operators, and line workers.
Train operators on safe equipment use, SOPs, hygiene, and food safety practices.
Set clear performance expectations, give regular feedback, and contribute to performance reviews.
Enforce occupational health and safety standards and lead incident investigations.

6. Production Reporting & KPIs

Track and report daily, weekly, and monthly KPIs, including throughput, downtime, yield, and waste.
Analyze performance trends and present root causes and action plans to management.
Maintain accurate production, maintenance, and quality records.
Support budgeting for plant operations, maintenance, and spare parts.

Qualifications & Experience:

Bachelor’s degree or advanced diploma in mechanical, electrical, electromechanical, industrial, or food process engineering, food science, or a related field.
At least 5 years of experience in a processing plant (food, beverage, dairy, meat, poultry, or fish processing preferred), including hands-on supervision of machinery-heavy production lines.
Strong process control skills and proven experience running preventive and corrective maintenance programs.
Working knowledge of quality control and food safety standards such as HACCP, GMP, or ISO 22000.
Cold chain or perishable-product experience is a strong plus.
Proven ability to lead shift teams and operators in a production environment.
Comfortable with production reporting and KPIs such as throughput, downtime, and yield; good working knowledge of Excel.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to diagnose equipment and process issues quickly under pressure.
Rwandan national, or already holding the right to work in Rwanda (Kivu Choice is not able to sponsor work permits for this role).
Fluency in English and Kinyarwanda; French or Swahili is an advantage.

How to Apply:

If you are interested in this position, prepare the following:
Job application letter
Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Copy of your degree and other academic qualifications
Copy of your ID How to apply: send all the required documents to our email address: recruiting@kivuchoice.com 
Submission Deadline: 30th September 2026.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis as they are submitted.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

ndangira.title_raw: Business Development Director - African Quality Assurance Centre Holding Company at Afreximbank - African Export-Import Bank: (Deadline Ongoing)
ndangira.description:
Job Description

The Business Development Director is responsible for driving growth, market expansion, and strategic partnerships for AQAC Holding Company through structured sales, marketing and key account development activities. This role focuses on identifying new opportunities, strengthening client relationships, and positioning AQAC as Africa’s leading provider of laboratory and quality assurance services. The Business Development Director will work closely with the CEO, Finance Director, and subsidiary leaders to deliver sustainable revenue growth and enhance AQAC’s market presence across the continent.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Growth & Market Expansion

Develop and execute business development strategies aligned with AQAC’s vision and growth objectives.
Identify new markets, industries, and geographic regions for expansion with emphasis on strategic sectors and strategic countries.
Lead market entry strategies, feasibility studies, and partnership negotiations in collaboration with the CEO and FD.
Monitor industry trends and competitor activities to maintain competitive advantage to strengthen AQAC’s market positioning as a global TIC player.

Client Acquisition & Relationship Management

Develop and implement a go-to market strategy for all AQAC’s
Build and maintain strong relationships with governments, multinational corporations, and local industries as key clients and revenue anchors.
Drive new client acquisition through a structured sales pipeline and ensure retention of key accounts.
Negotiate and secure long-term contracts with high-value clients including framework agreements and multi-country contracts.
Enhance customer satisfaction through tailored solutions and service excellence.

Partnerships & Alliances

Establish strategic partnerships with universities, research institutions, and industry associations.
Collaborate with regulators and government agencies to influence policy and standards.
Develop alliances with international TIC (Testing, Inspection, Certification) companies to strengthen AQAC’s global reach.

Innovation & Service Development

Identify client needs and translate them into new service offerings with clear commercial and pricing models
Develop and implement a CRM system across all AQAC’s.
Support R&D initiatives by aligning business opportunities with innovation projects.
Promote digital transformation services (LIMS, AI-driven analytics).
Drive ESG-linked business opportunities, including sustainability-focused testing and certification.

Financial & Strategic Contribution

Contribute to revenue growth targets and profitability goals.
Provide input into capital allocation decisions for new laboratories and expansions.
Ensure business development initiatives deliver measurable ROI.
Collaborate with Finance Director to align BD strategies with financial planning.

Leadership & Team Development

Lead and mentor the business development team across subsidiaries.
Build capacity in sales, marketing, and client relationship management.
Promote a culture of innovation, accountability, and customer focus.
Ensure succession planning for key BD roles.

Requirements

Proven experience as Business Development Director, Head of Sales, or senior executive in TIC, healthcare, industrial services, or related sectors.
Strong track record in market expansion, client acquisition, and partnership development.
Excellent negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Deep understanding of African markets and global business practices.
Advanced degree in Business Administration, Marketing, or related field.
Professional certifications in business development, sales, or project management are desirable.

Benefits

Comprehensive Private Medical Cover: Premium health insurance coverage for the Chief Executive Officer and eligible dependants, in line with the Company’s executive benefits framework.
Executive Development: Access to relevant leadership development, executive education, industry forums and professional development opportunities aligned with the strategic requirements of the role.
Performance-Linked Incentive: Eligibility for an annual performance bonus based on the achievement of approved corporate, financial and individual performance objectives, subject to Board approval and applicable Company policy.
Other Benefits: Additional benefits and employment terms will be provided in accordance with the Company’s applicable policies and as further outlined in the employment contract.
