Plumber at RwandAir Ltd
RwandAir Ltd is the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, operating domestic and international services across East Africa, Central Africa, West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe, and the Middle East from its main base at Kigali International Airport.
As part of its expansion strategy, RwandAir is seeking qualified and competent candidates for the following position:
Job Title
Plumber
Reporting Line
Facilities Maintenance Specialist
Department
HR
Location
Kigali International Airport, Kigali, Rwanda
Job Purpose
The Plumber will perform plumbing installation, maintenance, repair, and inspection activities across RwandAir facilities to ensure the continuous availability, safety, efficiency, and compliance of water supply, drainage, sanitation, and related plumbing systems while minimizing operational disruptions.
Key Duties and Responsibilities

Carry out preventive and corrective maintenance of plumbing, water supply, drainage, sanitation, and associated systems.
Inspect plumbing infrastructure to identify leaks, blockages, equipment failures, and other defects and undertake appropriate corrective actions.
Repair, replace, and install pipes, valves, taps, sanitary fixtures, pumps, water tanks, and related plumbing components.
Respond promptly to plumbing emergencies and breakdowns, particularly in critical operational and service areas.
Conduct routine inspections and report major defects, deterioration, or replacement requirements to the Facilities Maintenance Specialist.
Support renovation, construction, and facility improvement projects involving plumbing installations and modifications.
Ensure all plumbing works comply with applicable safety regulations, technical standards, and company procedures.
Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, inspections, repairs, materials used, and outstanding work orders.
Coordinate with contractors, suppliers, and service providers during specialized maintenance or installation projects.
Ensure proper utilization, maintenance, and accountability of tools, equipment, and plumbing materials.
Maintain a clean, safe, and organized work environment.
Immediately escalate significant plumbing failures, safety hazards, water damage, or operational risks to the Facilities Maintenance Specialist.
Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor.

Qualifications, Professional Requirements & Experience
Experience

Minimum 2 years of relevant experience in plumbing installation, maintenance, and repair.
Experience in airports, airlines, hotels, hospitals, commercial buildings, industrial facilities, or other large-scale operational environments is an added advantage.
Experience responding to maintenance issues in service-critical environments is preferred.

Essential Qualifications

Minimum Diploma in Plumbing, Plumbing Technology, Building Services Engineering, or a related technical discipline from a recognized institution.
Trade certification or professional registration in plumbing is an added advantage.
Sound knowledge of water supply, drainage, sanitation, pumping systems, and plumbing infrastructure.
Ability to read and interpret technical drawings, schematics, and plumbing layouts.
Basic knowledge of occupational health, safety, and environmental practices.
Basic computer literacy and ability to use maintenance management systems and work-order platforms.
Good communication, teamwork, and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently and manage urgent maintenance requirements effectively.
Willingness to work outside normal working hours, including weekends and public holidays, when operationally required.

Strong technical and troubleshooting skills.
Attention to detail and commitment to quality workmanship.
High level of integrity, professionalism, and accountability.
Strong safety awareness and compliance mindset.
Reliability, responsiveness, and customer-service orientation.
Effective interpersonal and teamwork skills.
Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines.
Practical, proactive, and solution-oriented approach to work.

Application letter addressed to the Chief HR & Administration Officer

ndangira.title_raw: Manager, Fleet and Corporate Services at RwandAir Ltd : (Deadline 2026-Oct-10)
ndangira.description:
Manager, Fleet and Corporate Services at RwandAir Ltd
RwandAir Ltd is the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, operating domestic and international services across East Africa, Central Africa, West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe, and the Middle East from its main base at Kigali International Airport.
As part of its expansion strategy, RwandAir is seeking qualified and competent candidates for the following position:
Job Title
Manager, Fleet and Corporate Services
Reports To
Director, EAS & LR
Department
Administration – Fleet and Corporate Services
Location
Kigali International Office, Kigali, Rwanda
Job Purpose
The Manager, Fleet and Corporate Services will provide overall leadership, coordination, and control of the Logistics Unit, covering fleet management and uniform operations.
The role is responsible for ensuring the reliable operation and maintenance of the organization's fleet and drivers, as well as the efficient supply, manufacturing coordination, and distribution of uniforms.
The Manager will also plan and manage the unit's budget, monitor performance against targets, and lead, develop, and supervise staff to deliver cost-effective, timely, and quality logistics services.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
Fleet Management

Oversee effective management of the organization's fleet, ensuring vehicles are roadworthy, available, and deployed according to operational requirements.
Direct scheduled and preventive maintenance, repairs, and servicing of fleet assets to minimize downtime and extend asset life.
Supervise the Fleet Manager and, through them, the Fleet Operations and Fleet Maintenance functions, driver team leaders, and drivers.
Ensure compliance with vehicle licensing, insurance, safety, and regulatory requirements.
Maintain accurate fleet and maintenance records.
Manage driver allocation, scheduling, discipline, welfare, and performance.
Promote safe driving practices and compliance with organizational policies.
Monitor fleet running costs, fuel consumption, and vehicle utilization.
Drive continuous improvements in fleet efficiency and value for money.

Uniform Operations – Supply, Manufacturing & Distribution

Lead uniform operations to ensure adequate supply, timely manufacturing, and accurate distribution.
Coordinate the end-to-end uniform manufacturing process with internal units and external suppliers/manufacturers.
Ensure quality, cost, and delivery requirements are met.
Oversee stock and inventory management for uniforms and related materials.
Minimize shortages, wastage, and unnecessary holding costs.
Ensure deliveries and distribution are efficiently planned and completed on schedule.
Supervise the Uniform Operations Specialist and Uniform Supply Officers.
Set service standards and monitor service quality.

Budgeting & Monitoring

Prepare, justify, and manage the annual Logistics Unit budget covering fleet, maintenance, uniform supply, and distribution.
Monitor expenditure against the approved budget.
Analyze budget variances and take corrective action.
Track unit plans and activities against agreed targets, timelines, and performance indicators.
Report progress to the Director.
Identify cost-saving opportunities and ensure resources are used efficiently and accountably.

Staff Management & Leadership

Lead, supervise, motivate, and develop Logistics Unit staff.
Set objectives and manage employee performance.
Allocate work and monitor productivity.
Ensure appropriate staffing levels across fleet and uniform functions.
Identify training and development needs.
Support capacity building within the unit.
Promote a culture of safety, discipline, teamwork, accountability, and continuous improvement.

General Responsibilities

Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, health and safety standards, and relevant regulations.
Prepare periodic and ad hoc reports on unit operations, performance, and budget for management.
Perform other duties reasonably assigned by the Director, EAS & LR or management.

Minimum Qualifications
Applicants should have:

A Bachelor's degree in:

Logistics
Supply Chain Management
Transport/Fleet Management
Business Administration
Or a related field.

A relevant professional or postgraduate qualification is an added advantage.

Experience

3–5 years of substantial experience in logistics, fleet, and/or operations management.
Experience involving supervisory or managerial responsibility for staff, budgets, and service delivery.

Desired Competencies & Skills

Strong leadership, people management, and team development skills.
Sound knowledge of fleet operations, vehicle maintenance, and driver management.
Understanding of supply, manufacturing coordination, inventory, and distribution processes.
Strong budgeting, financial monitoring, and cost-control skills.
Good planning, organization, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities.
Effective communication, reporting, and stakeholder-management skills.
Proficiency in relevant IT and logistics/fleet management systems.

How to Apply
Applicants should submit:

Application letter addressed to the Chief HR & Administration Officer
Recent Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Copies of notarized degree/diploma certificates
Relevant professional certificates
Copies of academic papers
Photocopy of Passport/National ID
Three referees

Application: https://erecruitment.rwandair.com/
Location: Kigali, Rwanda
Employer: RwandAir Ltd

ndangira.description:
NDT Level 2 Engineer at RwandAir Ltd
RwandAir Ltd is the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, operating domestic and international services across East Africa, Central Africa, West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe, and the Middle East from its main base at Kigali International Airport.
As part of its expansion strategy, RwandAir is seeking qualified and competent candidates for the following position:
Job Title
NDT Level 2 Engineer
Reports To
NDT Level 3 Engineer
Department
Technical
Location
Kigali International Airport – Town Office, Kigali, Rwanda
Job Purpose
The NDT Level 2 Engineer will perform and certify Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) inspections in support of RwandAir's line maintenance, base maintenance, outstation operations, workshops, and third-party maintenance activities.
The role is responsible for supporting aircraft and component structural integrity through accurate inspection, interpretation, and reporting in accordance with approved manuals, regulatory requirements, and industry standards.
The position reports to the NDT Level 3 Engineer and provides timely NDT support across RwandAir's operations to ensure regulatory, technical, and safety compliance.
Key Duties and Responsibilities

Conduct scheduled and unscheduled NDT inspections of aircraft and aircraft components in accordance with approved standards and regulatory requirements.
Exercise the relevant license/approval and issue Certificates of Release to Service for completed work where applicable.
Perform NDT inspections using detection systems approved by the OEM and documented in approved technical data.
Ensure inspected components are correctly handled, labelled, blanked, and routed with the relevant documentation.
Plan and coordinate allocated NDT inspection activities.
Prepare inspection reports and record all NDT inspections on the appropriate checklists.
Ensure availability and serviceability of NDT equipment, tools, and technical data.
Ensure NDT shop tools, equipment, and accessories are properly calibrated and report any discrepancies or failures.
Conduct periodic quality checks of Dye Penetrant and Magnetic Particle Inspection equipment, materials, and processes.
Conduct periodic quality checks of Ultrasonic Inspection transducers and equipment.
Review inspection procedures to ensure they remain current and comply with regulatory requirements.
Report safety hazards and occurrences.
Respond to internal and external audits and implement corrective actions for identified nonconformities.
Maintain a clean and orderly working environment.
Maintain valid NDT qualifications and complete mandatory annual eyesight tests.
Ensure timely renewal of relevant authorizations before expiry.

Management & Leadership

Establish team objectives and priorities aligned with business objectives.
Supervise Level 1 specialists and trainees and direct daily activities.
Train and develop employees to support succession planning.
Contribute to national talent development by coaching and developing national trainees.

Personal Development

Take responsibility for continuous professional development and growth of technical expertise.
Keep up to date with market trends and technical developments.
Assist in responding to emergencies or major operational disruptions affecting RwandAir or its subsidiaries.
Train other staff in various duties as required by the business.

Data Protection
The successful candidate will be expected to:

Handle, use, disclose, and request information in accordance with RwandAir Group data protection principles.
Comply with company policies regarding information security and privacy.
Maintain confidentiality and protect information from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, alteration, destruction, or other security risks.
Consult the Group's Data Protection Officer on relevant data protection and privacy matters.

Safety
The role requires the candidate to:

Promote understanding and compliance with workplace health and safety requirements.
Ensure compliance with safety, security, quality, environmental, and operational policies and procedures.
Support appropriate reporting and investigation of injuries, incidents, near misses, and hazards.
Ensure relevant safety information and training requirements are communicated to staff.

Environmental Responsibilities
The successful candidate will:

Contribute to RwandAir's environmental objectives and targets.
Support the implementation and maintenance of the Environmental Management System.
Apply environmental knowledge and principles to business processes and decision-making to improve efficiency and reduce operational and environmental risks.

Minimum Qualifications & Experience
Applicants should have:

At least 5 years of experience in aviation/NDT or workshop maintenance.
An engineering degree or diploma in one of the following disciplines:

Aeronautical Engineering
Avionics
Mechanical Engineering
Electrical Engineering
Electronics

Experience in aircraft/component maintenance or NDT inspection.
Minimum Level 2 NDT Methods Qualification and a proven track record in line, base, or workshop maintenance environments.
At least one of the following:

Current or previous NDT approval in one method.
NDT EN4179 or PCN (Aerospace) qualification in one or more inspection methods such as PT, MT, UT, ET, RT, or TT.
Successful completion of the qualification examination with the required minimum experience/hours.

Other Desired Competencies & Skills
Applicants should have knowledge of:

Regulations and standards applicable to aircraft airworthiness and maintenance.
NDT inspection procedures.
Aviation quality management systems.
Computer and system analytical skills.

How to Apply
Applicants should submit the following documents:

Application letter addressed to the Chief HR & Administration Officer
Recent Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Copies of notarized degree/diploma certificates
Relevant professional certificates
Copies of academic papers
Photocopy of Passport/National ID
Three referees

Application deadline: 1 October 2026

Internal Auditor at RwandAir Ltd
RwandAir Ltd is the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, operating domestic and international services across East Africa, Central Africa, West Africa, Southern Africa, Europe, and the Middle East from its main base at Kigali International Airport.
As part of its expansion strategy, RwandAir is seeking qualified and competent candidates for the following position:
Job Title
Internal Auditor
Reports To
Senior Internal Auditor
Department
Internal Audit
Location
Kigali International Airport – Town Office, Kigali, Rwanda
Job Purpose
The Internal Auditor will use systematic and disciplined audit approaches to evaluate and improve the effectiveness of RwandAir's risk management, internal controls, and governance processes.
The role involves conducting financial, operational, systems, and process audits, including reviews of outsourced operations, and reporting on the adequacy of internal controls to support the efficient and effective use of organizational resources.
Key Duties and Responsibilities

Perform financial, operational, and compliance audits in accordance with the internal audit program.
Assist senior auditors in carrying out various audit reviews and assignments.
Prepare relevant information, including draft findings and recommendations, under the supervision of a Senior Internal Auditor.
Review internal controls designed to safeguard RwandAir's financial and physical assets and recommend improvements where weaknesses are identified.
Evaluate significant new services, processes, operations, and controls.
Coordinate audit assignments with the Senior Auditor.
Maintain clear audit work papers and audit trails using the appropriate tools.
Investigate irregularities identified by or reported to the Internal Audit function.
Review RwandAir's practices and records for compliance with established policies and procedures.
Develop recommendations to improve internal controls, operational efficiency, and record keeping.
Follow up on the implementation of external audit recommendations.
Perform any other duties assigned by the supervisor or management.

Minimum Qualifications and Experience
Applicants should have:

A Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or Management.
One or more professional certifications such as CPA, CIA, or ACCA, or be currently pursuing one of these qualifications.
Knowledge of accounting packages such as Sun, Microsoft Dynamics NAV, SAGE, Pastel, QuickBooks, or similar systems.
3–5 years of experience as an Auditor in robust institutions.
Thorough understanding of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) and applicable regional statutory requirements.
Proven ability to analyze risks and develop recommendations requiring appropriate remedial action.
Proficiency in computer applications, including word processing, databases, spreadsheets, accounting packages, internet applications, and workflow processes.
High standards of integrity and the ability to establish productive relationships while treating people fairly and respectfully.
Strong communication, presentation, analytical, and organizational skills.
Good understanding of risk management and audit processes.
Ability to document and understand business processes accurately and completely.
Ability to apply international audit standards in practical situations.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Strong interpersonal skills and attention to detail.

ndangira.title: Investment Manager at Afreximbank - African Export-Import Bank
ndangira.title_raw: Investment Manager at Afreximbank - African Export-Import Bank: (Deadline Ongoing)
ndangira.description:
Job Description

As an Investment Manager at FEDA, you will play a pivotal role in each stage of
the investment process for our Direct Investment Fund strategy. This role involves leading the
assessment of potential investments, overseeing financial analysis, driving deal structuring and
negotiation, managing due diligence, and monitoring portfolio performance. You will also work
closely with cross-functional teams, guiding the drafting of concept papers for various projects.
The ideal candidate should possess exceptional analytical skills, a deep understanding of the
private equity sector, and experience with direct investments, particularly in Africa. An ability to
excel in a dynamic and fast-paced environment is crucial.
Duties and Responsibilities:
 Lead and manage the investment team through all phases of the investment process and
the funds’ life cycle, including deal origination, evaluation of investment opportunities,
participation in investment committees and board meetings, portfolio company
management, exit strategies, and fundraising activities.
 Conduct thorough risk assessments, identify opportunities, and evaluate the potential
merits of investments or innovative greenfield projects.
 Lead comprehensive financial analysis, modeling, and valuation to evaluate potential
investment opportunities and perform portfolio monitoring.
 Oversee the deal structuring process including analyzing investment terms, preparing
term sheets and investment memos, leading negotiations and coordinating deal execution
meetings.
 Conduct in depth due diligence on target companies, including interactions with executive
management and research industry trends, competitive landscapes, and financial
performance.
 Coordinate with due diligence advisors, review their deliverables and present findings to
FEDA’s management and investment and strategy committee.
 Evaluate and report on the performance of portfolio companies, identifying key
performance indicators and suggesting improvements. Monitor value-creation plan
including ESG action plan for portfolio companies.
 Prepare monthly and quarterly investment reports to FEDA’s governance (Executive
Management, Board, Investors etc.)
 Stay informed on market trends, regulatory changes, and economic factors that may impact FEDA’s investments.
 Assist in fundraising efforts, including creating marketing materials and participating in
investor meetings for portfolio companies or FEDA’s funds.
 Undertake additional responsibilities as assigned by Management.
Requirements
Analytical Thinking: Ability to dissect complex financial information, identify key trends and
insights, and draw logical conclusions.
 Financial Modeling: Proficient in building and utilizing financial models to assess
investment opportunities, forecast financial performance, value an investment, and
evaluate risk.
 Research and Due Diligence: Skilled in conducting comprehensive research, analyzing
market trends, and performing due diligence on potential investments.
 Attention to Detail: Strong focus on accuracy and precision in financial analysis, data
interpretation, and report preparation.
 Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, with the
ability to effectively articulate investment recommendations and complex financial
concepts.
 Adaptability: Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment, managing multiple
projects and priorities effectively with strong work ethic.
 Teamwork: Collaborative mindset, excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to work
effectively within a team and across departments.
Qualifications:
 Master’s degree in finance, economics, banking, engineering, sciences, or a related field
with a strong academic performance.
 Minimum 7 years of work experience, 5 of which in investment banking, private equity, or
a similar financial role is highly desirable.
 Strong understanding of financial analysis techniques, valuation methodologies, and
investment principles.
 Proficient in financial modeling, Excel, and other relevant analytical tools.
 Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to analyze and interpret
complex financial data.
 Proficiency in and extensive experience with the legal and regulatory frameworks governing private equity investments.
 Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy in financial analysis and
reporting.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex
information in a clear and concise manner.
 Ability to work effectively in a team-oriented environment, collaborating with professionals
from diverse backgrounds.
Benefits

Private Health Insurance
Training & Development
Performance Bonus

ndangira.description:
BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential. 
Position: Technical Sector Officer - Community Mobilization
Job Location:  Ruhango District, Rwanda
About the AIM Program:
The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.
About the Role:
The Technical Support Officer, Community Mobilization (TSO-CM) will support the Technical Coordinator Community Mobilization in planning and implementing social empowerment and community engagement activities, including gender and social inclusion, disability inclusion, SRHR, SGBV, community dialogues, and grassroots-level advocacy. They will also contribute to staff capacity development through targeted training and supervision. Additionally, the TSO-CM will provide technical assistance, support, and quality control in implementing SGBV and SRHR community-based case management and referral systems.
The TSO-CM will collaborate with the country program team, AIM central team, BI technical anchors, and Technical Coordinators to improve program quality, contextualize training modules, and train staff on new materials and tools. They will ensure effective delivery of gender equality and social inclusion (GESI), disability inclusion (DI), Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR), enabling environment and advocacy components are integrated into the overall AIM programmatic operations.
The ideal candidate for this role is one who is proactive, passionate, resourceful, and enjoys being a team player.
Key Responsibilities:
1. Technical Support

Support AIM field team in inception phase activities (community mobilization and inception meetings, transect walks, surveys, YDC formation).
Train regional staff on GESI, GBV, disability inclusion, domestic violence reporting, and women's rights advocacy; enhance PA/mentor capacity on GESI, community mobilization, SRHR, and GBV sessions.
Support social and behaviour change communication (SBCC) planning, monitoring, and evaluation and coordinating with the project team.
Lead the implementation of SBCC dialogue sessions at the community level, targeting local, religious, and cultural leaders, as well as other duty bearers.
Guide community leaders in developing action plans based on commitments made during SBCC dialogue sessions. Support tracking and follow-up on these action plans to ensure progress and accountability.
Identify and adapt safe, accessible club spaces with reasonable accommodations and gender-segregated infrastructure (restrooms, dignity kits, baby changing stations), prioritizing marginalized groups including PWDs.
Support coordination with stakeholders (government, INGOs, CSOs, YDC members, and service providers) for social empowerment and enabling environment interventions.
Participate in regional GESI, SRHR, and SGBV working groups, advocating for women's and girls' rights.
Mentor and support youth advocates in developing, implementing & monitoring advocacy action plans, overseeing practical implementation (events, stakeholder meetings, logistics, linkage to CSO networks and technical working groups).
Lead community action planning sessions to develop community action plans, consolidate commitments and ensure community-led solutions.
Organize action planning and handover meetings at the end of each cohort to secure firm commitments from local leaders and ensure the sustainability of the outcomes.

2. Coordination, Planning and Partnership

Support coordination with a range of stakeholders, including government entities, INGOs, CSOs, YDC members, and service providers at the sub-national level, to support interventions as well as the program’s grassroots advocacy and partnerships work. 
Coordinate and consolidate the mapping of SRHR and SGBV service providers at the regional level.
Organize events for the celebration of international observance days such as International Women's Day, the 16 Days of Activism, and International Day of the Girl Child in the regions.
Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments in youth advocacy action plans.

3. Reporting, Documentation and Communication

Contribute to program reports and deliverables as required and demonstrate the status of GESI and grassroots-level advocacy activities towards achieving expected results.
Quality management, checks, and assurance in the SGBV case recording database to ensure accuracy, efficiency, and timely reports.
Identify and document best practices, most significant change stories, and share this knowledge with colleagues. Ensure quality reporting on enabling environments, community mobilization, and GESI indicators, and document good practices.
Support regional managers, branch managers and programme assistants regularly to ensure timely and high-quality programmatic data entry and reporting in relevant manual and digital MIS (BInsight) by the Program Assistants, and mentors.
Support documentation of program wins and success stories / case studies
Ensure timely preparation and submission of programmatic management information system (MIS), financial and donor reports.

4. Policy and Strategy Compliance

Popularize the Enabling Environment Strategy, GESI policies and SGBV, SRHR and disability inclusion guidelines among the frontline staff through orientations and trainings
Support in policy-related materials development and localization.

Safeguarding responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation.
Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.

Major Challenges:

Access of hard to reach locations in the communities AIM serves
Buy-in for advocacy, GESI & SRHR work at the respective regions
Managing coordination among several team members within the BRAC family.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

Timely achievement of project activities.
Efficient case management and referral systems.
Effective staff capacity building on advocacy, GESI, SRHR, DI and SGBV.
Effective implementation of resources and tools.
Functional SGBV & SRH case management referral mechanism and database.
Strong partnerships established.
Effective implementation of youth advocacy action plans.
Community dialogues delivered using GESI-responsive SBCC messages and tools.
Individual/specific KPIs as agreed with supervisor.

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree / Graduate or Post graduate in International Development, Gender, Sociology, Anthropology, Social Sciences or any other related fields.

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Training materials development, staff capacity building, and facilitation skills
Computer literacy and presentation skills
Report writing and documentation of Most Significant Change Stories
Proactive, self-starter and independent worker with the ability to support large teams
Demonstrate commitment to community mobilization work around education, GESI, SRHR, and advocacy work, applying rights-based, human-centered, and survivor-centered approaches.
Exhibit empathy and positive interpersonal skills, including cultural competence.

Experience Requirements:

3-5 years of relevant experience in gender equality, social inclusion, SGBV, community engagement, and advocacy.
Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to advocacy, community engagement and empowerment-related activities, training module development and execution, and training facilitation.
Experience working in integrated programs targeted for adolescent girls and young women is a plus.
Previous experience in the development of SBCC messages, tools, and materials for community-based dialogues and other activities.
Experience in conducting advocacy, community mobilization and engagement activities is also an added advantage.

Employment type: Regular/Fixed-Term
About BRAC International:
BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.
BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)
Our Core Values:
Integrity: We approach our work with honesty and integrity.
Innovation: We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.
Inclusiveness: We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most.
Effectiveness: We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty.
If you feel you are the right match for the above-mentioned position, please follow the application process to grab your dream opportunity! 
Qualified and interested candidates are recommended to email their Resume with a signed cover letter and any supporting documents in a single PDF format mentioning a brief academic background, career summary, core competence, notarized copies of academic qualifications and professional certifications to sbirwanda.recruitment@brac.net.
Please mention the name of the position in the subject bar
Application deadline: 2nd October 2026
Please note that the shortlisting will be done on rolling basis, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
BRAC is committed to safeguarding children, young people and adults, and expects all employees and volunteers to share the same commitment. We believe every stakeholder and every member of the communities we work with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm, abuse, neglect, harassment, and exploitation - regardless of age, race, religion, and gender, status as an individual with a disability or ethnic origin. Therefore, our recruitment policy and procedure include extensive background checks and disclosure of criminal records in order to ensure safeguarding to the fullest extent.
“BRAC International is an equal opportunities employer”

About the AIM Program:
The Mastercard Foundation Accelerating Impact for Young Women (AIM) in Partnership with BRAC is equipping 2 million adolescent girls and young women (AGYW) with age-appropriate entrepreneurship, employability, and life-skills training, as well as the tools to start and scale their own businesses. The nine-year program (2021-2030) applies BRAC’s proven model using microfinance, youth empowerment, agriculture, education and skills development to improve lives and livelihoods. It currently operates in seven African countries: Sierra Leone, Liberia, Uganda, Tanzania, Rwanda, Ghana, and Kenya. Based on the AGYW age, needs, and circumstances, AGYW are placed on one of two pathways in the AIM program: an education pathway or a livelihood pathway.
About the AIM Education Pathway:
The AIM Education pathway is designed to increase access to and completion of quality secondary education for adolescent girls, aged 12-17, across the AIM countries: Ghana, Kenya, Liberia, Rwanda, Sierra Leone, Tanzania, and Uganda. The program seeks to achieve three core objectives: (1) to empower 400,000 adolescent girls by increasing their agency, voice, and life skills; (2) to support adolescent girls to complete at least lower secondary school; and (3) to improve gender-responsive education in at least 2,000 secondary schools, positively impacting an estimated 2.4 million students.
This AIM education pathway is closely aligned with the Mastercard Foundation’s strategic priorities under its Young Africa Works initiative, particularly the emphasis on improving the quality and accessibility of secondary education to better prepare young people for meaningful work. Through a set of integrated interventions, AIM Education targets structural and social challenges that often hinder girls’ education—including financial barriers, inadequate infrastructure, undertrained teachers, harmful gender norms, lack of community support, and weak school governance systems.
About the Role:
The Technical Sector Officer (TSO) - Education will support the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in planning, implementing, and ensuring the quality delivery of the AIM education pathway.
They will be responsible for technical & implementation-related tasks under AIM education pathway, i,e. facilitating training, reviewing content and curriculum and adapting it to their context, and supporting teachers' professional development as well as school leadership's school improvement planning processes. They will also contribute to staff capacity development through targeted training and supervision.
The TSO-Education will collaborate with the region & country level program team, other sectral TSOs for any technical need/query, to improve program quality, contextualize training modules, and train staff on new materials and tools. They will ensure effective delivery of gender responsive training for the teachers and school management and support creating an enabling learning environment in the AIM supported secondary schools. S/he will Also ensure effective delivery of parental engagement to support in increasing access to and completion of quality secondary education for very young adolescents (VYAs) and adolescent girls (AGs) aged 12-17 years.
An ideal candidate for this role is one with strong technical skills and experience in developing and reviewing quality education curriculum content, teachers’ guides, teacher training manuals, including a strong background in training teachers and educators. S/he should have strong training skills, coordination and negotiation skills, be proactive, passionate, resourceful, and enjoy being a team player.
Key Responsibilities:
Technical Support:

Support AIM team in the inception phase activities (in delivering education messages during community mobilization and inception meetings, family meetings, YDC meetings, etc.).
Work closely with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in preparing the MoU templates for the schools. 
Support in obtaining Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with relevant ministries at the regional and/or district/county level, and schools.
Meet with relevant regional and district officials and share the MoU that outlines the key objectives of AIM education pathways and how Ministry of Education and the district will support and allow access to local education departments and schools, and school records.
Support developing/reviewing/updating/adapting, existing teachers’ guide and contents for the teachers and school leadership in the country context in coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BRAC International (BI) technical anchors.
Support developing /reviewing/updating/adapting the training guide on school management and school improvement plans in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors. 
Support developing a training guide for the peer mentors, support groups, and tutoring in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors.
Support AIM program assistants (PAs) to identify Teacher Champions in the schools 
Support the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education to ensure the establishment of a robust system for the smooth transfer of school-related support costs to ensure AGs' financial support to continue their education. 

Direct Operational Support: 

Facilitate training for AIM PAs, teachers, and school leadership on gender responsive pedagogy, mentorship, and tutoring. 
Facilitate training for school leadership, school management/and parent-teacher associations (PTAs) on school improvement planning. 
Work closely with the school administrations, head teachers, teachers and school management committees (SMCs)/PTAs for the inception and introduce the AIM education pathway activities.
Support AIM PAs to do monthly follow-ups of the AIM education pathway interventions for quality program outputs.
Conduct/attend different levels of staff meetings. 
Identify the knowledge gap of programme staff and take necessary steps for their improvement.

Coordination, Planning and Partnership and M&E: 

Support coordination with a range of stakeholders, including teachers, school leadership, school management, parents' teachers association, Government education officials, to support school-related interventions 
Work with the identified Alternative Education providers in the region and coordinate to enrol eligible AIM participants
Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery
Report back to the Government education officials/MoE as outlined in the MoU on activities done by BRAC.

Monitoring, Reporting, Documentation and Communication: 

Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery.
Contribute to program reports and deliverables as required.
Identify and document best practices, most significant change stories, and share this knowledge with colleagues. 
Ensure quality reporting on enabling learning environments at school, and document good practices.
Support regional managers, branch managers, and programme Officers regularly to ensure timely and high-quality programmatic data entry and reporting in the relevant manual and digital MIS (BInsight).
Support the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in the documentation of program wins and success stories / case studies 
Ensure timely preparation and submission of programmatic management information system (MIS), training reports and share project progress reports regularly with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education.

Safeguarding responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation.
Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.

Major Challenges:

Access of hard to reach locations in the communities AIM serves
Coordination with different schools 
Coordination with the BI team in different time zones 
Managing coordination among several team members within the BRAC family.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

Timely achievement of project activities.
Quality of the training guides and content prepared
Efficient and quality delivery of the different AIM education pathway training.
Effective staff, teachers, and school leadership capacity building on gender responsiveness 
Effective use of resources and tools.
Strong partnerships established with schools and the Government education officials 
Individual/specific KPIs as agreed with the supervisor.

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or Postgraduate in Education/ International, Development/ Gender/ Sociology/ Anthropology/ Social Sciences and/or other relevant fields

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Training materials development, staff capacity building, and facilitation skills
Computer literacy and presentation skills
Report writing and documentation of Most Significant Change Stories
Proactive, self-starter and independent worker with the ability to support large teams
Demonstrate commitment to community mobilization work around education, GESI, SRHR, and advocacy work, applying rights-based, human-centered, and survivor-centered approaches.
Exhibit empathy and positive interpersonal skills, including cultural competence.

Experience Requirements:

3-5 years of relevant experience in education training, development of training guide, contents and curriculum, gender equality, social inclusion, community engagement, and school engagement.
Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to teachers’ training module development and execution, and training facilitation
Experience working in integrated programs targeted for adolescent girls and young women is a plus.
Previous experience in the development of Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) messages, tools, and materials for community-based dialogues and other activities.
Experience in conducting advocacy, community mobilization and engagement activities is also an added advantage

Meet with relevant regional and district officials and share the MoU that outlines the key objectives of AIM education pathways and how Ministry of Education and the district will support and allow access to local education departments and schools, and school records.
Support developing/reviewing/updating/adapting, existing teachers’ guide and contents for the teachers and school leadership in the country context in coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BRAC International (BI) technical anchors.
Support developing /reviewing/updating/adapting the training guide on school management and school improvement plans in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors. 
Support developing a training guide for the peer mentors, support groups, and tutoring in close coordination with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education and BI technical anchors.
Support AIM program assistants (PAs) to identify Teacher Champions in the schools 
Support the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education to ensure the establishment of a robust system for the smooth transfer of school-related support costs to ensure AGs' financial support to continue their education. 

Direct Operational Support: 

Facilitate training for AIM PAs, teachers, and school leadership on gender responsive pedagogy, mentorship, and tutoring. 
Facilitate training for school leadership, school management/and parent-teacher associations (PTAs) on school improvement planning. 
Work closely with the school administrations, head teachers, teachers and school management committees (SMCs)/PTAs for the inception and introduce the AIM education pathway activities.
Support AIM PAs to do monthly follow-ups of the AIM education pathway interventions for quality program outputs.
Conduct/attend different levels of staff meetings. 
Identify the knowledge gap of programme staff and take necessary steps for their improvement.

Coordination, Planning and Partnership and M&E: 

Support coordination with a range of stakeholders, including teachers, school leadership, school management, parents' teachers association, Government education officials, to support school-related interventions 
Work with the identified Alternative Education providers in the region and coordinate to enrol eligible AIM participants
Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery
Report back to the Government education officials/MoE as outlined in the MoU on activities done by BRAC.

Monitoring, Reporting, Documentation and Communication: 

Contribute to the design and implementation of a monitoring framework to track progress, assess impact, and inform adjustments of the training plans and delivery.
Contribute to program reports and deliverables as required.
Identify and document best practices, most significant change stories, and share this knowledge with colleagues. 
Ensure quality reporting on enabling learning environments at school, and document good practices.
Support regional managers, branch managers, and programme Officers regularly to ensure timely and high-quality programmatic data entry and reporting in the relevant manual and digital MIS (BInsight).
Support the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education in the documentation of program wins and success stories / case studies 
Ensure timely preparation and submission of programmatic management information system (MIS), training reports and share project progress reports regularly with the AIM Senior Technical Specialist, Education.

Safeguarding responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the programme’s goals on safeguarding implementation.
Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so.

Major Challenges:

Access of hard to reach locations in the communities AIM serves
Coordination with different schools 
Coordination with the BI team in different time zones 
Managing coordination among several team members within the BRAC family.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs):

Timely achievement of project activities.
Quality of the training guides and content prepared
Efficient and quality delivery of the different AIM education pathway training.
Effective staff, teachers, and school leadership capacity building on gender responsiveness 
Effective use of resources and tools.
Strong partnerships established with schools and the Government education officials 
Individual/specific KPIs as agreed with the supervisor.

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree or Postgraduate in Education/ International, Development/ Gender/ Sociology/ Anthropology/ Social Sciences and/or other relevant fields

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Training materials development, staff capacity building, and facilitation skills
Computer literacy and presentation skills
Report writing and documentation of Most Significant Change Stories
Proactive, self-starter and independent worker with the ability to support large teams
Demonstrate commitment to community mobilization work around education, GESI, SRHR, and advocacy work, applying rights-based, human-centered, and survivor-centered approaches.
Exhibit empathy and positive interpersonal skills, including cultural competence.

Experience Requirements:

3-5 years of relevant experience in education training, development of training guide, contents and curriculum, gender equality, social inclusion, community engagement, and school engagement.
Previous experience in providing technical assistance, especially related to teachers’ training module development and execution, and training facilitation
Experience working in integrated programs targeted for adolescent girls and young women is a plus.
Previous experience in the development of Social and Behaviour Change Communication (SBCC) messages, tools, and materials for community-based dialogues and other activities.
Experience in conducting advocacy, community mobilization and engagement activities is also an added advantage

Position: Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration
Job Location: Branch Offices in Muhanga, Ruhango, Nyanza, Huye, Nyamagabe & Nyaruguru Districts
About the Role:
The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration, reporting to the Branch Manager (BM) with dotted reporting to Assistant Regional Accounts Manager, s/he will manage direct branch-level accounts and finance, procurement, coordination, partnership, and administrative staff in the branch (if any), support in overall programme implementation and other assigned activities. This will include day-to-day finance management and implementation, staff-capacity development, financial monitoring, and stakeholder management. She will support the BM to ensure effective and timely program implementation and quality assurance. The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration will also be responsible for overall finance reporting, banking, cash requisition, reporting (MIS, internal, and donor reporting) and supporting other technical and operational activities at the branch level.
Key Duties/Responsibilities:
The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration will be responsible with the following:
Finance and Accounts Related Activities:

Record all Mobile Money deposits by updating the daily register and filling in all relevant vouchers and receipts with the necessary approvals, and ensure they are properly preserved.
Each morning, review with the BM and other POs to determine the day’s expected Mobile Money inflows and plan for proper reconciliation
Share the collection sheets with the relevant POs based on the collection schedule (using VSLA platform) printed collection sheets.
Synchronize collections made by PAs with the accounting system, ensuring accuracy of both the collections and corresponding accounting records.
Submit the cash requisition with the signature of the BM to the regional accounts officer based on the approved activity plan. 
At the end of each business day and month-end, perform required cash reconciliation and check the collection ledger and DCR.
Ensure cash transfer under the Education Pathway.
Track and maintain sufficient cash flow for smooth day-to-day project activities based on the country policy.
Record all branch-level expenses and financial transactions in the accounting system promptly to ensure accurate and timely month-end closing.
Serve as custodian of all financial and procurement documents, records, and information at the branch level, ensuring they are well-organized for research, monitoring, supervision, and audit purposes.

Branch Operations Support:

Occasionally visit AIM clubs, attend YDC meetings, VSLA meetings, and follow up on ongoing different field-level trainings. Livelihood & education participants etc.
Support in the mentors’ recruitment process
Support in club space identification and completion of the agreement, club operations, participants' invitation according to the programme operations manual. 
Support in service provider mapping and establishment of working relationships. 
Support in identification of school(s) to provide education support as per the programme design. 
Help to ensure timely disbursement of livelihood and education pathways support to the participants. 
Custody of all branch-level electronic devices and furniture and maintain stock register.
Act as the technical focal point at the branch level to ensure the use of Binsight and other digital tools.

Technical and Implementation Support:

Help AIM Branch Manager to provide supervisory support to all AIM related program activities at the branch level, ensuring activity planning, roll-out, implementation, and tracking, in accordance with the operations manual; ensure achievement of programmatic targets as per AOP. 
Help BM in team-set up, staff onboarding, training and activity planning of AIM-PAs 
Ensure the use of the Binsight app from the household (HH) survey to all other related activities. 
Provide technical guidance and direction to POs to match participants to livelihood and Education pathways 
Help to ensure timely preparation and submission of MIS, financial and donor reports 
Help in the establishment of market development and value-chain activities

Supervisory, and Coordination Support:

Lead all branch-level activities and serve as the branch’s second-main focal point for internal and external stakeholders
Supervise branch administrative staff (where applicable) e.g. office assistant, providing guidance, training, and performance feedback.
Co-facilitate monthly branch coordination meetings to ensure communication, planning and internal alignment 
Help in monitoring/research and survey (including HH survey) related activities at the branch level
Help/lead in AIM community dialogue(s), workshops, meetings

General Administration Support:

Support the efficient functioning of the Branch office, ensuring a conducive and safe working environment.
Coordinate the provision of office supplies and consumables, ensuring adequate stock levels and timely replenishment in the Branch office.
Implement and maintain effective record-keeping systems for administrative documents and data.
Serve as the primary point of contact for all safety and security matters within the Branch.
Coordinate incident reporting, ensuring timely and thorough documentation of incidents and corrective actions.

Safeguarding Responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the project goals on safeguarding implementation.
Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Finance/Accounts/Business Administration/ Commerce and /or other relevant fields.

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Experience in project management and coordination, including supervision and monitoring, administration, finance, and logistics 
Strong Microsoft Office skills
Strong sense of teamwork and collaboration, and demonstrated ability to build relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Personal qualities of integrity, credibility, and dedication to the mission of BRAC.

Experience Required:

At least 2 years’ experience in national/international development sector, including experience with managing finance and accounts for development programs including microfinance, livelihood, education, agricultural and food security, and/or girl’s and women’s empowerment programs.

Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration

BRAC is the world’s largest, and leading development organization dedicated to poverty alleviation and empowerment of the poor. Initiated in Bangladesh in 1972, BRAC now operates in 11 countries across Asia, Africa. To counter poverty and promote social empowerment, BRAC strategically integrates development programs in microfinance, agriculture, health, education, human rights and legal aid, community empowerment, and more.
BRAC Rwanda Microfinance Company PLC is registered with Rwanda Development Board in September 2018 and was approved license from the National Bank of Rwanda to operate Microfinance and other financial services in Rwanda.

BRAC International is Hiring! Join BRAC International to create opportunities for people to realise their potential. 
Position: Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration
Job Location: Branch Offices in Muhanga, Ruhango, Nyanza, Huye, Nyamagabe & Nyaruguru Districts
About the Role:
The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration, reporting to the Branch Manager (BM) with dotted reporting to Assistant Regional Accounts Manager, s/he will manage direct branch-level accounts and finance, procurement, coordination, partnership, and administrative staff in the branch (if any), support in overall programme implementation and other assigned activities. This will include day-to-day finance management and implementation, staff-capacity development, financial monitoring, and stakeholder management. She will support the BM to ensure effective and timely program implementation and quality assurance. The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration will also be responsible for overall finance reporting, banking, cash requisition, reporting (MIS, internal, and donor reporting) and supporting other technical and operational activities at the branch level.
Key Duties/Responsibilities:
The Officer, Branch Accounts & Administration will be responsible with the following:
Finance and Accounts Related Activities:

Record all Mobile Money deposits by updating the daily register and filling in all relevant vouchers and receipts with the necessary approvals, and ensure they are properly preserved.
Each morning, review with the BM and other POs to determine the day’s expected Mobile Money inflows and plan for proper reconciliation
Share the collection sheets with the relevant POs based on the collection schedule (using VSLA platform) printed collection sheets.
Synchronize collections made by PAs with the accounting system, ensuring accuracy of both the collections and corresponding accounting records.
Submit the cash requisition with the signature of the BM to the regional accounts officer based on the approved activity plan. 
At the end of each business day and month-end, perform required cash reconciliation and check the collection ledger and DCR.
Ensure cash transfer under the Education Pathway.
Track and maintain sufficient cash flow for smooth day-to-day project activities based on the country policy.
Record all branch-level expenses and financial transactions in the accounting system promptly to ensure accurate and timely month-end closing.
Serve as custodian of all financial and procurement documents, records, and information at the branch level, ensuring they are well-organized for research, monitoring, supervision, and audit purposes.

Branch Operations Support:

Occasionally visit AIM clubs, attend YDC meetings, VSLA meetings, and follow up on ongoing different field-level trainings. Livelihood & education participants etc.
Support in the mentors’ recruitment process
Support in club space identification and completion of the agreement, club operations, participants' invitation according to the programme operations manual. 
Support in service provider mapping and establishment of working relationships. 
Support in identification of school(s) to provide education support as per the programme design. 
Help to ensure timely disbursement of livelihood and education pathways support to the participants. 
Custody of all branch-level electronic devices and furniture and maintain stock register.
Act as the technical focal point at the branch level to ensure the use of Binsight and other digital tools.

Technical and Implementation Support:

Help AIM Branch Manager to provide supervisory support to all AIM related program activities at the branch level, ensuring activity planning, roll-out, implementation, and tracking, in accordance with the operations manual; ensure achievement of programmatic targets as per AOP. 
Help BM in team-set up, staff onboarding, training and activity planning of AIM-PAs 
Ensure the use of the Binsight app from the household (HH) survey to all other related activities. 
Provide technical guidance and direction to POs to match participants to livelihood and Education pathways 
Help to ensure timely preparation and submission of MIS, financial and donor reports 
Help in the establishment of market development and value-chain activities

Supervisory, and Coordination Support:

Lead all branch-level activities and serve as the branch’s second-main focal point for internal and external stakeholders
Supervise branch administrative staff (where applicable) e.g. office assistant, providing guidance, training, and performance feedback.
Co-facilitate monthly branch coordination meetings to ensure communication, planning and internal alignment 
Help in monitoring/research and survey (including HH survey) related activities at the branch level
Help/lead in AIM community dialogue(s), workshops, meetings

General Administration Support:

Support the efficient functioning of the Branch office, ensuring a conducive and safe working environment.
Coordinate the provision of office supplies and consumables, ensuring adequate stock levels and timely replenishment in the Branch office.
Implement and maintain effective record-keeping systems for administrative documents and data.
Serve as the primary point of contact for all safety and security matters within the Branch.
Coordinate incident reporting, ensuring timely and thorough documentation of incidents and corrective actions.

Safeguarding Responsibilities:

Ensure the safety of team members from any harm, abuse, neglect, harassment and exploitation to achieve the project goals on safeguarding implementation.
Act as a key source of support, guidance and expertise on safeguarding for establishing a safe working environment.
Practice, promote and endorse the issues of safeguarding policy among team members and ensure the implementation of safeguarding standards in every course of action.
Follow the safeguarding reporting procedure in case any reportable incident takes place, encourage others to do so

Academic Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Finance/Accounts/Business Administration/ Commerce and /or other relevant fields.

Required Skills, Competencies & Knowledge:

Experience in project management and coordination, including supervision and monitoring, administration, finance, and logistics 
Strong Microsoft Office skills
Strong sense of teamwork and collaboration, and demonstrated ability to build relationships with individuals from diverse backgrounds
Personal qualities of integrity, credibility, and dedication to the mission of BRAC.

Experience Required:

At least 2 years’ experience in national/international development sector, including experience with managing finance and accounts for development programs including microfinance, livelihood, education, agricultural and food security, and/or girl’s and women’s empowerment programs.

Employment type: Regular/Fixed-Term
About BRAC International:
BRAC International (BI), a leading non-profit organization, is on a mission to empower people and communities facing poverty, illiteracy, disease, and social injustice. Our vision is to create a world free from exploitation and discrimination, where everyone has the opportunity to realize their potential. We design proven, scalable solutions that equip people with the support and confidence they need to achieve their potential.
BRAC was founded in Bangladesh in 1972 and over the last five decades has grown to become one of the world’s largest non-governmental organisations (NGOs), reaching over 100 million people. We started our first international operation by venturing into Afghanistan in 2002, building on lessons from our work in Bangladesh to support a nation devastated by war. Currently operating in 16 countries across Asia and Africa. Born, proven and led in the Global South, BRAC International brings a unique Southern perspective and commitment to continuous learning, providing a depth of insight, experience and evidence to meet the needs of diverse communities with humility and courage across Asia and Africa. To learn more about BRAC International, please visit (www.bracinternational.org)
Our Core Values:
Integrity: We approach our work with honesty and integrity.
Innovation: We innovate and iterate to improve our impact.
Inclusiveness: We foster inclusion to reach those who need it most.
Effectiveness: We strive for effectiveness to better serve people in poverty.
If you feel you are the right match for the above-mentioned position, please follow the application process to grab your dream opportunity!
Qualified and interested candidates are recommended to email their Resume with a signed cover letter and any supporting documents in a single PDF format mentioning a brief academic background, career summary, core competence, notarized copies of academic qualifications and professional certifications to bracrwandarecruitment@gmail.com.
Please mention the name of the position in the subject bar
Application deadline: 2nd October 2026
Please note that the shortlisting will be done on rolling basis, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
BRAC is committed to safeguarding children, young people and adults, and expects all employees and volunteers to share the same commitment. We believe every stakeholder and every member of the communities we work with has the right to be protected from all forms of harm, abuse, neglect, harassment, and exploitation - regardless of age, race, religion, and gender, status as an individual with a disability or ethnic origin. Therefore, our recruitment policy and procedure include extensive background checks and disclosure of criminal records in order to ensure safeguarding to the fullest extent.
“BRAC International is an equal opportunities employer”

ndangira.title: Senior Resource Development Manager at World Vision International Rwanda
ndangira.title_raw: Senior Resource Development Manager at World Vision International Rwanda : (Deadline 09-10-2026)
ndangira.description:
JOB OPPORTUNITY 
Senior Resource Development Manager
World Vision is a child-focused Christian humanitarian organization implementing development programmes in 30 Districts of Rwanda. Our interventions in the strategic period of 2026-2030 seek to reach 2.5 million of the most vulnerable children. This is done through programming in Child Protection, Education, Nutrition and WASH, and Poverty Alleviation (Resilience and Livelihoods).
World Vision Rwanda seeks to hire a highly qualified, dedicated, and experienced Rwandan national for the role of Senior Resource Development Manager, joining an established and experienced team. This stimulating position incorporates a range of skills and development in multiple areas, allowing for an exciting opportunity for career growth in a dynamic, global organization. It will be based in Kigali at the Head Office and will report to the National Director. 
Purpose of the position:

The Senior Resource Development Manager provides strategic leadership and overall accountability for World Vision Rwanda's resource mobilization and external engagement agenda. The position leads the development and implementation of strategies that secure sustainable and diversified funding, strengthen organizational positioning, and advance strategic relationships that contribute to the achievement of World Vision Rwanda's Strategic Objectives. As a member of the Senior Leadership Team, the Manager provides organizational leadership on resource acquisition, donor engagement, funding diversification, business development, and market positioning across institutional, private sector, philanthropic, and domestic funding streams. The role ensures that World Vision Rwanda is strategically positioned within the development landscape, influences key stakeholders, and secures the resources required to deliver sustainable impact for vulnerable children, families, and communities. The Manager serves as a principal advisor to the National Director and Senior Leadership Team on donor trends, development financing, external relations, strategic opportunities, and organizational growth priorities.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

% of time

Activity

End Results

15%

Strategic Leadership and Organizational Growth

Effective implementation of World Vision Rwanda's Resource Mobilization Strategy, resulting in achievement of organizational resource acquisition objectives.
Diversified and sustainable funding portfolio that supports organizational growth, resilience, and long-term impact.
Strong alignment between resource acquisition priorities and National Strategy objectives, ensuring resources are directed toward strategic priorities.
Enhanced organizational decision-making through timely advisory support on funding opportunities, market trends, and resource mobilization risks.
A culture of innovation, accountability, and resource stewardship embedded across the organization, strengthening funding competitiveness and sustainability.

20%

External Relations, Donor Engagement and Positioning

Enhanced organizational visibility, reputation, and influence among donors, government institutions, development partners, foundations, and private sector stakeholders.
Strong and sustainable strategic relationships established and maintained with senior donor representatives, decision-makers, and key development partners.
World Vision Rwanda positioned as a preferred and credible development partner in national, regional, and international forums.

Increased strategic partnership and resource acquisition opportunities through effective representation, stakeholder engagement, and high-level negotiations.

20%

Resource Acquisition and Business Development (Growing the pipeline and securing new funding)

Annual resource acquisition targets established and achieved, contributing to overall strategic funding goals.
Increased funding secured through proactive business development, donor positioning, and opportunity pursuit.
Strong strategic partnerships, consortiums, and alliances that enhance competitiveness and access to high-value opportunities.
A healthy and forward-looking funding pipeline that supports sustained organizational growth.

30%

Resource Acquisition, Portfolio Performance and Sustainability (Managing and growing the value, quality, and sustainability of the funding portfolio).

A diversified and sustainable funding portfolio that supports long-term organizational impact and resilience.
Improved proposal success rates and funding outcomes through high-quality, competitive, and compliant submissions.
Strong donor retention, stewardship, and strategic partnerships that expand funding opportunities.
Enhanced financial sustainability through diversified revenue streams and continuous improvement in resource mobilization performance.

5%

Technical support, Mentorship and Talent Development

A high-performing, skilled, and motivated Resource Mobilization team capable of delivering World Vision Rwanda's resource acquisition and growth objectives.
Effective workforce planning, succession management, and staff development, ensuring continuity of critical resource mobilization capabilities and leadership pipeline development.
Strong cross-functional collaboration and alignment across Programmes, Operations, Finance, Communications, Support Offices, and other stakeholders in support of resource acquisition goals.
A culture of accountability, continuous learning, and high performance embedded within the Resource Mobilization function, resulting in improved effectiveness, efficiency, and results delivery.

5%

Strategic Advisory and Organizational Leadership

Resource mobilization priorities effectively integrated into organizational strategy, planning, and decision-making.
Senior leadership equipped with timely strategic intelligence and analysis to guide growth, sustainability, and funding decisions.
Enhanced organizational positioning, readiness, and responsiveness to emerging donor, partnership, and development financing trends.
Strengthened organizational influence and visibility through effective representation in strategic national, regional, and global forums.

5%

Other Responsibilities

Effective contribution to National Office leadership, organizational priorities, and strategic initiatives.
Compliance with organizational policies, standards, and regulatory requirements across the Resource Mobilization function.
Successful delivery of special assignments and cross-organizational initiatives as delegated.
Consistent promotion of World Vision's mission, values, and organizational reputation through all resource mobilization activities.

Knowledge/Qualifications for the role

Required Professional Experience

Minimum 7 - 10 years of progressive experience in resource mobilization, donor engagement, business development, strategic partnerships, and grant acquisition, including senior leadership responsibility.
Demonstrated track record of securing significant funding from institutional donors, bilateral and multilateral agencies, UN organizations, foundations, private sector partners, and domestic funding sources.
Proven experience leading resource acquisition and business development functions, including donor positioning, funding pipeline management, partnership development, opportunity prioritization, and strategic funding decisions.
Experience overseeing donor intelligence, portfolio management, funding diversification, and resource mobilization systems to support long-term organizational growth and impact.
Extensive experience building and managing high-level relationships with donors, government institutions, development partners, foundations, private sector leaders, and other strategic stakeholders.
Demonstrated success leading complex proposal development processes, consortium building, negotiations, and high-value funding pursuits involving multidisciplinary teams and multiple stakeholders.
Experience advising senior leadership on donor trends, development financing, funding risks, resource mobilization strategies, and organizational growth opportunities.
Proven leadership experience in developing high-performing teams, strengthening organizational capacity, and driving resource mobilization performance and sustainability.

Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification

Education

Master's Degree in International Development, Business Administration, Economics, Public Policy, International Relations, Communications, Social Sciences, or a related field.
A Bachelor's Degree in a relevant discipline, combined with substantial senior-level resource mobilization and leadership experience, may be considered.

NOTE: If a foreign institution issued the degree, an equivalence certificate from the Rwanda Higher Education Council (HEC) will be required)  
Professional Training

Activity

Position: Planning MEAL Officer
Vacant positions: One (01)

Context of the position: 
SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation.
