ndangira.title_raw: Rwanda Driver (Fixed-Term)  at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 16-12-2026)
ndangira.description:
About One Acre Fund
Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.
Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.
About the Role
Seeking a driver to transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between OAF sites, maintain the fleet and cargo in excellent condition, and provide insights on truck operations and charging to inform future electric truck ownership.
Responsibilities
Cargo Transport

Transport agricultural and non-agricultural inputs between assigned OAF sites, ensuring delivery strictly to the specified locations within set timelines.
Collaborate with the warehouse team to load, offload, and reload trucks, verifying that the physical cargo matches the exact quantity and quality stated on delivery documents.
Secure all materials in transit using appropriate equipment to prevent loss, theft, tampering, or damage (e.g., perforations, wet bags, or torn stitching).
Proactively gather information regarding the location and accessibility of field sites and chargers within the assigned district prior to departure.

Vehicle Maintenance

Conduct weekly vehicle checks, perform minor repairs, and submit maintenance requests to your manager to ensure that the vehicle under their care is kept in good running condition at all times.
Mitigate damage to the truck by avoiding risky routes or driving techniques.
Ensure safety and custody of the vehicles including tools.
Ensure availability of all the required documents/supplies including vehicle insurance, registration, first aid kit, and necessary spare parts in the assigned vehicle.
Ensure that, in the event of an accident involving the vehicle, the necessary steps required by rules and regulations are followed.

Documentation & Communication

Accurately manage all delivery documents, including Delivery Notes, Load Cards, and Truck Management Sheets (TMS). Return fully signed delivery documents to your manager within one (1) business day of delivery. 
Obtain official signatures from authorized OAF representatives at both the originating and destination sites to confirm the exact weight/number of inputs dispatched and received.
Immediately notify your manager via text (or call for urgent cases) in the event of accidents, field staff unavailability, data discrepancies, charging problems, mechanical problems, adverse weather, route accessibility issues, data discrepancies, or if any party refuses to sign the delivery documents.
Communicate regularly relevant trial information, such as GPS coordinates, KM range, battery levels, charging experience, driving experience, road quality, etc.
Ensure that all required driving training is successfully completed and certifications are kept up to date

Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.
Qualifications
Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Valid category C driver’s licence
Experience driving cargo trucks on dirt roads outside of Kigali
Working knowledge of local roads and routes, ability to utilize maps / GPS systems
Working knowledge of electric vehicle mechanics (truck maintenance, interpret truck KM range / battery life)
Sound knowledge of road safety regulations
Effective communication skills (verbal and written) in Kinyarwanda
Punctual and reliable, customer service

Preferred Start Date
As soon as possible
Job Location
Kigali, Rwanda
Benefits
Health insurance, paid time off 
Contract Duration
3 months
Eligibility
This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.
Application Deadline
23 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.
One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.
We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

ndangira.description:
Audit and Accounts Trainee Job Vacancy at HLB Rwanda. 
HLB Rwanda is a leading Accounting and Business Advisory firm in the region with a diverse  client portfolio. The firm is currently sourcing for talent to join our team in the Audit  department and Accounts department. This is a unique opportunity for an ambitious candidate  willing to join a multicultural workforce. The successful candidate will be responsible for the  following: 
Your key responsibilities; 
As an Audit and Accounts Trainee, you will work on various audit engagements in different  industry sectors. You will; 
➢ Develop an understanding of the audit client’s business. 
➢ Interact with the clients in order to collect all the necessary data/information, set-up  and maintain audit files, prepare lead schedules, etc. 
➢ Support the planning, execution and delivery of assurance engagements.
➢ Clearly and accurately document the execution of specific audit procedures as defined  by the engagement objectives, audit client's engagement history, and planned audit  approach. 
➢ Recognize potential audit issues or unusual relationships from basic analysis of the  financial statements and communicate them to the assurance team. 
Qualifications and Competence Required: 
➢ Graduate in the field of accounting and finance. 
➢ At least two years’ experience in audit or accounting environment. 
➢ Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 
➢ Strong drive to excel professionally, and to guide and motivate others.
➢ Advanced written and verbal communication skills. 
➢ Dedicated, innovative, resourceful, analytical and able to work under pressure.
➢ Foster an efficient, innovative and team-oriented work environment. 
Method of Application 
Interested candidates should submit their CV’s and copies of Academic/professional certificates  to; elie@hlbrwanda.com  and copy info@hlbrwanda.com ; using the position as the subject of  the email. Application Deadline is 27th September 2026.

Audit and Accounts Trainee Job Vacancy at HLB Rwanda. 

HLB Rwanda is a leading Accounting and Business Advisory firm in the region with a diverse  client portfolio. The firm is currently sourcing for talent to join our team in the Audit  department and Accounts department. This is a unique opportunity for an ambitious candidate  willing to join a multicultural workforce. The successful candidate will be responsible for the  following: 

Your key responsibilities; 

As an Audit and Accounts Trainee, you will work on various audit engagements in different  industry sectors. You will; 

➢ Develop an understanding of the audit client’s business. 

➢ Interact with the clients in order to collect all the necessary data/information, set-up  and maintain audit files, prepare lead schedules, etc. 

➢ Support the planning, execution and delivery of assurance engagements.

➢ Clearly and accurately document the execution of specific audit procedures as defined  by the engagement objectives, audit client's engagement history, and planned audit  approach. 

➢ Recognize potential audit issues or unusual relationships from basic analysis of the  financial statements and communicate them to the assurance team. 

Qualifications and Competence Required: 

➢ Graduate in the field of accounting and finance. 

➢ At least two years’ experience in audit or accounting environment. 

➢ Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

➢ Strong drive to excel professionally, and to guide and motivate others.

➢ Advanced written and verbal communication skills. 

➢ Dedicated, innovative, resourceful, analytical and able to work under pressure.

➢ Foster an efficient, innovative and team-oriented work environment. 

Method of Application 

Interested candidates should submit their CV’s and copies of Academic/professional certificates  to; elie@hlbrwanda.com  and copy info@hlbrwanda.com ; using the position as the subject of  the email. Application Deadline is 27th September 2026.

ndangira.title_raw: Legal Officer at ECOFLEET SOLUTIONS Ltd : ( Deadline 05-10-2026)
ndangira.description:
ECOFLEET SOLUTIONS LTD JOB DESCRIPTION 
LEGAL OFFICER 

Job Title 
Legal Officer

Reports To 
Head of Legal & Company Secretary

Department 
Legal Department

Location 
Kigali, Rwanda

Job Type 
Full-time

1. ROLE SUMMARY 
The Legal Officer supports the Head of Legal & Company Secretary in providing sound legal advice, drafting and reviewing corporate documents, and managing legal risks to protect the commercial and regulatory interests of Ecofleet Solutions Ltd. 
2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE 
The role involves supporting corporate governance, contract management, regulatory compliance, and litigation processes. The Legal Officer works closely with internal departments and external counsel, reporting directly to the Head of Legal & Company Secretary. 
3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

Draft, review, and negotiate commercial contracts, agreements, and MOUs. 
Provide legal opinions on labor law, commercial transactions, and intellectual property matters. 
Maintain statutory records and ensure timely corporate filings with RDB and relevant authorities. 
Coordinate with external counsel on litigation and represent the company in administrative proceedings where required. 
Review and update internal policies to ensure legal and regulatory compliance. 
Identify and mitigate legal risks across company operations. 

4. WORKING RELATIONSHIPS 
The Legal Officer maintains the following key working relationships:

Relationship 
Nature of Engagement

Head of Legal & Company Secretary
Direct reporting line; legal strategy and escalation of key legal matters.

Internal Departments 
Legal advisory support on contracts, transactions, and compliance matters.

External Counsel 
Coordination on litigation and specialised legal matters.

RDB & Regulatory Authorities
Corporate filings and regulatory compliance.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS 

Legal documents reviewed and returned within 48-72 hours. 
Minimisation of legal exposure and successful out-of-court settlements. 
100% compliance with statutory filing deadlines. 

6. CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS 

Excellent legal drafting and negotiation skills. 
Fluent in English and Kinyarwanda; French is an added advantage. 
Strong interpersonal and presentation skills. 

7. VALUES & CULTURAL FIT 

High integrity and professionalism in legal practice. 
Sound judgement and attention to detail. 
Collaborative approach with internal departments and external counsel. 
Commitment to protecting Ecofleet's legal and commercial interests. 

8. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 
Minimum: 

Bachelor of Laws (LL.B) and Diploma in Legal Practice (DLP). 
Minimum of 4 years of post-qualification legal experience in a corporate environment or law firm.

Preferred: 

Experience in logistics, transport, or fleet management sectors is an advantage.

How to Apply
Applicants should submit their application by email to careers@ecofleet.rw.
Applications should be compiled into one folder or file clearly labeled with the position applied for and must include:

A cover letter addressed to Aubin RUKERA, Chief Executive Officer, Ecofleet Solutions Ltd
A detailed Curriculum Vitae
Certified copies of academic and professional certificates

ECOFLEET SOLUTIONS LTD JOB DESCRIPTION 
DIGITAL INNOVATION & ANALYTICS OFFICER (1) 

Job Title 
Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer

Reports To 
Chief Digital & Experience Officer (CDXO)

Department 
Digital & Experience

Location 
Kigali, Rwanda

Job Type 
Full-time

1. ROLE SUMMARY 
The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer drives data-driven decision-making and innovation across Ecofleet's operations and digital ecosystem. Reporting to the CDXO, the role focuses on transforming data into actionable insights, identifying opportunities for innovation, and supporting the continuous improvement of services, systems, and customer experience. The Officer plays a central role in analytics, reporting, and digital innovation, working across departments to unlock value from data and support strategic and operational performance. 
2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE 
The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer develops and manages data analytics frameworks and reporting systems, analyzes operational, financial, and digital data to generate insights, and identifies and supports the implementation of digital innovation initiatives. The role builds dashboards and visualization tools for decision-making, supports predictive analytics and performance optimization efforts, and promotes a data-driven culture across the organization. 
3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

Collect, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources (FMS, finance systems, digital platforms, operations). 
Develop and maintain dashboards and reports for operational and executive use. 
Identify trends, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities across fleet operations and customer experience. 
Support development of predictive models (e.g., demand forecasting, maintenance planning, route optimization). 
Collaborate with the M&E Officer to align KPI tracking and reporting frameworks. 
Work with the FMS Product Officer and Platform & UX Officer to enhance data availability and usability. 
Explore and recommend innovative digital solutions (automation, AI, data tools) to improve performance. 
Support pilot projects and innovation initiatives with data analysis and evaluation.
Ensure data quality, consistency, and governance across systems. 
Present insights and recommendations to leadership in a clear and actionable manner. 

4.WORKING RELATIONSHIPS 
The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer maintains the following key working relationships: 

Relationship 
Nature of Engagement

CDXO 
Strategic direction on analytics and innovation priorities.

FMS Product Officer 
Access to fleet data and system-based insights.

Platform & UX Officer 
User behavior analytics and experience optimization.

Enterprise IT & Cybersecurity Officer
Data infrastructure, security, and governance.

M&E Officer 
Alignment of KPIs, reporting standards, and performance frameworks.

COO 
Operational insights and performance optimization.

CFO 
Financial analytics and cost optimization.

CSEO 
Sustainability metrics and environmental performance tracking.

Data & Analytics Solution Providers
Tools, platforms, and technical support.

Consultants, Research & Innovation Partners
Support on analytics and innovation initiatives.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS 

Availability of accurate, timely, and actionable analytics dashboards. 
Increased use of data in operational and strategic decision-making. 
Measurable improvements driven by data insights (efficiency, cost savings, service quality). 
Successful implementation of innovation initiatives and pilots. 
Strong alignment between analytics outputs and business needs. 
Improved data quality and consistency across systems. 

6. CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS 

Strong analytical and data interpretation skills. 
Proficiency in data tools (Excel, Power BI, SQL, or similar). 
Understanding of data modeling, visualization, and reporting. 
Ability to translate data into actionable insights. 
Curiosity and innovation mindset.
Strong communication and presentation skills. 
Attention to detail and data accuracy. 

7. VALUES & CULTURAL FIT 

Data-driven mindset and commitment to evidence-based decisions. 
Curiosity and continuous improvement. 
Collaboration across departments. 
Accountability and ownership of insights and outcomes. 
Passion for innovation in mobility and public service. 

8. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 
Minimum: 

Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field. 
3-5 years' experience in data analysis, analytics, or digital innovation roles. 

Preferred: 

Experience in transport, logistics, energy, or infrastructure sectors. 
Strong skills in Power BI, SQL, Python, or similar tools. 
Experience with predictive analytics or machine learning (basic to intermediate). 
Experience working with cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders. 
Exposure to digital transformation or innovation projects.

The Officer plays a central role in analytics, reporting, and digital innovation, working across departments to unlock value from data and support strategic and operational performance. 

2. SCOPE OF THE ROLE 

The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer develops and manages data analytics frameworks and reporting systems, analyzes operational, financial, and digital data to generate insights, and identifies and supports the implementation of digital innovation initiatives. The role builds dashboards and visualization tools for decision-making, supports predictive analytics and performance optimization efforts, and promotes a data-driven culture across the organization. 

3. KEY RESPONSIBILITIES 

  • Collect, clean, and analyze data from multiple sources (FMS, finance systems, digital platforms, operations). 
  • Develop and maintain dashboards and reports for operational and executive use. 
  • Identify trends, inefficiencies, and improvement opportunities across fleet operations and customer experience. 
  • Support development of predictive models (e.g., demand forecasting, maintenance planning, route optimization). 
  • Collaborate with the M&E Officer to align KPI tracking and reporting frameworks. 
  • Work with the FMS Product Officer and Platform & UX Officer to enhance data availability and usability. 
  • Explore and recommend innovative digital solutions (automation, AI, data tools) to improve performance. 
  • Support pilot projects and innovation initiatives with data analysis and evaluation.
  • Ensure data quality, consistency, and governance across systems. 
  • Present insights and recommendations to leadership in a clear and actionable manner. 

4.WORKING RELATIONSHIPS 

The Digital Innovation & Analytics Officer maintains the following key working relationships: 

Relationship  Nature of Engagement
CDXO  Strategic direction on analytics and innovation priorities.
FMS Product Officer  Access to fleet data and system-based insights.
Platform & UX Officer  User behavior analytics and experience optimization.
Enterprise IT & Cybersecurity Officer Data infrastructure, security, and governance.
M&E Officer  Alignment of KPIs, reporting standards, and performance frameworks.
COO  Operational insights and performance optimization.
CFO  Financial analytics and cost optimization.
CSEO  Sustainability metrics and environmental performance tracking.
Data & Analytics Solution Providers Tools, platforms, and technical support.
Consultants, Research & Innovation Partners Support on analytics and innovation initiatives.

5. INDICATORS OF SUCCESS 

  • Availability of accurate, timely, and actionable analytics dashboards. 
  • Increased use of data in operational and strategic decision-making. 
  • Measurable improvements driven by data insights (efficiency, cost savings, service quality). 
  • Successful implementation of innovation initiatives and pilots. 
  • Strong alignment between analytics outputs and business needs. 
  • Improved data quality and consistency across systems. 

6. CORE COMPETENCIES & SKILLS 

  • Strong analytical and data interpretation skills. 
  • Proficiency in data tools (Excel, Power BI, SQL, or similar). 
  • Understanding of data modeling, visualization, and reporting. 
  • Ability to translate data into actionable insights. 
  • Curiosity and innovation mindset.
  • Strong communication and presentation skills. 
  • Attention to detail and data accuracy. 

7. VALUES & CULTURAL FIT 

  • Data-driven mindset and commitment to evidence-based decisions. 
  • Curiosity and continuous improvement. 
  • Collaboration across departments. 
  • Accountability and ownership of insights and outcomes. 
  • Passion for innovation in mobility and public service. 

8. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

Minimum: 

  • Bachelor's degree in Data Science, Statistics, Economics, Engineering, Information Systems, or related field. 
  • 3-5 years' experience in data analysis, analytics, or digital innovation roles. 

Preferred: 

  • Experience in transport, logistics, energy, or infrastructure sectors. 
  • Strong skills in Power BI, SQL, Python, or similar tools. 
  • Experience with predictive analytics or machine learning (basic to intermediate). 
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders. 
  • Exposure to digital transformation or innovation projects.

How to Apply

Applicants should submit their application by email to careers@ecofleet.rw.

Applications should be compiled into one folder or file clearly labeled with the position applied for and must include:

  • A cover letter addressed to Aubin RUKERA, Chief Executive Officer, Ecofleet Solutions Ltd
  • A detailed Curriculum Vitae
  • Certified copies of academic and professional certificates

ndangira.title_raw: 4 Job Positions of Electrical Technician at Central University Hospital of Kigali (CHUK): (Deadline Sep 28, 2026)
ndangira.description:
Job responsibilities
Install, maintain, test, and repair hospital electrical systems and equipment. Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on electrical installations. Inspect electrical panels, distribution boards, cables, switches, sockets, lighting, and protective devices. Troubleshoot electrical faults and restore power safely and promptly. Maintain main power supply, generators, UPS systems, batteries, and emergency power systems. Maintain normal and emergency lighting systems, including lighting in operating theatres, wards, laboratories, and other critical areas. Test and maintain electrical protection systems such as circuit breakers, fuses, earthing, and surge protection. Monitor electrical loads and identify potential overloads or unsafe conditions. Carry out electrical installations for new buildings, renovations, and hospital equipment. Support the installation and connection of medical and non-medical equipment in coordination with biomedical and engineering teams. Respond to electrical emergencies and power failures, particularly in critical clinical departments. Carry out routine inspections and electrical safety testing. Read and interpret electrical drawings, wiring diagrams, and technical specifications. Maintain accurate records of inspections, repairs, maintenance, faults, and electrical test results. Assist in energy-efficiency initiatives and monitor unnecessary power consumption. Supervise or coordinate electrical contractors when required. Ensure all electrical work follows applicable electrical codes, occupational-safety requirements, and hospital procedures. Maintain electrical tools, testing instruments, spare parts, and equipment in good condition.

Qualifications

Advanced Diploma in Electrical Engineering,
0 Year of relevant experience

Advanced Diploma (A1) in Renewable Energy
0 Year of relevant experience

Knowledge to advise on the electrical power aspects of new equipment and systems;

Knowledge of electrical or electronic parts and hardware on hospital equipment

ndangira.title: 4 Job Positions of Laundry Machine Operator/A1 at Central University Hospital of Kigali (CHUK)
ndangira.title_raw: 4 Job Positions of Laundry Machine Operator/A1 at Central University Hospital of Kigali (CHUK): (Deadline Sep 28, 2026)
ndangira.description:
Job responsibilities
Operate industrial washing machines, dryers, extractors, ironing machines, and other laundry equipment. Sort hospital linen according to type, colour, level of contamination, and washing requirements. Load and unload laundry machines safely and according to equipment capacity. Select appropriate washing programs, temperatures, chemicals, and cycle times. Ensure contaminated and heavily soiled linen is handled according to hospital infection-control procedures. Monitor machines during operation and identify unusual noise, vibration, leakage, overheating, or other faults. Report equipment breakdowns and technical problems to the maintenance or engineering team. Perform routine cleaning and basic operator-level maintenance of laundry machines. Ensure correct use and storage of laundry detergents, disinfectants, and other chemicals. Transfer clean linen safely to drying, ironing, folding, and storage areas. Operate industrial pressing, ironing, folding, and finishing equipment where required. Maintain cleanliness and organization of the laundry area. Follow hospital infection-prevention, occupational-health, and safety procedures. Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) when handling contaminated linen or chemicals. Avoid mixing clean and dirty linen and maintain proper separation between clean and contaminated areas. Record laundry quantities, machine cycles, chemical usage, and equipment problems where required. Assist in identifying damaged linen and separating items requiring repair or disposal. Ensure clean linen is properly folded, packaged, stored, and delivered to hospital departments. Report shortages of detergents, linen, PPE, and other laundry supplies. Work closely with nursing, housekeeping, infection-control, and maintenance teams.

Qualifications

Advanced Diploma in Mechanical Engineering
2 Years of relevant experience

Advanced Degree in Biomedical Engineering
2 Years of relevant experience

Advanced Diploma in Electromechanical Engineering
2 Years of relevant experience

Advanced diploma in clinical Engineering
2 Years of relevant experience

Understanding the field of biomedical engineering and its contribution to effective healthcare services

ndangira.description:
Job Description

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Program Overview
The Government of Rwanda (GoR) strives to achieve Universal Health Coverage (UHC) by enabling equitable access to quality health services for the population as outlined in the Fourth Health Sector Strategic Plan (HSSP IV). This commitment has been made against a backdrop of rising health care costs and uncertainty around the future availability of donor funding and calls for improved health sector sustainability. Acknowledging this, the Government aims to employ effective, equitable, efficient, and sustainable health care financing and systems strengthening, emphasizing primary health care as the cornerstone of a strong and sustainable health system.
CHAI Rwanda’s Health System Strengthening (HSS) programs work on a day-to-day basis with Government leadership in the Ministry of Health (MoH) and the Rwanda Social Security Board (RSSB). The goal of those programs is to support the Government to accelerate progress towards UHC by ensuring the sustainable delivery of quality, essential health services. This includes designing and implementing national Primary Health Care (PHC) reforms from health centre level down to community health, to increase health workforce availability, to prioritize and sustainably finance essential services. It also aims to support improved management, financing, and delivery of quality primary health care.
Position Overview
CHAI currently seeks an Associate, Data Science to work with the Ministry of Health (MOH), reporting directly to the head of data science at the National Health Intelligence Centre to help improve the quality, governance, and use of evidence on policy decision-making. S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI supported initiatives.
The Associate, Data Science is responsible for leading advanced data analytics, statistical modelling, and applied machine learning across priority public health and clinical domains. The role ensures that health data is transformed into high-quality, reliable, explainable, and decision-ready intelligence that informs AI development, policy decisions, and health system's performance improvement. This role serves as the technical bridge between raw health data, AI models, and real-world decision-making, ensuring scientific rigour, reproducibility, and national-scale usability.
This is a top government priority for MOH, and the Associate, Data Scientist will therefore be seconded to the MOH/NHIC, S/He also reports in parallel to CHAI, HSS digital health program manager for specific CHAI-supported initiatives.

Responsibilities

Advanced Data Analytics and Statistical Modelling

Lead advanced descriptive, predictive, and inferential analyses across clinical, surveillance, and health systems datasets.
Develop and validate predictive models, risk stratification algorithms, forecasting models, epidemiological and operational analytics.
Apply rigorous statistical methods, hypothesis testing, and causal inference techniques to support decision-making.
Ensure all analytics are clinically interpretable, policy-relevant, and scientifically defensible.

Feature Engineering & Machine Learning Support

Design robust feature engineering pipelines from EMRs, HMIS, LMIS and surveillance platforms.
Support AI Engineers with high-quality training datasets, feature selection, bias detection and data representativeness testing.
Contribute to development of machine learning models, particularly in tabular health data, time-series forecasting and population-level risk prediction.

Data Quality, Governance, and Integrity

Lead implementation of data quality frameworks, completeness, consistency, accuracy, and timeliness checks.
Perform data audits, outlier detection, bias and missing data analysis.
Ensure compliance with national health data governance standards, privacy and ethical data use policies.
Maintain full data documentation, metadata standards, and lineage tracking.

Health Systems Intelligence & Decision Support

Develop decision-support analytics and public health dashboards for disease burden tracking, resource allocation and service delivery optimization.
Translate analytical outputs into policy briefs, executive dashboards, technical report.
Ensure outputs are actionable, explainable, and aligned with the national health priorities.

Data Engineering Support and Pipeline Optimization

Work closely with Data engineers, integration teams and AI engineers to ensure analytics assets are scalable, reproducible and production ready.
Support data pipeline optimization, ETL quality validation and real-time and batch processing readiness.

Mentorship, Capacity Building & Collaboration

Mentor junior data scientists and analysts.
Lead internal analytics communities of practice, code reviews and methodology workshops.
Serve as a technical reviewer for analytics protocols, research designs and data science deliverables.

Innovation and Continuous Improvement

Stay current with advances in Machine Learning, Statistical Science, Health Analytics, Artificial Intelligence and Causal Inference trends.
Propose innovative analytics and data science use cases for public health, service delivery, health financing, supply chain and logistics for pharmaceuticals and disease surveillance.

Qualifications

M.Sc. degree in relevant discipline (Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Actuarial Science, Operations Research, Statistics, Epidemiology, Health Informatics).
5–8 years of professional experience in the field of advanced analytics and/or applied statistics preferably with Data Science applications.
Solid mathematical foundation and knowledge of various statistical methods (e.g. regression, classification, clustering, experimental design, modelling, advanced forecasting).
Proven experience working with large-scale datasets, regulated data environments, preferably within a health domain.
Strong proficiency in data visualization, demonstrated experience in Python, R, SQL, and working with structured, semi-structured and unstructured datasets.
Ability to focus on vaguely defined problems requiring the application of a creative approach.
Strong teamwork skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for coordinating across teams.
Ability to mentor and lead teams in a fast-paced and changing environment.

Application Procedure
After submitting your CV (maximum 3 pages) through this link, please email a letter of interest (maximum 1 page) outlining how your background meets the requirements outlined above to chairwandarecruiting@clintonhealthaccess.org with " Associate, Data Scientist " in the subject line.
The deadline for applications is October 12, 2026. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
In compliance with the data protection law of Rwanda and by submitting your application and CV, you explicitly consent to the collection, processing, and storage of your personal data by Clinton Health Access Initiative for the sole purpose of managing and conducting the recruitment process for the position for which you have applied.

ndangira.description:
1. Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation at SOS Children's Villages Rwanda: ( Deadline 27-09-2026)
VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
Position: Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation
Vacant positions: One (01)
Download Travel Guides
Type of contract: Fixed term
Working location: National Office
Supervisor: Deputy National Director - Operations
Deadline: 27th September 2026
Context of the position: 
SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.
JOB PURPOSE
To move ICT from 'fixing laptops' to 'leveraging technology' for social impact. The Senior Manager, ICT and Programmes Digitalisation leads SOS Rwanda's ICT function and drives the organisation's digital transformation agenda, designing and implementing ICT strategy, managing all ICT systems and infrastructure, leading the digitalisation of programme and operational workflows, implementing secure digital case management platforms, ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, and building staff digital literacy across all four Program Areas.
Resume writing service
The position is the functional supervisor of the ICT Administrator in Kigali and provides technical oversight to location-level ICT focal points.
Main clients: 

Deputy National Director for Operations
National Director
All National Management Team (NMT) members
Head of Finance — ERP and financial systems
Head of MEAL — digital MEL platforms
Head of HROD — HRIS systems
Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics — procurement systems
Programme teams across all four area offices
SOS Regional ICT Advisor (ESAF) and SOS International ICT teams
ICT Administrator- Kigali (direct report)

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:
ICT Strategy and Governance

Develop, implement, and update SOS Rwanda's ICT strategy — aligned with SOS Strategy 2030, MA Strategic Plan 2023–2027, and global SOS ICT standards.
Define national ICT budgets, procurement plans, and multi-year ICT investment roadmaps.
Develop and implement ICT policies and standards — covering architecture, security, disaster recovery, procurement, and service provision.
Participate in regional ICT knowledge-sharing processes and coordinate with the SOS ESAF ICT Advisor on global standards and initiatives.
Lead ICT governance — including vendor management, service level agreements, and ICT committee oversight.

Programmes Digitalisation & Digital Case Management
Download Travel Guides

Implement and manage a secure, cloud-based digital case management platform for tracking child progress — ensuring data privacy and compliance with Rwanda data protection laws and SOS-KDI data protection rules.
Lead the digitalisation of SOS Rwanda's programme functions — introducing digital case management, beneficiary tracking, and electronic documentation workflows across all four locations.
Equip field staff with mobile tools for real-time community reporting — reducing the 'paperwork lag' and improving data quality.
Drive paperless operations across all locations — designing change management plans that support staff adoption of new digital tools.
Collaborate with the Director of Strategy and Programme Implementation and the MEAL function to align digitalisation initiatives with programme quality and RBM needs.
Explore, evaluate, and pilot AI adoption and knowledge management tools that enhance programme decision-making and organisational efficiency.

 ERP, HRIS and Operational Systems

Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of SOS Rwanda's ERP system — ensuring integration across finance, procurement, HR, and programme functions.
Manage the HRIS system — ensuring data integrity, user access management, and alignment with HR processes.
Lead the digitisation of procurement and supply chain systems in coordination with the Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics.
Ensure all ICT systems are properly integrated, reducing data silos and enabling organisation-wide reporting and analytics.

Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and Business Continuity

Manage SOS Rwanda's IT network and server infrastructure across all locations — ensuring 99%+ system uptime, reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness.
Develop and implement a comprehensive cybersecurity framework — including data protection, access control, threat monitoring, and incident response — ensuring the cybersecurity audit score meets SOS-KDI standards.
Ensure compliance with SOS-KDI data protection rules and Rwanda data protection regulations, including the privacy of child and family records.
Design and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans — ensuring operational resilience in the event of system failures.

Digital Literacy & Capacity Building
Form An LLC

Build digital literacy across SOS Rwanda — designing and delivering ICT training programmes for staff at all levels and locations.
Supervise the ICT Administrator and provide technical oversight to location ICT focal points.
Coach programme and operations staff on effective use of digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and case management.
Train community partners and staff on using technology for education, health monitoring, and economic strengthening.

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements:
Education & Professional Qualifications

Master’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or related field (Master's preferred for Grade 5).
ITIL, PMP, or relevant technical certifications required (Grade 5 requirement).
Cybersecurity certification (CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or equivalent) is a strong advantage.

Professional Experience

Minimum of 7 years of progressive ICT experience; 3+ years in senior ICT leadership or digital transformation role.
Demonstrated experience leading digital transformation initiatives in an INGO, NGO, or complex multi-site organisation.
Proven experience with ERP systems (SOS ERP, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent) and HRIS platforms.
Strong track record in cybersecurity management, data protection, and ICT governance.
Experience with ICT4D tools — digital case management, mobile data collection, cloud platforms.
Experience working across multiple sites and geographically dispersed teams.

Skills & Competencies
Download Travel Guides

Digital Transformation Strategy and Programme Digitisation.
ICT Infrastructure Management and Systems Architecture.
Data Governance and Cybersecurity.
ERP Systems Management and Integration.
Vendor Management and contract administration.
Strong change management and adult learning facilitation skills.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
Good understanding of programme monitoring, MEAL, and data analytics.
Fluent English; Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.
Commitment to SOS values and ethical use of data and technology in child-related programmes.

How to apply 
The interested Candidates in this position should send a detailed Curriculum Vitae with three (3) traceable professional references, application letter , Rwandan national Identity Card and academic certificates/degrees to sos.recruitment@sos-rwanda.org and properly fill the application form found via the followingLINKby not later than 27th September, 2026 at 5:00 pm Kigali time. 
Please mention in the subject of your email “Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalization”.
Female candidates are encouraged to apply, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
“SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda/ International holds strict child safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for conducts of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring decisions will give due emphasize to assessing candidates value congruence and thorough background checks, police clearance reference check processes”. 
Done in Kigali on 17th September 2026.
Jean Bosco KWIZERA
National Director

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
Position: Front Office Officer
Vacant positions: One (01)
Type of contract: Fixed term
Working location: National Office
Supervisor: Head of HR and Organisational Development
Deadline: 27th September 2026
Context of the position: 
SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Front Office Officer, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.
JOB PURPOSE
The main role for this position is to provide professional, efficient, and welcoming front-office and administrative support by managing the reception area, receiving and directing visitors and calls, handling correspondence, and providing timely assistance to staff and external stakeholders. The Front Office Officer ensures effective communication and smooth day-to-day front-office operations while maintaining a professional image of the organization and safeguarding confidential information.
Main clients: 

All SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda staff and departments
All visitors, guests, and members of the public coming to SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
Children, young people, families, and other programme participants visiting the organization
Government institutions, partners, donors, service providers, and other external stakeholders
Candidates, consultants, and other individuals visiting SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda for official purposes

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:
The Front Office Officer is responsible for managing the reception area and serving as the first point of contact for visitors, staff, partners, and other stakeholders. The position ensures professional handling of telephone calls, correspondence, visitors, and general inquiries while providing timely administrative support. The officer maintains accurate front-office records, ensures compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, and security procedures, and contributes to creating a welcoming and professional image of SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda. Below are the details:
 Reception and Customer Service

Receive and welcome all visitors, guests, and stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner.
Identify visitors and direct them to the appropriate staff members or departments.
Ensure that visitors receive timely and accurate information and assistance.
Maintain a professional, clean, and welcoming reception environment.
Handle inquiries and provide appropriate responses or referrals.

Telephone and Communication Management

Receive and manage incoming telephone calls and direct them to the appropriate staff members.
Take and relay messages accurately and promptly.
Manage general front-office email inquiries and ensure that correspondence is directed to the relevant departments.
Support effective communication between staff, visitors, and external stakeholders.

Visitor and Front Office Administration

Maintain accurate records of visitors, appointments, deliveries, and other front-office activities.
Manage visitor access in accordance with organizational security and safeguarding procedures.
Coordinate appointments and meeting arrangements as required.
Receive and distribute incoming correspondence, documents, and deliveries.
Maintain an organized filing system for front-office records.

Administrative Support

Provide general administrative support to the Administration and other departments as assigned.
Support the preparation and coordination of meetings, events, and official visits.
Assist with photocopying, scanning, printing, document distribution, and other routine administrative tasks.
Support the coordination of office supplies and other front-office requirements.

Safeguarding, Confidentiality and Security

Ensure that all visitors and stakeholders are treated in accordance with SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda's safeguarding standards and procedures.
Maintain confidentiality of organizational, staff, visitor, and programme-related information.
Immediately report any safeguarding, security, or other concerns through the appropriate channels.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and health and safety requirements.

Professional Representation

Serve as the first point of contact for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and promote a professional and positive image of the organization.
Maintain professional conduct and demonstrate respect, integrity, and courtesy in all interactions.
Build positive working relationships with staff, visitors, partners, government representatives, and other stakeholders.

Reporting and Other Responsibilities

Prepare routine front-office reports and maintain relevant records as required.
Monitor and report issues affecting the smooth operation of the reception area.
Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the supervisor.

Child Protection Policy

At all times, avoid actions or behaviour that could be construed as poor or potentially abusive practice. 
Report any child safeguarding concerns immediately in accordance with the organizational’s Child Protection Policy
Promote and uphold the organisation’s values and child safeguarding principles in all interactions and decision – making

Data Protection Policy.

At all times ensure that personal data of SOS Children’s Villages beneficiaries and their families as well as SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda co-workers is handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing SOS Children’s Villages.
Ensure that personal sponsor information and data used and administered for the benefit of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda, is stored and transferred securely, handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing data protection laws. Donor data will remain under the control of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda and shall not be forwarded to or swapped with other organizations.

Required key skills set.
Must have the following:

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Strong customer service and reception skills
Good organizational and time-management skills
Professional, courteous, and welcoming attitude
Good telephone and email communication skills
Attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information
Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications
Ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds
Problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure

Formal qualifications 

Education: Diploma in Front Office Management, Business Admin, or related field
Professional Qualification: Customer Service certification preferred

 Experience requirements 

Experience: 3+ years reception/front office experience; corporate environment
Skills & Competencies: Reception Management, Telephone Etiquette, Visitor Management, Mail Handling, Office Administration, Professional Presentation, Customer Service Orientation, English & Kinyarwanda fluency.

How to apply 
The interested Candidates in this position should send a detailed Curriculum Vitae with three (3) traceable professional references, application letter , Rwandan national Identity Card and academic certificates/degrees to sos.recruitment@sos-rwanda.org and properly fill the application form found via the followingLINK by not later than 27th September, 2026 at 5:00 pm Kigali time. 
Please mention in the subject of your email “Front Office Officer”.
Female candidates are encouraged to apply, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
“SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda/ International holds strict child safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for conducts of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring decisions will give due emphasize to assessing candidates value congruence and thorough background checks, police clearance reference check processes”. 
Done in Kigali on 17th September 2026.
Jean Bosco KWIZERA
National Director

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
Position: Front Office Officer
Vacant positions: One (01)
Type of contract: Fixed term
Working location: National Office
Supervisor: Head of HR and Organisational Development
Deadline: 27th September 2026
Context of the position: 
SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Front Office Officer, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.
JOB PURPOSE
The main role for this position is to provide professional, efficient, and welcoming front-office and administrative support by managing the reception area, receiving and directing visitors and calls, handling correspondence, and providing timely assistance to staff and external stakeholders. The Front Office Officer ensures effective communication and smooth day-to-day front-office operations while maintaining a professional image of the organization and safeguarding confidential information.
Main clients: 

All SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda staff and departments
All visitors, guests, and members of the public coming to SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda
Children, young people, families, and other programme participants visiting the organization
Government institutions, partners, donors, service providers, and other external stakeholders
Candidates, consultants, and other individuals visiting SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda for official purposes

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:
The Front Office Officer is responsible for managing the reception area and serving as the first point of contact for visitors, staff, partners, and other stakeholders. The position ensures professional handling of telephone calls, correspondence, visitors, and general inquiries while providing timely administrative support. The officer maintains accurate front-office records, ensures compliance with safeguarding, confidentiality, and security procedures, and contributes to creating a welcoming and professional image of SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda. Below are the details:
 Reception and Customer Service

Receive and welcome all visitors, guests, and stakeholders in a professional and courteous manner.
Identify visitors and direct them to the appropriate staff members or departments.
Ensure that visitors receive timely and accurate information and assistance.
Maintain a professional, clean, and welcoming reception environment.
Handle inquiries and provide appropriate responses or referrals.

Telephone and Communication Management

Receive and manage incoming telephone calls and direct them to the appropriate staff members.
Take and relay messages accurately and promptly.
Manage general front-office email inquiries and ensure that correspondence is directed to the relevant departments.
Support effective communication between staff, visitors, and external stakeholders.

Visitor and Front Office Administration

Maintain accurate records of visitors, appointments, deliveries, and other front-office activities.
Manage visitor access in accordance with organizational security and safeguarding procedures.
Coordinate appointments and meeting arrangements as required.
Receive and distribute incoming correspondence, documents, and deliveries.
Maintain an organized filing system for front-office records.

Administrative Support

Provide general administrative support to the Administration and other departments as assigned.
Support the preparation and coordination of meetings, events, and official visits.
Assist with photocopying, scanning, printing, document distribution, and other routine administrative tasks.
Support the coordination of office supplies and other front-office requirements.

Safeguarding, Confidentiality and Security

Ensure that all visitors and stakeholders are treated in accordance with SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda's safeguarding standards and procedures.
Maintain confidentiality of organizational, staff, visitor, and programme-related information.
Immediately report any safeguarding, security, or other concerns through the appropriate channels.
Ensure compliance with organizational policies, procedures, and health and safety requirements.

Professional Representation

Serve as the first point of contact for SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda and promote a professional and positive image of the organization.
Maintain professional conduct and demonstrate respect, integrity, and courtesy in all interactions.
Build positive working relationships with staff, visitors, partners, government representatives, and other stakeholders.

Reporting and Other Responsibilities

Prepare routine front-office reports and maintain relevant records as required.
Monitor and report issues affecting the smooth operation of the reception area.
Perform any other duties relevant to the position as assigned by the supervisor.

Child Protection Policy

At all times, avoid actions or behaviour that could be construed as poor or potentially abusive practice. 
Report any child safeguarding concerns immediately in accordance with the organizational’s Child Protection Policy
Promote and uphold the organisation’s values and child safeguarding principles in all interactions and decision – making

Data Protection Policy.

At all times ensure that personal data of SOS Children’s Villages beneficiaries and their families as well as SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda co-workers is handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing SOS Children’s Villages.
Ensure that personal sponsor information and data used and administered for the benefit of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda, is stored and transferred securely, handled confidentially and in accordance with prevailing data protection laws. Donor data will remain under the control of SOS Children’s Villages in Rwanda and shall not be forwarded to or swapped with other organizations.

Required key skills set.
Must have the following:

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
Strong customer service and reception skills
Good organizational and time-management skills
Professional, courteous, and welcoming attitude
Good telephone and email communication skills
Attention to detail and ability to maintain accurate records
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive information
Good computer skills, including Microsoft Office applications
Ability to work effectively with people from diverse backgrounds
Problem-solving skills and ability to work under pressure

Formal qualifications 

Education: Diploma in Front Office Management, Business Admin, or related field
Professional Qualification: Customer Service certification preferred

 Experience requirements 

Experience: 3+ years reception/front office experience; corporate environment
Skills & Competencies: Reception Management, Telephone Etiquette, Visitor Management, Mail Handling, Office Administration, Professional Presentation, Customer Service Orientation, English & Kinyarwanda fluency.

How to apply 
The interested Candidates in this position should send a detailed Curriculum Vitae with three (3) traceable professional references, application letter , Rwandan national Identity Card and academic certificates/degrees to sos.recruitment@sos-rwanda.org and properly fill the application form found via the followingLINK by not later than 27th September, 2026 at 5:00 pm Kigali time. 
Please mention in the subject of your email “Front Office Officer”.
Female candidates are encouraged to apply, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
“SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda/ International holds strict child safeguarding principles and a zero-tolerance policy for conducts of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse in the workplace and other places where the organization’s activities are rendered. Parallel to technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring decisions will give due emphasize to assessing candidates value congruence and thorough background checks, police clearance reference check processes”. 
Done in Kigali on 17th September 2026.
Jean Bosco KWIZERA
National Director

Position: Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation
Vacant positions: One (01)
Type of contract: Fixed term
Working location: National Office
Supervisor: Deputy National Director - Operations
Deadline: 27th September 2026
Context of the position: 
SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is an independent member association affiliated to the SOS Federation. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda leverages existing community resources to strengthen quality childcare and protection through a holistic continuum of care tailored to orphans, vulnerable children, and their families. SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda actively advocates for the promotion of childcare and child protection. In Rwanda, SOS Children’s Villages operates in four Program Areas based in Gasabo, Gicumbi, Kayonza and Nyamagabe. To further fulfil the above-mentioned responsibilities, SOS Children’s Villages Rwanda is seeking for a competent Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalisation, to base at its National Office Kigali, Kinyinya.
JOB PURPOSE
To move ICT from 'fixing laptops' to 'leveraging technology' for social impact. The Senior Manager, ICT and Programmes Digitalisation leads SOS Rwanda's ICT function and drives the organisation's digital transformation agenda, designing and implementing ICT strategy, managing all ICT systems and infrastructure, leading the digitalisation of programme and operational workflows, implementing secure digital case management platforms, ensuring cybersecurity and data protection, and building staff digital literacy across all four Program Areas.
The position is the functional supervisor of the ICT Administrator in Kigali and provides technical oversight to location-level ICT focal points.
Main clients: 

Deputy National Director for Operations
National Director
All National Management Team (NMT) members
Head of Finance — ERP and financial systems
Head of MEAL — digital MEL platforms
Head of HROD — HRIS systems
Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics — procurement systems
Programme teams across all four area offices
SOS Regional ICT Advisor (ESAF) and SOS International ICT teams
ICT Administrator- Kigali (direct report)

Key Performance Areas and Main Responsibilities:
ICT Strategy and Governance

Develop, implement, and update SOS Rwanda's ICT strategy — aligned with SOS Strategy 2030, MA Strategic Plan 2023–2027, and global SOS ICT standards.
Define national ICT budgets, procurement plans, and multi-year ICT investment roadmaps.
Develop and implement ICT policies and standards — covering architecture, security, disaster recovery, procurement, and service provision.
Participate in regional ICT knowledge-sharing processes and coordinate with the SOS ESAF ICT Advisor on global standards and initiatives.
Lead ICT governance — including vendor management, service level agreements, and ICT committee oversight.

Programmes Digitalisation & Digital Case Management

Implement and manage a secure, cloud-based digital case management platform for tracking child progress — ensuring data privacy and compliance with Rwanda data protection laws and SOS-KDI data protection rules.
Lead the digitalisation of SOS Rwanda's programme functions — introducing digital case management, beneficiary tracking, and electronic documentation workflows across all four locations.
Equip field staff with mobile tools for real-time community reporting — reducing the 'paperwork lag' and improving data quality.
Drive paperless operations across all locations — designing change management plans that support staff adoption of new digital tools.
Collaborate with the Director of Strategy and Programme Implementation and the MEAL function to align digitalisation initiatives with programme quality and RBM needs.
Explore, evaluate, and pilot AI adoption and knowledge management tools that enhance programme decision-making and organisational efficiency.

 ERP, HRIS and Operational Systems

Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and continuous improvement of SOS Rwanda's ERP system — ensuring integration across finance, procurement, HR, and programme functions.
Manage the HRIS system — ensuring data integrity, user access management, and alignment with HR processes.
Lead the digitisation of procurement and supply chain systems in coordination with the Senior Manager, Procurement and Logistics.
Ensure all ICT systems are properly integrated, reducing data silos and enabling organisation-wide reporting and analytics.

Infrastructure, Cybersecurity and Business Continuity

Manage SOS Rwanda's IT network and server infrastructure across all locations — ensuring 99%+ system uptime, reliability, performance, and cost-effectiveness.
Develop and implement a comprehensive cybersecurity framework — including data protection, access control, threat monitoring, and incident response — ensuring the cybersecurity audit score meets SOS-KDI standards.
Ensure compliance with SOS-KDI data protection rules and Rwanda data protection regulations, including the privacy of child and family records.
Design and maintain business continuity and disaster recovery plans — ensuring operational resilience in the event of system failures.

Digital Literacy & Capacity Building

Build digital literacy across SOS Rwanda — designing and delivering ICT training programmes for staff at all levels and locations.
Supervise the ICT Administrator and provide technical oversight to location ICT focal points.
Coach programme and operations staff on effective use of digital tools for monitoring, reporting, and case management.
Train community partners and staff on using technology for education, health monitoring, and economic strengthening.

Formal qualifications and Experiencerequirements:
Education & Professional Qualifications

Master’s or bachelor’s degree in information technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or related field (Master's preferred for Grade 5).
ITIL, PMP, or relevant technical certifications required (Grade 5 requirement).
Cybersecurity certification (CompTIA Security+, CISSP, or equivalent) is a strong advantage.

Professional Experience

Minimum of 7 years of progressive ICT experience; 3+ years in senior ICT leadership or digital transformation role.
Demonstrated experience leading digital transformation initiatives in an INGO, NGO, or complex multi-site organisation.
Proven experience with ERP systems (SOS ERP, SAP, Microsoft Dynamics, or equivalent) and HRIS platforms.
Strong track record in cybersecurity management, data protection, and ICT governance.
Experience with ICT4D tools — digital case management, mobile data collection, cloud platforms.
Experience working across multiple sites and geographically dispersed teams.

Skills & Competencies

Digital Transformation Strategy and Programme Digitisation.
ICT Infrastructure Management and Systems Architecture.
Data Governance and Cybersecurity.
ERP Systems Management and Integration.
Vendor Management and contract administration.
Strong change management and adult learning facilitation skills.
Ability to communicate technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences.
Good understanding of programme monitoring, MEAL, and data analytics.
Fluent English; Kinyarwanda and/or French is an advantage.
Commitment to SOS values and ethical use of data and technology in child-related programmes.

How to apply 
The interested Candidates in this position should send a detailed Curriculum Vitae with three (3) traceable professional references, application letter , Rwandan national Identity Card and academic certificates/degrees to sos.recruitment@sos-rwanda.org and properly fill the application form found via the followingLINKby not later than 27th September, 2026 at 5:00 pm Kigali time. 
Please mention in the subject of your email “Senior Manager ICT and Programs Digitalization”.
Female candidates are encouraged to apply, and only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

Parallel to technical competence, recruitment, selection and hiring decisions will give due emphasize to assessing candidates value congruence and thorough background checks, police clearance reference check processes”. 
Done in Kigali on 17th September 2026.

ndangira.description_html:
JOB VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT 

The Management of INDONGOZI SACCO NYAMASHEKE invites applications from qualified and interested candidates for the following vacant positions, as part of its efforts to strengthen its operations and improve service delivery.

No Position Required Qualification Required Experience Eligible Candidate Other Employment Details Deadline of Submission
1 Customer Care Officer (3) At least A2 in Accounting, or CMP certificate for completing Level One, or possessing the higher degree in Accounting, Finance, management or any related field.  Relevant experience in customer care services, preferably in banking, SACCO or microfinance is an added advantage. Open to qualified internal and external candidates meeting the requirements. Must have completed secondary education with 70% minimum marks;  Full-time; Permanent subject to successful probation. Reporting to the Branch Business Manager. Duties include customer reception and assistance, complaint handling and follow-up, member records, account opening support, customer information, statements, customer satisfaction surveys, product information and consumer support. Wednesday, 23 September 2026 at 05:00 p.m. (Rwanda Time)

Required Skills and Competencies:

  • Excellent customer service orientation;
  • Good communication and interpersonal skills;
  • Good negotiation and problem-solving skills;
  • Patience and a positive attitude;
  • Ability to handle complaints professionally;
  • Ability to multitask and work under pressure;
  • Attention to detail and confidentiality;
  • Ability to work effectively with different categories of customers.

GENERAL REQUIREMENTS

Applicants must:

  • Meet the minimum academic and professional requirements for the position applied for;
  • Have the required experience, where applicable;
  • Demonstrate integrity, professionalism and good conduct;
  • Possess good communication, teamwork and interpersonal skills;
  • Have basic computer literacy relevant to the position;
  • Be willing to work at any branch or outlet of INDONGOZI SACCO NYAMASHEKE, as assigned by Management;
  • Be available to undergo the institution's recruitment and selection process.

One (1) Vacant Post at UFC Plc Head Office

Location : Rwanda

Job description for Legal Officer 

  • Draft and review loan contracts, ensuring all loan files are legally compliant before disbursement;
  • Draft, review, and negotiate contracts and other key documents, assessing their legal implications and advising UFC PLC accordingly;
  • Prepare, review, and amend contractual instruments to facilitate and support various business activities;

  • Collaborate with concerned departments to identify legal risks and implement appropriate mitigation strategies;
  • Oversee the progress of ongoing litigation and manage relationships with external Lawyers;
  • Collaborate with Professional Court Bailiff in the execution of Court Cases and other related legal correspondences and make sure that they are executed successfully;
  • Provide timely and practical legal opinions to guide decision-making processes in compliance with existing laws and regulations;
  • Review ongoing legal cases and offer strategic advice to safeguard the interests of UFC PLC;
  • Ensure adherence to legal compliance within internal policies and procedures;
  • Monitor and ensure compliance with microfinance regulations governing the operations of UFC PLC;
  • Handle correspondence with clients, regulatory bodies, and law enforcement, ensuring appropriate responses;
  • Collaborate with various departments within UFC PLC to provide legal support and guidance as needed.
  • Promptly identify and advise on conflicts of interest in alignment with UFC PLC policies and the Code of Conduct.
  • Maintain all corporate records and documenting all corporate decisions;
  • Collect all documents for drawdown on credit facility to ensure that the institution’s interest is adequately protected and conditions precedent met before disbursement.

  • Prepare and Maintain Litigation Schedule in collaboration with External Lawyers

  • Minimum of 2 years of relevant legal experience in the banking, microfinance sector or law firm;
  • Prior experience in providing legal counsel and ensuring compliance within a financial institution;
  • Deep understanding of relevant laws and regulations, with strong drafting and negotiation skills;
  • Ability to juggle multiple tasks while meeting deadlines in a fast-paced environment;
  • Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management abilities;
  • High level of integrity and ability to handle confidential matters;
  • Knowledge of IECMS (Integrated Electronic Case Management System) for following up on Court Cases of UFC PLC;
  • Fluency in English, French, and Kinyarwanda, both written and spoken.
