ndangira.title: Pediatric Surgery Faculty  at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)
ndangira.title_raw: Pediatric Surgery Faculty  at University of Global Health Equity (UGHE): (Deadline 10-10-2026)
ndangira.description:
Position: Pediatric Surgery Faculty
Job Title: Faculty, Pediatric Surgery
Reports to: Head, Department of Surgery
Group/Department: Department of Surgery / Division of Clinical Medicine, University of Global Health Equity (UGHE)
Location: Primarily Butaro Campus and Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, with frequent travel to Kigali and other teaching sites in Rwanda
Position Overview
The Faculty of Pediatric Surgery will play a key role in advancing UGHE’s mission to deliver equitable, high-quality medical education and surgical care for children. The faculty member will contribute to undergraduate and postgraduate medical education, clinical pediatric surgical service delivery, research, and global surgery initiatives focused on children’s surgical care.
The Pediatric Surgery faculty member will actively participate in clinical teaching at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital and affiliated training sites, contribute to curriculum development in pediatric surgery, mentor students and trainees, and support the implementation of the General Surgery Residency Program aligned with COSECSA standards, including strengthening pediatric surgical training exposure.
The ideal candidate is highly self-motivated, academically productive, and committed to surgical education, research, and strengthening pediatric surgical capacity in resource-limited settings. The individual must be organized, collaborative, adaptable, and passionate about improving access to safe, timely, and affordable surgical care for children.
Responsibilities
Undergraduate Medical Education

Contribute to curriculum, syllabus, and content development in pediatric surgery across the MBBS/MGHD curriculum.
Deliver lectures, small group sessions, simulation-based teaching, and bedside clinical instruction.
Provide clinical supervision to medical students during surgery clerkships, with emphasis on pediatric surgical conditions.
Participate in student assessment (OSCEs, written exams, workplace-based assessments).
Supervise and mentor undergraduate research projects.
Coordinate pediatric surgery teaching activities with visiting and adjunct faculty.
Collaborate with affiliated hospitals to ensure effective delivery of pediatric surgical education.
Ensure quality and consistency of clinical teaching across all rotation sites.
Provide leadership for pediatric surgery modules or thematic blocks as assigned.
Participate in direct patient care as part of clinical teaching responsibilities.

Postgraduate and Residency Education

Contribute to implementation of competency-based training aligned with COSECSA standards.
Ensure quality supervision of residents rotating through pediatric surgery.
Provide structured clinical supervision in neonatal and pediatric surgical care.
Participate in WBAs, logbook reviews, case discussions, and operative competency assessments.
Contribute to exam preparation for COSECSA membership and fellowship examinations.
Mentor residents in clinical practice, research, leadership, and professionalism.
Participate in M&M conferences, journal clubs, and academic rounds.
Support development of simulation-based training for pediatric surgical procedures.
Contribute to accreditation and quality assurance processes.
Support development of pediatric surgery training pathways within UGHE programs.

Clinical Service Delivery

Support and scale-up of comprehensive pediatric surgical services at Butaro Level II Teaching Hospital, including:

Pediatric general surgery and emergency care
Pediatric Oncologic Surgery
Strengthen systems for perioperative care of children, including anesthesia, critical care, and nutrition.
Develop and implement clinical protocols, safety standards, and quality improvement initiatives.
Support multidisciplinary care involving pediatrics, anesthesia, nursing, and allied health professionals.
Strengthen referral systems and district-level capacity for pediatric surgical care.
Participate in on-call coverage and emergency pediatric surgical services.

Research and Scholarship

Initiate and support research in pediatric surgery, neonatal surgery, and global children’s surgery.

Develop grant proposals, research publications, and technical reports.
Mentor students and residents in research activities.
Conduct implementation and operational research focused on improving access to pediatric surgical care in Rwanda and similar settings.

Center for Equity in Global Surgery (CEGS) Activities

Participate in CEGS academic and administrative activities.
Contribute to global surgery conferences, seminars, and collaborations.
Build partnerships with national and international pediatric surgery programs.
Support grant writing and resource mobilization.
Advocate for equitable access to surgical care for children.

Institutional Service and Leadership

Serve on UGHE committees as assigned.
Contribute to departmental strategy and academic program development.
Engage in community outreach and child health advocacy initiatives.
Promote interprofessional education and collaboration.
Perform other duties as assigned by UGHE leadership.

Qualifications and Skills
Mandatory

Medical degree (MD, MBBS, or equivalent) from a recognized institution.
Postgraduate qualification in Pediatric Surgery (Fellowship, MMed, or equivalent recognized specialist qualification).
Board certification or equivalent specialist recognition in Pediatric Surgery.
Eligible for medical licensure/registration in Rwanda.
Demonstrated clinical expertise in pediatric surgical care, including neonatal surgery.
Experience in teaching undergraduate and postgraduate trainees.
Demonstrated research experience.
Commitment to academic medicine and mentorship.
Strong interpersonal and teamwork skills in multidisciplinary settings.
Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Preferred

MSc in Public Health, Global Health, or Medical Education.
Experience in health systems strengthening and surgical capacity building in low-resource settings.
Experience working in academic medical centers.
Expertise in research methods and implementation science.
Experience in competency-based medical education.
Grant writing experience and peer-reviewed publications.
Familiarity with COSECSA or similar regional training frameworks.

How to Apply
Applicants should provide: (1) curriculum vitae, (2) Degree, (3) A cover letter describing your interest in UGHE and relevant experience. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page.
University of Global Health Equity is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Organizational Profile
UGHE is a new kind of university focused on training the next generation of global leaders in health care delivery. The university launched in Rwanda in September 2015. Through an academic experience uniquely rooted in the values of equity, students are empowered to both ease suffering at the bedside and drive transformational, systemic changes to the health system.
UGHE is an initiative of Partners In Health (PIH), an internationally recognized non-profit organization whose mission is to provide a preferential option for the poor in health care. In over nearly three decades of operating alongside public sectors in countries around the world, PIH has developed a model to deliver high quality healthcare to some of the world’s most marginalized communities. Nowhere has this impact been more profound than in Rwanda, where Inshuti Mu Buzima—PIH’s sister organization—and our government partners have driven innovation for a decade.
Members of the UGHE community are tenacious and resolute in our drive to attain social justice, make common cause with those in need, listen to and learn from others, and operate with honesty and humility as we uphold academic integrity and intellectual curiosity. The University of Global Health Equity seeks individuals committed to these values to join the team.
Commitment to Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Sexual Harassment:
At UGHE, we are committed to ensuring that those who benefit from our work- including community members – as well as our students, contractors, staff, and visitors to our campus are treated with dignity and respect and protected from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment and any form of systemic abuse, whilst reducing risk and vulnerabilities. A range of pre-employment checks will be undertaken in conformity with UGHE’s policy.
UGHE will request information from applicants’ previous employers about any findings of fraud, harassment, sexual harassment and any form of systemic abuse or incidents under investigation when the applicant left employment. By applying, the job applicant confirms their understanding of these recruitment procedures.
CLICK HERE TO READ MORE AND APPLY

Description Position Title: Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain
Department/Unit: IGHER-Biobank
Reports To: Biobank Program
Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites
Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension
Position SummaryThe Biobank Technician II – Data Management and Cold Chain is responsible for maintaining accurate biobank information systems, managing specimen inventory records, monitoring storage conditions, and ensuring uninterrupted cold chain operations.The position ensures sample traceability, data integrity, specimen security, and compliance throughout the biobank lifecycle. The Technician also provides essential operational support to clinical trial activities by maintaining trial sample accountability records, supporting monitoring visits, and ensuring accurate documentation of research specimens.
Key Responsibilities

Maintain accurate biobank and clinical trial sample databases, including inventory, location, processing, storage, transfers, and access history.
Reconcile physical specimens with electronic records and resolve discrepancies.
Track sample receipt, storage, retrieval, shipment, and chain of custody.
Monitor cold-chain conditions, including −80°C freezers and liquid nitrogen systems, and respond to temperature excursions.
Generate sample inventory and accountability reports and support audits, monitoring visits, and regulatory inspections.
Maintain compliance with SOPs, protocols, ethics, data protection, and quality requirements, including CAPA.
Maintain equipment, storage, and maintenance records and support contingency planning.
Collaborate with laboratory, clinical, data, and research teams and support clinical trial start-up, monitoring, and close-out activities.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Health Informatics, Biomedical/Laboratory Sciences, Data Management, Biotechnology, IT, Life Sciences, or related field.

Experience:

2–3 years’ experience in biobank operations, laboratory data management, clinical research, or health information systems.

Experience with databases, sample tracking, and electronic records.
Data management, quality assurance, Excel/database systems, cold-chain monitoring, and research documentation.
Preferred Training: GCP, GCLP, biobank, data management, or biosafety training.
Strong attention to detail, organization, accountability, problem-solving, teamwork, and commitment to data quality.
Accurate and timely inventory, complete sample traceability, reliable cold-chain monitoring, and accurate clinical trial specimen accountability.

 To apply 
Applicants should provide: (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) graduate transcripts, (3) examples of relevant teaching experience or course materials, where available, and (4) a personal statement describing their teaching approach and experience working with diverse student populations. Position Title: Biobank Technician I
Department/Unit: IGHER - Biobank Program
Reports To: Biobank Head
Location: Kigali with possible travel to research sites and sample collection locations
Position type: Two-year contract with possible extension
Position Summary
The Biobank Technician I – Sample Processing is responsible for supporting the collection, receipt, processing, aliquoting, labeling, storage preparation, and quality control of biological specimens collected from clinical trials, population-based research studies, and other biomedical research projects.The position ensures that all biological samples are handled, processed, and stored according to approved Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), biosafety requirements, and biobank quality standards.The Biobank Technician I works closely with Clinical Research Coordinators, Principal Investigators, laboratory personnel, data management teams, and research partners to ensure specimen integrity, traceability, and compliance throughout the research lifecycle.
Key Responsibilities

Receive, process, label, aliquot, store, retrieve, and prepare biological specimens for shipment according to approved SOPs.
Maintain accurate sample identification, tracking, chain-of-custody, and inventory records.
Conduct routine quality checks, document deviations, and support CAPA, audits, and continuous quality improvement.
Operate and maintain laboratory equipment, including centrifuges, biosafety cabinets, refrigerators, freezers, and pipettes.
Maintain biosafety, GCLP/GCP, confidentiality, and laboratory safety standards.
Monitor laboratory supplies and report equipment or operational issues.
Collaborate with clinical, laboratory, data management, and research teams to support clinical trials and research projects.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical/Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biotechnology, Biology, Biochemistry, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field.

Experience

Minimum 2 years of laboratory experience, preferably involving human biological specimens in research, clinical trials, hospitals, or diagnostic laboratories.
Skills: Knowledge of sample processing, biosafety, laboratory quality standards, documentation, and basic laboratory information systems; good computer skills.
Preferred Training: GCLP, GCP, biosafety, and research ethics certification/training.

To apply 
Applicants should provide: (1) a curriculum vitae, (2) graduate transcripts, (3) examples of relevant teaching experience or course materials, where available, and (4) a personal statement describing their teaching approach and experience working with diverse student populations. Applicants may also include an example of relevant scholarly work. Please upload these under the ‘Additional Files’ tab on the application page.

ndangira.description:
Description
Position Title: Biobank Head
Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)
Duty Station: UGHE-AVEGA Biobank and UGHE, Kigali. Frequent travel to the Butaro campus, Northern Province, Burera District, Rwanda
Contract Duration: Two (2) years, renewable based on performance
Position Summary
The Biobank Head provides strategic, scientific, technical, and operational leadership for the establishment and management of the UGHE-AVEGA Biobank, a core research infrastructure of the Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER). The position is responsible for leading the planning, establishment, operationalization, accreditation, and continuous improvement of the biobank to support clinical trials, translational research, precision medicine, genomics, oncology, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and population health research.
The Head is responsible for the overall administration and day-to-day management of biobank operations, including biospecimen acquisition, processing, storage, inventory management, retrieval, distribution, Laboratory Information Management System (LIMS) administration, quality management systems, biosafety and biosecurity, regulatory compliance, equipment management, financial oversight, and supervision of biobank personnel.
Reporting to the Clinical research lead/Director of IGHER, the Biobank Head works closely with the Head of the UGHE-AVEGA Clinical Trial Unit to ensure seamless integration of biobanking services into all clinical trials and research activities conducted through UGHE. The position also collaborates closely with the Biobank Project Consultant (External Scientific Consultant) to establish the biobank according to international standards, develop governance structures, implement quality systems, strengthen institutional capacity, and position UGHE as a national and regional centre of excellence in biobanking.
The Biobank Head will play a pivotal leadership role in developing institutional policies, standard operating procedures, governance frameworks, regulatory systems, quality assurance programs, and strategic partnerships that ensure the biobank operates in accordance with ISBER Best Practices, ISO 20387, Good Clinical Laboratory Practice (GCLP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and all applicable national and international regulatory requirements.
Key Responsibilities

Lead the establishment and operation of the UGHE–AVEGA Biobank and align activities with UGHE/IGHER priorities.
Establish SOPs, Quality Management Systems, governance, and regulatory compliance, including preparation for ISO 20387 accreditation and ISBER Best Practices.
Lead implementation and management of the LIMS and ensure secure, accurate, and traceable data management.
Oversee biospecimen management, quality, traceability, security, staffing, equipment, budgets, and daily operations.
Integrate biobanking with clinical trials and research programs and develop national and international collaborations.
Build staff capacity through training, mentorship, and competency development in biobanking, GCP/GCLP, biosafety, and quality management.

Qualifications
Education
PhD (preferred) or Master's in Biobanking, Medical Laboratory Sciences, Biomedical/Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pathology, Genomics, Public Health, Clinical Research, or related field. Position Title: Biobank Coordinator (Administrative & Research Operations)
Department: Institute of Global Health Equity Research (IGHER)
Reports To: Head of Biobank 
Location: Kigali with regular travel to research sites
Contract Duration: Two year contract with possible extension for another two years
Position Summary
The Biobank coordinator will provide operational, administrative, and research coordination support for biobank activities and clinical trial projects. The position will ensure effective planning, implementation, documentation, and monitoring of research activities while maintaining compliance with institutional policies, ethical requirements, Good Clinical Practice (GCP), and biobank quality standards.
The Coordinator will serve as a key liaison between investigators, clinical trial teams, laboratory personnel, research participants, regulatory bodies, and collaborating institutions. The role requires strong organizational skills, attention to detail, experience in research administration, and the ability to coordinate multiple activities simultaneously.
Key Responsibilities

Coordinate daily biobank operations, including specimen collection, processing, storage, tracking, inventory, access, documentation, and compliance.
Support clinical trial implementation, including timelines, regulatory documentation, site coordination, monitoring visits, recruitment tracking, essential documents, and logistics.
Coordinate research activities, work plans, meetings, reports, budgets, procurement, travel, and project documentation.
Ensure adherence to GCP, ethics and regulatory requirements, biobank policies, data protection, and support audits and accreditation activities.
Serve as a coordination point among investigators, clinical teams, laboratory/biobank staff, sponsors, regulators, and research partners, ensuring effective communication and follow-up.

Required Qualifications and competence

Bachelor’s degree in Health/Biomedical/Laboratory Sciences, Public Health, Clinical Research, Life Sciences, Health Administration, or related field; Master’s degree is an advantage.
Experience: 3–5 years’ experience in clinical research, clinical trials, biobanking, laboratory research, or research administration.
Experience with research documentation, databases, regulatory/ethics submissions, and multidisciplinary teams.
Knowledge of ICH-GCP, biobank operations, sample management, and research compliance.
Experience with REDCap, CTMS, LIMS, or similar research data systems is an advantage.
Strong organizational, coordination, communication, documentation, problem-solving, and time-management skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and ability to manage confidential research information.
GCP, research ethics, clinical research, biobank, or data management certification is an advantage.
Ability to coordinate multiple activities, maintain accurate records, meet deadlines, and support clinical trials, audits, reporting, and research logistics.

ndangira.description_html:
Job Title: Project Assistant (3 Vacancies)

Department/Group: Implementation

Reporting To: Project Officer Years of Experience 2+ Years

Location: Rutsiro (2) and Nyamasheke (1)

Travel Required: 90%

Job description

About Raising The Village

At Raising The Village (RTV), we are dedicated to eradicating ultra-poverty in Sub-Saharan Africa. As a dynamic, rapidly growing international development organization, we’ve assembled a team of over 350+ passionate individuals in Uganda, Rwanda, DRC and Tanzania, alongside an additional 15+ professionals in North America. Together, we are committed to elevating communities out of ultra-poverty by implementing innovative solutions and leveraging advanced data analytics to drive impact.

To date, our holistic approach has positively impacted over 1,000,000 lives since 2012, and we’re poised to achieve even greater milestones, aiming to assist 1 million individuals annually by 2027. Our growth and success are fueled by the invaluable support of global partners who share our vision of sustainable change. Learn more about our impactful programs at www.raisingthevillage.org

Position Summary

Role and Responsibilities

Project Implementation

  • Conduct project design review meetings with respective partner villages and provide feedback as required to update project designs and budgets prior to implementation;
  • Coordinate training activities including but not limited to financial literacy and behavior and mindset change, water and health sanitation, village savings and loans associations, agriculture, livestock care and management, etc.
  • Responsible to implement RTV’s project methodologies with the purpose of increasing household income and reducing extreme poverty as per project designs;
  • Develop and submit list of required goods and services for project implementation to the procurement and logistics officer;
  • Responsible to verify goods/inputs prior to distribution;
  • Conduct project follow-up and provide support and guidance to community groups and individual households to ensure project compliance continuation.
  • Identify potential risks and issues and provide mitigation measures and recommendations for improvements;
  • Conduct regular meetings with leadership and community members on performance, participation, and perceptions of RTV based projects.

Government & Community Coordination and Support

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with Cell-level government officials (SEDOs and Executive Secretaries) to support day-to-day RTV program activities.
  • Work closely with community leadership and support structures including Inteko z’abaturage, Incuti z’umuryango, Abajyanama b’Ubuzima, Abajyanama b’Ubuhinzi (farmer promoters), para-social workers, community coaches, technical and village coaches, and other community actors to ensure their active participation in RTV programs.
  • Mobilize households and communities for trainings, meetings, and program activities to promote clear understanding, strong participation, and adoption of RTV program components.
  • Assist in delivering trainings to community and cell-level actors on RTV program methodology, M&E processes, technology use, and field protocols, under the guidance of the Project Officer or Project Manager.
  • Provide on-the-job support and follow-up to community and government actors during implementation to help address challenges and encourage consistent participation.
  • Promote positive collaboration and trust between RTV staff, government officials, and community structures to strengthen community ownership and contribute to sustainable program impact.

Reporting and Administration

Develop and manage work plans;

  • Complete field reporting on a weekly basis and provide support with information sharing for donor reporting and proposal writing as might be required;
  • Attend and participate in weekly staff meetings as well as cluster team meetings to highlight issues and success and outline next steps;
  • Complete weekly financial request, submissions and accountabilities to the Project Officer;
  • Take photographs and share them for data repository.

Monitoring and Evaluation:

  • Support field monitoring activities such as attendance tracking, basic data collection, household follow-ups, and reporting using RTV tools and systems.
  • Providing feedback and recommendations to the Project Officer and Project Manager, and the program team to improve RTV’s way of work;
  • Provide suggestions to management on potential activities that need to be redone, reviewed or introduced to ensure sustainability of RTV projects, methodologies, and improvement in the lives of community members.

Note: Other requirements might be required by their direct supervisor and/or management.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, Social Work, Humanities, Community Development, or related field of study
  • Bachelor’s degree in agriculture is preferred but not required
  • Minimum of two (2) years of relevant work experience at the village level
  • Demonstrated experience working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at Sector and Cell levels (mandatory)

Preferred Skills if any

Strong training & facilitation skills;

  • Strong communication skills, both verbal and written English;
  • Fluent in local languages where RTV works;
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office programs i.e. Word and Excel
  • Understanding of Community Based Development Principles
  • Organizes work effectively while remaining aware of changing priorities and deadlines;
  • Able to work independently to accomplish tasks, but also as part of a team to achieve mutual goals and objectives;
  • Able to think outside of the box to provide plausible solutions to issues and challenges;
  • Strong work ethic, flexible, and able to build relationships with various stakeholders most notably colleagues, and community members;
  • Able to keep a positive attitude in a fast-paced and challenging environment;
  • Energetic and physically able to hike high to hike high terrain;
  • Able to travel approximately 90% of time;
  • Ability to ride a motorbike with a valid Rwandan rider’s permit (class A) and demonstrated experience navigating remote, rural and hilly terrain (mandatory).

We encourage women, people with disabilities and minority groups to apply for this position. RTV is committed to equal opportunities and diversity of perspective at the workplace. 

Disclaimer: Raising the Village DOES NOT charge any kind of FEE(s) at whichever stage of the recruitment process.

Support implementation and transition activities;

Ensure staff receive proper orientation and training;

Administration and logistical support

Conduct on-going interviews of leadership and community on performance, participation, and perceptions
Manage and report on office budgets and expenditures
Track and review on-going financial reports and progress
Complete weekly, monthly, quarterly and annual reports and provide them to relevant management staff
Complete necessary reporting for local government district office
Oversee on-going growth and development programming
Support in the recruitment of new staff
Prepare office accountability and ensure bi-weekly submission to the Finance Officer

Qualifications, Education and Job Requirements

University Degree in Project Management, Social Work and Social Administration, Project planning and Development, Community Development, or related fields
Masters or Post Graduate Diploma in Project planning and Management will be an added advantage.
Minimum of four (5) years of working experience.
Demonstrated experience (at least 3 years) working with and coordinating local government institutions and officials, particularly at District and Sector levels (mandatory)
At least 3 years at a supervisory level.
Experience in project design, budgeting and project management and implementation at village levels

Personal and Skills Development

ndangira.title_raw: Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-term) at One Acre Fund : (Deadline 03-12-2026)
ndangira.description:
Conservation Agriculture (Fixed-term) at One Acre Fund : (Deadline 03-12-2026)
About One Acre Fund
Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.
Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.
About the Role
We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate Senior Agronomist with in-depth expertise and at least 6 years of experience in Conservation Agriculture and deploying farmer training in these practices in the field.
Responsibilities
Conservation Agriculture Strategy & Extension Development

Develop and continuously improve scalable conservation agriculture advisory models in collaboration with farmer advisory and field teams.
Design practical extension materials, training manuals, visual guides, and digital tools tailored to diverse farmer needs and contexts.
Translate technical concepts including cover cropping, minimum tillage, agroforestry, and integrated pest management into practical field-based curricula.
Adapt advisory approaches and materials based on climate, soil, socioeconomic conditions, farmer feedback, and field learning.

Farmer Training, Field Deployment & Adoption

Provide hands-on technical guidance to field teams delivering farmer trainings, workshops, Farmer Field Schools, and demonstration plots.
Build the capacity of field staff and local extension agents to effectively promote and support conservation agriculture adoption.
Provide timely agronomic troubleshooting to farmers and field teams addressing crop, soil, pest, and climate-related challenges.
Work with MEL and field teams to develop and implement systems that track adoption, farmer outcomes, and opportunities for scaling.

Agronomic Research, Practice Optimization & Impact

Evaluate and refine conservation agriculture practices to improve soil health, water retention, biodiversity, productivity, and farmer profitability.
Collaborate with R&D teams to design and oversee field assessments of soil health, crop performance, and environmental outcomes.
Analyze field evidence and farmer feedback to identify high-impact practices and recommend improvements to conservation agriculture programming.
Translate research findings and field learning into practical recommendations, extension content, and scalable implementation models.

Partnership & Cross-Functional Project Leadership

Build and manage strategic relationships with public, private, NGO, academic, and other technical partners supporting conservation agriculture initiatives.
Coordinate project plans, timelines, deliverables, reporting, and data sharing across internal teams and external consortium partners.
Represent the conservation agriculture program in technical discussions and ensure strong alignment between farmer needs, organizational priorities, and partner objectives.
Identify opportunities for collaboration, innovation, and resource mobilization that strengthen program quality, scale, and long-term impact.

Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.
Qualifications
Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Master’s degree in Agronomy, Agroecology, Crop Science, Soil Science, or a closely related agricultural field.
Minimum 6 years of relevant professional experience in agronomy, conservation agriculture, regenerative agriculture, or agroecological farming systems.
Proven experience developing agricultural extension materials and leading farmer-facing training, capacity building, or advisory programs.
Demonstrated experience coordinating multi-stakeholder projects involving government, NGOs, research institutions, academia, or private-sector partners.
Strong hands-on experience working directly with smallholder farmers and field teams, with willingness to travel extensively and spend significant time in rural settings.
Proficiency in English is required; additional regional or international languages are an advantage.

Preferred Start Date
As soon as possible
Job Location
Kigali, Rwanda
Benefits
Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits
Contract Duration
2 years, renewable with a high chance based on good performance.
Eligibility
This role is open to all applicants; however, candidates with citizenship or permanent residency in Kenya, Rwanda, Uganda, Tanzania, or Burundi are strongly preferred.
Application Deadline
03 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis, which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.
One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.
We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Our 8,000+ team is drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. With operations across ten African countries, we make farmers more prosperous by providing easy access to quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, and agricultural training to improve harvests. On average, the farmers we serve earn 40 percent more profits from their land when they enroll with One Acre Fund. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chilli.

Establish 0-6 month strategic targets and set price baselines to negotiate maximum cost savings.
Continually optimise sourcing processes for higher operational efficiency.

Analyse annual spend across key categories to establish a quarterly-reviewed tender calendar.
Conduct market research to boost competition and contract effectiveness.
Oversee full contract lifecycles and Long-Term Agreements (LTAs) by tracking price tolerances and managing change control systems.
Analyse market risks and report overall cost savings.

Conduct bi-annual vendor evaluations and monthly meetings with top suppliers to create performance improvement plans and enforce contractual commitments.
Act as the key liaison between external suppliers and One Acre Fund while directly supporting internal team procurement needs.

2–3 years of relevant experience in contract management, procurement sourcing, and end-to-end tendering operations.

Maintain the Division's communications calendar and coordinate inputs, timelines, follow-ups, and actions with department leads.
Prepare high-quality presentation decks, briefing notes, data summaries, and other materials for senior leadership.
Translate complex data, analytical findings, and team inputs into clear insights, recommendations, and actionable messages.

Coordinate selected CFO- and Senior Manager-sponsored initiatives by aligning stakeholders, tracking milestones, and proactively addressing blockers.
Lead or contribute to high-priority cross-functional and ad hoc projects across the Finance Division.
Apply structured problem-solving to ambiguous challenges and develop practical options and recommendations for leadership.

Develop structured outputs, including summaries, frameworks, financial models, and scenario analyses.
Provide flexible support across the Finance Division during periods of peak demand, staff transitions, or extended leave.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related field.
CPA or ACCA finalist.
About 5 years of working experience in finance, strategy, consulting, project management, or operations, within fast-paced medium- to large organisations.
Strong stakeholder management and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Proactive, detail-oriented, and solutions-focused approach.
Familiarity with financial analysis, management reporting, and business decision-making is preferred.
Comfortable navigating ambiguity and adapting to changing priorities.
Full professional proficiency in English, with strong written communication skills.

ndangira.description:
Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier at American Embassy Kigali Mission Rwanda : (Deadline 22-09-2026)
Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier
Vacancy Announcement: KIGALI-2026-010
The Embassy of the United States of America in Kigali, Rwanda is recruiting for an Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier.The position is open to All Interested Candidates/All Sources and available to start immediately.
Duties:
The Accounts Payable Technician/Alternate Cashier (APT/Alt Cashier) is a key member of the Accounts Payable Unit (APU) within the Financial Management Center (FMC) at Mission Kigali. The APT/Alt Cashier performs the full range of accounts payable and accounts receivable services for all subscribed ICASS agencies. The position also serves as a financial advisor to the Accounts Payable Manager (APM), ensuring timely and accurate processing of payments and receivables.
In the capacity of Alternate Cashier, the incumbent serves as the Embassy’s Principal Class B Cashier and accountable officer, responsible for managing cashier operations within an authorized advance. This includes oversight of cash on hand, transactions in transit, replenishments, and funds deposited in local checking accounts. The role also includes ensuring effective cash management and implementing cash risk mitigation measures.
The volume, quality, and timeliness of work must comply with Appropriation Law, Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP), the Foreign Affairs Manual (FAM), the Department of State Standardized Regulations (DSSR), ICASS service standards, and applicable host-government laws and regulations.
The APU manages vendor and employee payments and receivables for the Embassy and four partner agencies, across 15 allotments/appropriations, totaling more than $18 million in annual transactions. Duties are assigned by the Financial Specialist (FS) or Accounts Payable Manager (APM).All applications must be submitted via Electronic Recruitment Application (ERA) by September 22, 2026.Full announcement and application procedures are available on https://rw.usembassy.gov/jobs/
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. 
Please note that e-mailed applications are not accepted. Only applications submitted through our Electronic Recruitment Application will be considered.

RwandAir Ltd Vacancy: Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards – Deadline 11 September 2026
RwandAir Ltd, the flag carrier airline of Rwanda, is expanding its operations as it works toward 4-Star status and stronger regional hub leadership.
The airline is inviting applications from highly qualified and experienced professionals for the following position:
Job Title: Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards
Department: HR & AdministrationReports to: Chief HR & Administration OfficerLocation: Kigali International Airport, RwandaExperience Required: 10–12 years
Job Purpose
The Head of Organization Design & Total Rewards will lead the development of RwandAir's organization design, job architecture, workforce planning, compensation and benefits frameworks.
This is a strategic build role, responsible for developing and embedding systems covering an estimated workforce of 1,200–1,500 employees, including headquarters, outstations, flight crew, cabin crew, engineering and ground operations.
The successful candidate will help establish how work is organised across RwandAir and how roles are evaluated, graded, compensated and rewarded.
Key Duties and Responsibilities
1. Organization Design & Job Architecture

Develop and maintain RwandAir's organisation design standards, including spans, layers and decision rights.
Lead structural reviews across Commercial, Flight Operations, Ground Operations, Engineering, Cargo, Cabin Services and Corporate functions.
Design and implement an enterprise-wide job architecture covering job families, career levels and role profiles.
Establish workforce planning methodologies and productivity ratios.
Translate fleet and network plans into a credible three-year workforce and cost plan.

2. Total Rewards & Compensation

Develop RwandAir's Total Rewards philosophy, including market positioning, pay mix and differentiation.
Present the Total Rewards strategy for Executive Committee and Board approval.
Lead job evaluation using recognised methodologies such as Korn Ferry Hay, Mercer IPE or WTW GGS.
Chair the technical job evaluation panel.
Develop and maintain salary structures and annual pay review processes.
Conduct market benchmarking against regional and global airlines.
Develop compensation rules for flight crew and technical employees, including flight/duty pay, allowances and licence pay.
Oversee employee benefits such as medical insurance, pension, staff travel and housing.

3. Governance & Leadership

Lead the employment cost strategy and localisation/expatriate rewards framework.
Advise the Chief HR & Administration Officer and CFO on employment cost and organisational structure decisions.
Ensure structural changes maintain RCAA and IOSA postholder requirements and regulatory accountability.
Build and lead a technically strong Organization Design & Rewards team.
Develop and transfer technical capabilities to Rwandan HR professionals.

Minimum Qualifications
Applicants should have:

A Bachelor's Degree in Human Resource Management, Business Administration, Economics, Statistics, Industrial/Organisational Psychology or a related field.
10–12 years of progressive HR experience.
At least 5–6 years of specialist experience in reward, job architecture or organisation design.

Preferred Qualifications
The following are strongly preferred:

A Master's degree, such as MBA, MSc in HR Management or MSc in Organisational Psychology.
Accreditation in a recognised job evaluation methodology, including Korn Ferry Hay, Mercer IPE or WTW GGS.

Essential Experience
Candidates should demonstrate:

Experience leading at least one enterprise-wide job evaluation and grading implementation in an organisation with 1,000+ employees.
Experience in aviation or another regulated, multi-site and safety-critical industry. Aviation experience is strongly preferred.
Experience designing compensation for mixed workforce populations, including licensed/technical, operational shift, unionised, expatriate and local employees.
Experience presenting pay and organisational structure decisions at Board or Executive Committee level.

Other Desired Competencies & Skills
Previous Experience

Proven ability to move an organisation from having no formal framework to a governed and effective framework.
Strong ability to manage and communicate organisational change.
Confidence to challenge senior leaders when proposed structures or grades are not supportable.
Strong understanding of employment costs and their impact on business performance and the P&L.
Ability to handle executive compensation, restructuring and confidential employee information with a high level of discretion.

Job-Specific Skills

Strong knowledge of organisation design methodologies, including Galbraith Star Model, Kates Kesler and Ulrich value-chain logic.
Advanced job evaluation and grading expertise.
Strong compensation and benefits design capabilities.
Experience in salary structure development, market pricing, incentive design and benefits economics.
Advanced workforce analytics and cost modelling skills.
Working knowledge of aviation operations, including ICAO, IOSA, RCAA postholder structures, FTL, crew productivity, CASK and ASK.
Working knowledge of Rwandan Labour Law No. 66/2018.
Proficiency in HRIS/ERP systems, position management, organisation modelling and compensation modules.

Application Requirements
Applicants are required to submit:

Application letter addressed to the Chief HR & Administration Officer.
Recent Curriculum Vitae.
Copies of notarized Degree/Diploma certificates.
Relevant professional certificates.
Copies of academic papers.
Photocopy of Passport or National ID.
Three referees.

How to Apply
Interested and qualified candidates should submit their applications through the RwandAir e-Recruitment portal.
Application Deadline: 11 September 2026
Application Documents: PDF format only.
Important
This is a senior-level HR leadership position requiring substantial experience in organisation design, job evaluation, compensation and total rewards. Candidates should carefully review the minimum experience and specialist requirements before applying.

ndangira.title_raw: Territory Lead at  EarthEnable Rwanda: (Deadline 27-09-2026)
ndangira.description:
Territory Lead at EarthEnable Rwanda: (Deadline 27-09-2026)
JOB DESCRIPTION: TERRITORY LEAD 
Company: EarthEnable 
Reports to: District Operations Lead 
Location: Different districts in Rwanda 
Compensation: 320,000 - 350,000 RWF (Rwandan Franc) / month gross, depending on experience 
Who We Are 
At EarthEnable, we believe that our clients deserve our very best, that work should be fun, and that the best ideas could come from any part of the company. We celebrate each other’s wins, learn from our setbacks, and are deeply proud of the impact we make every day. We believe a home that doesn’t make you sick means more than living disease-free. It means pride and dignity in the place our customers most treasure: their homes. Being a part of our team means more than building housing products: it means building an organization and building a better future for rural families. 
What We Do 
EarthEnable is transforming the way people live, by making homes healthier for families across rural Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. 80% of Rwandans live in homes with dirt floors which are dusty, unsanitary, and fertile breeding grounds for parasites and germs. While replacing a dirt floor with concrete has significant health benefits (e.g. reducing diarrhea by 50% and parasitic infections by 80%), concrete is unaffordable for many who need it, and is also responsible for 8% of global carbon emissions. 
EarthEnable addresses this pressing and ubiquitous problem by selling high-quality, earthen housing products like our flagship floor that is 80% cheaper than concrete with 90% less embedded energy. Earthen floors, plasters, and blocks are composed of natural materials (gravel, clay, sand, and laterite) and sealed with a proprietary drying oil that makes them waterproof, strong, and polished. In our first decade of operations, EarthEnable has installed ~60,000 products for over 300,000 individuals and created livelihoods for over 1,300 people. See our new product - a full house - here!
Position Overview 
The Territory Lead is responsible for the overall performance, growth, and operational excellence of their assigned territory. This role combines commercial leadership, operational oversight, and people management to ensure sales targets are met, construction projects are executed efficiently, and customers receive an exceptional experience. 
The ideal candidate is a proactive and results-driven leader who can translate strategy into execution, build high-performing teams, and operate with strong business acumen in dynamic field environments. 
Key Responsibilities 
1. Territory Ownership and Business Performance 

Own the end-to-end performance of the territory, ensuring alignment with company growth objectives and operational priorities. 
Develop and execute localized sales and operational strategies informed by market insights, customer needs, and competitive dynamics. 
Drive achievement of assigned sales and build targets while maintaining strong quality and customer satisfaction standards. 
Monitor territory performance through data and KPIs, proactively identifying risks and implementing corrective actions. 

2. Sales Leadership and Customer Experience 

Lead the recruitment, onboarding, training, and ongoing development of Customer Sales Officers (CSOs) to build a strong and productive sales force. 
Equip teams with the tools, messaging, and support needed to effectively engage customers and convert leads. 
Champion customer-centric practices, ensuring a seamless journey from initial engagement through project completion. 
Strengthen relationships with cooperatives, institutions, local leaders, and community stakeholders to expand market reach and reinforce EarthEnable’s mission. 
Oversee territory-level marketing and activation initiatives to drive demand and brand visibility.

3. Operational and Construction Excellence

Who We Are 

At EarthEnable, we believe that our clients deserve our very best, that work should be fun, and that the best ideas could come from any part of the company. We celebrate each other’s wins, learn from our setbacks, and are deeply proud of the impact we make every day. We believe a home that doesn’t make you sick means more than living disease-free. It means pride and dignity in the place our customers most treasure: their homes. Being a part of our team means more than building housing products: it means building an organization and building a better future for rural families. 

What We Do 

EarthEnable is transforming the way people live, by making homes healthier for families across rural Rwanda, Uganda, and Kenya. 80% of Rwandans live in homes with dirt floors which are dusty, unsanitary, and fertile breeding grounds for parasites and germs. While replacing a dirt floor with concrete has significant health benefits (e.g. reducing diarrhea by 50% and parasitic infections by 80%), concrete is unaffordable for many who need it, and is also responsible for 8% of global carbon emissions. 

EarthEnable addresses this pressing and ubiquitous problem by selling high-quality, earthen housing products like our flagship floor that is 80% cheaper than concrete with 90% less embedded energy. ndangira.description:
Senior Program Manager, Cervical Cancer  at CHAI - The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc.: (Deadline 24 Aug 2027)
Job Description

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion, and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Program Overview
More than 300,000 women die of cervical cancer each year, despite the availability of proven prevention interventions that can dramatically reduce the burden of disease. Over 90% of these deaths occur among women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to high-quality prevention services has historically been limited. In 2018, the WHO issued a Global Call to Action Towards Cervical Cancer Elimination, and in 2020, the Member States of the World Health Assembly adopted a Cervical Cancer Elimination Strategy, setting targets to reach 70% screening coverage and 90% treatment coverage of screen-positive women by 2030.
CHAI’s cervical cancer program works to reduce cervical cancer incidence in LMICs by expanding access to secondary prevention services, thereby preventing mortality and morbidity while lowering cancer treatment costs for health systems. The program complements CHAI’s HPV vaccines work, which supports LMICs to introduce and routinize HPV vaccination for adolescent girls (primary prevention).
The program’s approach rests on three interconnected areas of work: (1) supporting Ministries of Health to introduce optimal tools, integrate services into routine healthcare, update policy, build workforce capacity, and strengthen health systems for scale-up; (2) market shaping to improve the access and affordability of existing and new technologies for screening and precancer treatment; (3) advancing innovation, including AI-based screening, to enable same-day screening and treatment.
The program has supported over 12 countries since 2019 to scale screening and treatment services, reaching more than 1.4 million women, while working to ensure high linkage to treatment and referral, improving the affordability and access of critical tools, and advancing the development of AI-assisted tools for screening. CHAI is now supporting governments to build nationally owned costed elimination plans, identifying sustainability pathways, and bringing low-cost AI-assisted screening tools to market.
Position Overview
The Senior Program Manager (SPM) holds day-to-day operational and technical leadership across country support, costing and financing, and diagnostics strategy and execution. The SPM guides associates, senior associates on the team, quality-assures outputs before Director reviews, and represents the program in technical coordination with CHAI's global diagnostics team and other teams across the matrix. The role combines people management, technical review, and direct workstream ownership, and acts as the critical link between country-facing staff and Director-level strategy and donor engagement.
The SPM works closely with the program’s country teams and CHAI’s global diagnostics, markets, health financing, AIR/research, and HPV vaccines teams.

The role manages some senior relationships, including at Unitaid, WHO, and other major donors, and is recognized as a subject-matter expert in cervical cancer prevention.
The base location is flexible with a preference for the role to be based in a program country, pending country leadership approval. An estimated 20% of international travel time is expected.

Responsibilities

Country support and cross-country learning

Guide associates and senior associates on the team in responding to country requests across relevant functional areas, including elimination plans, work plans, technical reports, and case studies.
Review and quality-assure country support outputs produced by associates and senior associates before Director review, including elimination plans, technical reports, donor reports, learning agenda pieces, memos, decks, case studies etc. Provide structured, actionable technical feedback to strengthen outputs.
Serve as the first point of escalation for country teams before issues reach the Director; quickly identify critical problems, break down and prioritize different parts of complex challenges, and apply lessons and best practices to redirect activities effectively.
Monitor the volume and pattern of country support requests and propose the team structure best suited to manage demand, whether organized around dedicated country assignments or around functional specialization.

Costing and financing workstream leadership

Provide technical and managerial oversight on the costing workstream, including on methodology, data quality, and consistency of costing outputs across programme countries. Guide the Associate serving as the costing focal point to deliver high-quality analyses aligned with the programme's broader elimination planning and financing strategy. (This workstream is expected to conclude within the next 6-9 months.)
Take on ownership of the cervical cancer financing workstream, with guidance from CHAI's global health financing team. Support countries to identify sustainable financing pathways for scale-up, conduct financing analyses, translate costing outputs into formats suitable for donor reporting and national planning, and develop a toolkit of financing approaches that can be adapted across settings.
Maximize the use of data to identify problems in financing and costing approaches, monitor progress, and develop effective, evidence-based solutions; apply lessons and best practices from across the program to inform or redirect activities.
Lead on creation of the learning agenda pieces for the costing and financing workstreams. Lead the development of cross-country learning products, work closely with the Senior Associate to track progress on other learning agenda commitments, provide technical reviews, and coordinate the dissemination and socialization of outputs with the communications team.

Diagnostics strategy and AI-assisted screening

Refine the program's diagnostics strategy, aligning country needs with global market-shaping priorities for screening and precancer treatment technologies, including new technologies entering the market — AI-assisted screening tools and near point of care HPV tests.
Work closely with the Global Diagnostics Team to ensure country-level and supplier-facing inputs are reflected in the program’s diagnostic strategy; apply knowledge across disciplines to inform approaches that bridge product, policy, and country adoption.
Flag country-level constraints or opportunities that should inform diagnostic tool selection, procurement pathways, or rollout sequencing.
Support country teams in scoping and planning for the deployment of AI-assisted screening tools. This would involve working closely with Global Markets team, global project manager for AI-assisted screening tools and the country teams to develop detailed, sequenced work plans that lay the operational groundwork for in-country introduction of such tools, covering regulatory approval pathways, digital health integration requirements, procurement and supply chain considerations, and service delivery readiness. Engage relevant CHAI teams with prior experience rolling out new health technologies to incorporate lessons learned into planning.

Resource mobilization and fundraising

Lead on the development of proposals for multi-country and country-level funding opportunities, coordinating input from cross-functional and cross-country teams.

Program reporting and financial management

Work with the senior associate and finance manager to prepare and finalise the periodic program and financial reports to key donors.
Work with the finance manager to develop annual budget revisions for donors, as well as forecasts and re-forecasts for the program; understand and flag the implications of over-spend or under-spend, and track obligations, commitments, and expenditure of funds in detail.

People management

Directly manage and mentor a small team of associates and senior associates, ensuring appropriate workload distribution, training, and performance feedback; bring individuals together to function as a cohesive and productive unit; provide guidance to other managers on staffing decisions and development plans where relevant.
Coach and support the professional development of associates and senior associates on the team, providing structured feedback and contributing to succession planning.
Lead cross-functional coordination across CHAI’s matrix, including with Global Diagnostics Team, Analytics and Implementation Research, Global Markets Team, health financing, and HPV vaccination teams.

Program strategy

Direct the team in shaping materials and key messages for senior stakeholders; support development and tailoring of program presentations at global and country level, translating technical content into accessible formats suited to relevant audiences for fundraising, internal and external strategy discussions, and dissemination of program learnings.
Support refinement of CHAI’s screening and treatment program strategy and CHAI’s integrated cervical elimination strategy; advise senior management on program objectives and strategy to achieve results.
Contribute to ideation and design of data visualizations and technical presentation of program data.
Evaluate the program’s current network of partners and technical advisors for relevance and effectiveness; identify and initiate new connections with senior external stakeholders that facilitate achievement of strategic goals, including collaborating with senior-level technical staff external to CHAI.

Additional responsibilities

Represent CHAI in WHO’s cervical cancer Guidelines Development Group, compile relevant updates from CHAI country global teams to feed into the GDG meetings, and report back progress and updates from GDG to program senior management.
Take initiative to address emerging priorities and respond to evolving program needs.
Undertake additional tasks as requested by the line manager to advance program objectives.

Qualifications

We seek an experienced and highly motivated program manager who is passionate about eliminating cervical cancer. An ideal candidate will be described as:

Strong strategic and analytical thinker: You understand the big picture and can translate complex challenges into clear, actionable workplans. You are comfortable working with large amounts of quantitative and qualitative data and can extract logical conclusions and recommendations to guide program direction.
Effective project and people management skills: You are adept at managing complex, multi-workstream initiatives from design to completion with clarity and accountability. You can guide and develop junior team members, foster collaboration across a matrixed organization, and ensure high-quality outputs under tight deadlines.
Entrepreneurial mindset: You are resourceful, proactive, and driven to find solutions, with a strong bias for action and a track record of delivering results in fast-paced, ambiguous environments.
Excellent interpersonal and relationship management skills: You have strong written and oral communication skills and can work effectively with a wide array of internal and external partners. You can respectfully and effectively navigate varied and sensitive stakeholder environments, including in-country teams and senior leaders.
Fundraising and resource mobilization experience: You are comfortable contributing to proposals and concept notes, coordinating input across teams, and supporting efforts to mobilize resources for program expansion.
Results driven: You remain engaged and motivated until a task is successfully completed, and you hold yourself and others accountable for delivering high-quality work

Experience:

Master’s degree (for example, MBA, MPH, or a related discipline) with 7–8 years of progressively responsible experience in global health, management consulting, or a related field.
Demonstrated experience leading global or multi-country teams and managing complex, high-value grant portfolios.
Proven track record in country programs, product access, or health financing within LMIC contexts.
Recognized expertise in the program’s technical area.
Excellent relationship management skills, including experience navigating senior, political, and multilateral stakeholder relationships.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including experience with creating and delivering high-quality presentations/ decks, with the ability to represent CHAI at high levels externally.
Willingness to travel internationally, approximately 20% of the time.

Advantages:

Experience working remotely with a decentralized team
Experience working in and/or supporting low- and middle-income countries.
Professional fluency in additional languages.

Job Description

The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication, and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work: http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org

Program Overview
More than 300,000 women die of cervical cancer each year, despite the availability of proven prevention interventions that can dramatically reduce the burden of disease. Over 90% of these deaths occur among women in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where access to high-quality prevention services has historically been limited. In 2018, the WHO issued a Global Call to Action Towards Cervical Cancer Elimination, and in 2020, the Member States of the World Health Assembly adopted a Cervical Cancer Elimination Strategy, setting targets to reach 70% screening coverage and 90% treatment coverage of screen-positive women by 2030.
CHAI’s cervical cancer program works to reduce cervical cancer incidence in LMICs by expanding access to secondary prevention services, thereby preventing mortality and morbidity while lowering cancer treatment costs for health systems. Rwanda Contracts Coordinator at One Acre Fund: (Deadline 14-11-2026)
About One Acre Fund
Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.
Our Rwanda program, founded in 2007 is our largest and operates under the local brand Tubura. We have more than 3,000 staff across all four provinces of Rwanda, as well as in Kigali. Together, we served more than 2.8 million farmers in 2024. We work closely with the government to support national efforts to improve food security. Additionally, we help channel funding and resources to promising agri-SMEs, supporting farmers by providing a market for high-impact crops such as coffee, avocado, and chili.
About the Role
Seeking an exceptional procurement and contracts professional with 2+ years of experience to increase our impact on farmers by driving cost-saving and coordinating contracting activities for the procurement department.
Responsibilities
Tender Management

Lead end-to-end tendering and contract execution for high-value goods and services by collaborating on departmental procurement plans, establishing 0–6 month strategic targets, setting price baselines to negotiate maximum cost savings, and continually optimizing sourcing processes for higher efficiency.

Contract Planning

Analyze annual spend across key categories to establish a quarterly-reviewed tender calendar while conducting market research to boost competition and contract effectiveness.

Contract Management

Oversee full contract lifecycles and LTAs by tracking price tolerances, managing change control systems, analyzing market risks, and reporting cost savings.

Supplier Performance Management

Conduct bi-annual vendor evaluations and monthly meetings with top suppliers to create performance improvement plans and enforce contractual commitments.

Stakeholder management

Act as the key liaison between external suppliers and One Acre Fund while directly supporting internal team procurement needs.

Career Growth and Development
We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.
Qualifications
Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

Contract management & procurement sourcing experience 
Data analysis & cost optimization 
Stakeholder & vendor management 
Degree in Procurement/Supply Chain or Law

Preferred Start Date
As soon as possible
Job Location
Kigali, Rwanda
Benefits
Health insurance, paid time off 
Eligibility
This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Rwanda.
Application Deadline
14 November 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.
One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.
Diversity, Equity, Inclusion (DEI), and anti-racism are deeply connected to our organization’s mission and purpose. One Acre Fund aspires to build a culture where all staff feel consistently valued, represented, and connected – so that our team can thrive as professionals, and achieve exceptional impact for the farmers we serve.
We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender, gender identity or expression. We are proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

About the Role

We are seeking a National Performance Trial Specialist to lead National Performance Trials (NPTs), ensuring scientific integrity through robust trial design and statistical analysis while building capacity by teaching and mentoring STB trainees.

Responsibilities

Lead National Performance Trial Design & Execution

  • Design and implement high-quality National Performance Trials (NPTs), ensuring scientifically robust experimental designs and field protocols.
  • Oversee trial implementation from planting through harvest, working closely with field teams to ensure accurate data collection and adherence to research standards.
  • Maintain compliance with Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), institutional guidelines, and international research best practices.

Deliver Advanced Data Analysis & Research Insights

  • Develop standardized data collection tools and quality assurance protocols for research teams.
  • Analyze complex trial data using statistical software to generate reliable insights and recommendations.
  • Create clear data visualizations, dashboards, and technical outputs that support evidence-based decision-making.

Build Research Capacity & Technical Expertise

  • Deliver training on experimental design, data management, and statistical analysis within the Seed Technology & Business (STB) Program.
  • Mentor trainees and provide technical guidance on research proposals, trial design, and data interpretation.
  • Promote best practices in agricultural research and strengthen the technical capacity of field and research teams.

Communicate Research Findings & Support Innovation

  • Prepare high-quality technical reports, presentations, and research briefs for internal and external stakeholders.
  • Translate scientific findings into practical recommendations for seed production, variety evaluation, and industry partners.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to improve research tools, data systems, and operational processes.

Drive Continuous Improvement in Research Quality

  • Identify opportunities to strengthen trial methodologies, data quality, and analytical approaches.
  • Support the adoption of digital tools and innovative solutions that improve research efficiency and decision-making.

  • Experience with agricultural research reporting and data analysis is a strong advantage.
  • Advanced analytical skills with experience using statistical software such as R, Genstat, SAS, STATA, or similar.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple research activities simultaneously.
  • Strong understanding of experimental design, quantitative and qualitative research methods, and data quality assurance.
